questions.answer: The investigation established that the diverted amount was $464,164.87.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2401
Date opened: November 15, 2024
Subject: Rudolpho Castellanos (individual), account 41-62701-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: closed_no_action

## Case Summary

On September 23, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit of Cortex Bank and Trust opened an investigation following an urgent escalation from the commercial banking division. The escalation concerned a single outbound domestic wire transfer of $464,164.87, originating from business operating account 41-62701-1 held by Rudolpho Castellanos. The transfer was executed on September 19, 2024. The relationship manager reported that Rudolpho Castellanos contacted the bank on the morning of September 23, 2024, stating that the funds were intended for a known supplier but had not been received by that supplier. The primary objective of the investigation was to determine if the transfer of $464,164.87 was the result of a business email compromise or other deceptive practice resulting in wire fraud, and to evaluate the circumstances surrounding the initiation and execution of the transfer.

The investigation focused on the communication and authorization events leading up to the September 19, 2024 wire transfer. The relationship manager indicated that Rudolpho Castellanos authorized the transfer based on payment instructions received via email, which he believed originated from a long-standing vendor. The investigation sought to reconstruct the sequence of events to assess the legitimacy of those instructions. Initial review of the account activity did not reveal any unauthorized access to the online banking platform by external actors; the transfer was initiated using the established credentials associated with the account. The inquiry centered on the origin and authenticity of the payment instructions that prompted the customer to initiate the transfer.

The escalation noted that the beneficiary of the wire transfer was listed as Aperture Freight Holdings Ltd. The customer asserted that the payment was intended for a different entity, Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC, a vendor with whom he had a prior business relationship. The investigation was tasked with establishing the connection, if any, between Aperture Freight Holdings Ltd. and Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC, or determining if the beneficiary information was fraudulently introduced. The customer provided copies of the email correspondence that contained the payment instructions to the relationship manager, which were subsequently forwarded to the Financial Intelligence Unit for analysis.

A critical component of the investigation was the examination of the email correspondence provided by the customer. The objective was to identify any indicators of compromise or manipulation within the communication chain. The investigation evaluated the sender's email address, the tone and content of the messages, and the specific payment details provided. The goal was to determine if the customer was induced to send funds to an unintended recipient through deceptive means. The investigation also reviewed the timing of the transfer request and the authorization process to identify any anomalies or deviations from standard procedures.

Following the customer's notification on September 23, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated standard recall procedures for the wire transfer of $464,164.87. The investigation tracked the status of the recall request and the response from the receiving institution. The primary question remained whether the customer was the victim of a targeted fraud scheme that successfully diverted the funds to an account controlled by a malicious actor, rather than the intended vendor. The investigation was designed to compile the necessary facts to determine the nature of the transaction and to support any subsequent reporting or recovery efforts. The scope of the review was limited to the circumstances directly related to the September 19, 2024 transfer and the associated communications.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On September 19, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received a customer complaint from Rudolpho Castellanos. Mr. Castellanos alleged that a wire transfer initiated from his account, 41-62701-1, was fraudulently induced. The customer asserted that he was deceived into wiring $464,164.87 to an unintended beneficiary. Mr. Castellanos stated that the funds were intended for a known vendor, but the payment instructions were altered prior to execution. The customer maintained that the alteration occurred without his knowledge or authorization. The customer contacted Cortex Bank and Trust after the intended vendor reported non-receipt of the payment. The customer provided a copy of the invoice, which he stated was received via email.

Mr. Castellanos indicated that he received the invoice from what he believed to be the vendor's standard email address. He further stated that the email contained a communication thread discussing an outstanding balance. The customer asserted that he reviewed the invoice and, believing it to be legitimate, initiated the wire transfer. The customer reported that the transfer was requested on August 22, 2024. He noted that the transfer was submitted near the end of the business day. The customer stated that he received no immediate notification of any discrepancy regarding the beneficiary information.

According to Mr. Castellanos, the intended vendor contacted him on September 23, 2024, inquiring about the status of the payment. Upon reviewing the transaction records, the customer realized the funds were sent to a beneficiary named Obsidian Holdings Trading Co., rather than the intended vendor. The customer stated that he had no prior business relationship with Obsidian Holdings Trading Co. He further asserted that he did not authorize a payment to this entity. The customer requested that Cortex Bank and Trust attempt to recall the wire transfer.

Following the customer's complaint, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the wire transfer. The investigation confirmed that a wire transfer in the amount of $464,164.87 was executed from account 41-62701-1 on August 22, 2024. The beneficiary of the transfer was identified as Obsidian Holdings Trading Co. The transfer was processed shortly before the daily wire cutoff time. The investigation sought to verify the customer's claim that the payment instructions were altered.

Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution to request a recall of the funds. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the wire transfer but indicated that the funds had been partially disbursed. The receiving institution placed a hold on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $51,058.14. The receiving institution requested a formal indemnification agreement before attempting to return the frozen funds. Cortex Bank and Trust provided the requested documentation.

The customer was informed of the partial freeze. Mr. Castellanos was advised that the recovery of the remaining funds was uncertain. The customer reiterated his assertion that the transfer was the result of a fraudulent scheme. The investigation noted that the customer's account activity prior to August 22, 2024, did not show any transfers to Obsidian Holdings Trading Co. The customer provided correspondence related to the transaction. The correspondence included an email that appeared to originate from the intended vendor. The email contained instructions to remit payment to a new account, citing a change in banking relationships. The email urged expedited processing of the payment. The customer stated that he relied on these instructions when initiating the wire transfer. The referral indicated a potential business email compromise scenario resulting in the diversion of funds. The investigation proceeded to analyze the transaction details and the provided correspondence to assess the validity of the customer's allegations.

## Timeline of Events

On July 24, 2024, the subject, Rudolpho Castellanos, initiated an email exchange with a known vendor contact. The vendor contact’s email address was subsequently identified as having been compromised or spoofed. The initial email from Castellanos inquired about a pending invoice for services rendered. The response received on July 26, 2024, purported to be from the vendor contact, but directed Castellanos to a new, lookalike sender domain that differed from the legitimate vendor domain by one character. This email instructed Castellanos to remit payment for the invoice to a new beneficiary, Obsidian Holdings Trading Co., rather than the customary vendor entity.

A subsequent email, received on July 30, 2024, from the lookalike domain, contained urgency language, insisting that the payment must be processed immediately to avoid disruption of services. This email overrode the established dual-approval control typically required for changes to vendor payment instructions. The email correspondence did not include any revised invoice or supporting documentation to substantiate the change in beneficiary or payment routing instructions.

## Funds Tracing

On September 19, 2024, at 4:51 PM, an authorized representative of Rudolpho Castellanos initiated an outbound domestic wire transfer from Cortex Bank and Trust account 41-62701-1. The transfer instruction, executed minutes before the 5:00 PM wire cutoff time, directed $464,164.87 to an account held at a domestic financial institution. The beneficiary named in the transfer instruction was Aperture Freight Holdings Ltd. The payment reference information included the phrase "urgent shipment invoice." The initiating party later stated this urgency language was a direct result of email communications received from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the known vendor, Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC. The communication requested immediate payment to avoid shipping delays and instructed the customer to bypass their internal dual-approval control for wire transfers. The beneficiary name, Aperture Freight Holdings Ltd., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC, nor did it match the name of the entity previously used for similar payments, Obsidian Holdings Trading Co.

The $464,164.87 transfer was processed and settled by Cortex Bank and Trust on September 19, 2024. The funds were credited to the receiving institution. Cortex Bank and Trust subsequently initiated a recall request for the full amount of the transfer, citing suspected fraud. Communication with the receiving institution confirmed receipt of the recall request. The receiving institution indicated that they were able to place a hold on a portion of the funds. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $51,058.14. This amount represents the only portion of the original transfer that has been successfully secured. The receiving institution has not provided a timeline for the potential return of these frozen funds to Cortex Bank and Trust.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

Investigation established that the funds diverted from Rudolpho Castellanos were credited to an account held in the name of Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC at an unaffiliated depository institution. Research indicated that this receiving entity was registered as a domestic limited liability company in the same state where the depository institution is headquartered. Registration documents filed with the state authority were examined. The formation date recorded for Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC was July 24, 2024. This date preceded the fraudulent outbound wire by several weeks, suggesting the entity was established in relatively close proximity to the suspected fraudulent activity. The registered agent address provided on the formation documents was a commercial mail receiving agency rather than a physical commercial premises. No website, online presence, or public advertising for Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC was identified during open-source research. The stated business purpose on the formation documents was generic, listing general merchandise trading, which provided little insight into the actual operations of the entity.

Information obtained through information-sharing protocols with the receiving institution provided details regarding the activity within the Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC account. The account was opened on July 26, 2024, two days after the entity's registration. Initial funding was a nominal cash deposit. Prior to the receipt of the $464,164.87 transfer from Rudolpho Castellanos, the account exhibited minimal activity, characterized by low-value debit card transactions consistent with minor administrative expenses. The receipt of the diverted funds represented a significant deviation from this established, albeit brief, historical pattern. The magnitude of the transfer was inconsistent with the prior activity and the generic stated business purpose of the entity.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The investigation obtained and reviewed documentary evidence, including email communications, wire transfer requests, invoices, and system logs, to evaluate the circumstances of the wire transfer. A telephonic interview was also conducted with the subject, Rudolpho Castellanos, by the relationship manager on September 19, 2024. The reviewing analyst subsequently reviewed the recorded call and the relationship manager's written notes.

During the September 19, 2024 interview, Castellanos stated that the wire transfer in question, totaling $464,164.87, was intended to settle a final invoice with a supplier, Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC, for a large shipment of raw materials. Castellanos indicated that he had a long-standing business relationship with this supplier and had previously remitted payments to them, typically via domestic ACH. He reported that on July 24, 2024, he received an email, ostensibly from his primary contact at Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC, containing an invoice and new wire instructions for payment. Castellanos stated that the email stressed the need for immediate payment to secure the release of the shipment, which was purportedly delayed at port. He acknowledged that he initiated the wire transfer on July 26, 2024, believing he was paying the legitimate vendor.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

On September 19, 2024, the reviewing analyst submitted a formal request for indemnification to the receiving institution, seeking the return of the $464,164.87 transferred from the account of Rudolpho Castellanos. The request cited suspected wire fraud, detailing that the customer had been induced by deception to remit funds to a beneficiary not intended to receive payment. The indemnification request included a hold harmless agreement executed by Cortex Bank and Trust, assuming liability for the return of funds should a legitimate claim arise. A parallel SWIFT recall message was transmitted on the same date, reiterating the fraudulent nature of the transaction and requesting an immediate freeze on the receiving account.

The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the indemnification request and SWIFT recall on September 23, 2024. In their response, the receiving institution indicated that they had placed an administrative hold on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account. The communication specified that $51,058.14 had been successfully frozen at the receiving institution. The receiving institution further stated that the remainder of the transferred funds had already been disbursed or withdrawn prior to the receipt of the recall notice, and were therefore no longer available for recovery.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that on August 22, 2024, the subject Rudolpho Castellanos initiated an outbound wire transfer of $464,164.87 from Cortex Bank and Trust account 41-62701-1. The beneficiary of this transfer was identified as Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC. Review of the transfer request documentation, including email correspondence provided by the subject, indicated the payment was intended for a long-standing vendor, Obsidian Holdings Trading Co., to settle an outstanding invoice for materials. The email instructing the payment was received from a sender domain differing from the vendor's known domain by a single character. The instruction contained language emphasizing urgency, which circumvented the subject's established dual-approval control for large outgoing transfers, and the transfer was initiated shortly before the daily wire cutoff time. The beneficiary name, Quarrystone Exports Enterprises LLC, did not match the invoicing vendor. The subject subsequently confirmed to the relationship manager that Obsidian Holdings Trading Co. had not requested the payment or changed its remittance instructions. The investigation determined the instruction was fraudulent and the funds had been diverted by deception. The receiving institution was contacted, and a portion of the funds was frozen; however, the subject incurred a residual loss of $413,106.73. Based on the determination that the subject was the victim of wire fraud and not the perpetrator of suspicious activity, the investigation fixed November 11, 2024 as the date of determination, and the alert was closed_no_action.

questions.answer: The amount of the outbound wire transfer was $1,590,970.21.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2402
Date opened: December 6, 2024
Subject: Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. (business), account 52-52289-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: referred_to_fincen

## Case Summary

On November 12, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit opened case FIU-WIRE-2402 upon receipt of an escalation from the commercial banking relationship manager for Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. The escalation detailed a wire transfer dispute raised by the customer concerning a $1,590,970.21 outbound funds transfer originating from Cortex Bank and Trust account 52-52289-1. The customer reported to the relationship manager that this payment, initiated on November 7, 2024, was intended to settle an invoice with an established supplier, Obsidian Metals Partners LP. The escalation noted that Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. was subsequently contacted by Obsidian Metals Partners LP regarding a past due balance, leading the customer to review the transaction details and discover that the funds had not been directed to the intended vendor.

The reviewing analyst assessed the referral to determine whether the circumstances of the November 7, 2024 transfer were consistent with wire fraud, specifically an instance where a customer was induced by deception to authorize a payment to an unintended beneficiary. Initial review of the wire instructions submitted through the commercial online banking portal confirmed that the beneficiary name entered was not Obsidian Metals Partners LP. The $1,590,970.21 wire transfer was instead directed to Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC. The customer asserted to the relationship manager that they had no business relationship with Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC and had not intended to remit funds to that entity. The customer further stated that the payment instructions were updated based on electronic correspondence they believed originated from their established contact at Obsidian Metals Partners LP.

The investigation focused on validating the customer's claim of deception and reconstructing the events leading to the authorization of the $1,590,970.21 transfer. The reviewing analyst sought to determine the mechanism by which the altered payment instructions were communicated to Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. and whether the customer's internal controls were circumvented. The escalation indicated that the customer was pursuing recovery efforts through the relationship manager, but the immediate objective of the Financial Intelligence Unit was to assess the activity for suspicious characteristics warranting regulatory reporting. The review period for this assessment was established as August 12, 2024 through December 9, 2024, to encompass the transaction date and allow for examination of historical account activity for context.

The case required an evaluation of the communications the customer relied upon when changing the beneficiary details. The analyst needed to establish whether the activity exhibited known typologies of business email compromise, where threat actors intercept vendor communications and substitute fraudulent payment instructions. The investigation also aimed to determine the final disposition of the funds to the extent possible, given that the transfer had cleared the Cortex Bank and Trust environment. The relationship manager reported that a request for the return of funds had been transmitted to the receiving institution, but the outcome of that request was pending at the time the escalation was filed. The reviewing analyst was tasked with documenting the sequence of events, evaluating the red flags present in the transaction flow, and concluding whether the activity met the threshold for filing a Suspicious Activity Report based on the suspected diversion of $1,590,970.21 from Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. through deceptive practices.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On December 6, 2024, a relationship manager supporting commercial banking customers submitted an internal referral regarding Fairmount Logistics Trading Co., a business customer maintaining a commercial checking account with Cortex Bank and Trust. The referral indicated that Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. had reported a suspected wire fraud event involving a significant diversion of corporate funds. The customer alleged that a wire transfer initiated on November 12, 2024, was fraudulently induced through deception, resulting in funds being directed to a beneficiary that the customer did not intend to pay.

According to the referral, Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. was in the process of finalizing a substantial equipment purchase and lease agreement with an established vendor, Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC. The customer stated that negotiations and preliminary invoicing had been ongoing for several weeks prior to the incident. On November 12, 2024, the customer’s accounts payable department received an email containing updated payment instructions for a previously agreed-upon invoice. The email, which appeared to originate from a known contact at Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC, directed payment to a new beneficiary account and emphasized that the transaction needed to be completed immediately to secure the equipment inventory.

The relationship manager noted that the customer described the email as highly convincing, utilizing the vendor's standard invoicing format and referencing specific details of the pending transaction. The communication contained urgency language that the customer later identified as a tactic to bypass internal controls. Specifically, the email insisted that failure to remit payment before the close of business would result in the cancellation of the order and the forfeiture of a previously paid deposit. This urgency, the customer reported, led the accounts payable staff to expedite the payment process, overriding their standard dual-approval control for large outgoing wire transfers.

The internal referral detailed that the customer initiated an outgoing wire transfer in the amount of $1,590,970.21 on November 12, 2024. The transfer was authorized and transmitted by Cortex Bank and Trust shortly before the daily wire cutoff time. The customer indicated that the payment was intended to settle the outstanding invoice with Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC. However, the updated payment instructions provided in the deceptive email directed the funds to an account held by a different entity, Obsidian Metals Partners LP.

The customer became aware of the suspected fraud several days later when Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC inquired about the status of the overdue payment. Upon reviewing the email correspondence, the customer's IT security team identified that the message containing the new payment instructions had originated from a lookalike sender domain. The domain closely resembled the legitimate vendor's domain but differed by one character, a discrepancy that went unnoticed by the accounts payable staff during the initial processing of the invoice.

Following the discovery of the discrepancy, Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. immediately contacted their relationship manager at Cortex Bank and Trust to report the incident and request a recall of the funds. The customer asserted that they had no prior business relationship with Obsidian Metals Partners LP and that the funds transfer to this entity was entirely unauthorized. The customer further alleged that the beneficiary name on the fraudulent payment instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, a detail that was also overlooked during the expedited payment process. The relationship manager escalated the customer's report to the Financial Intelligence Unit for further review and investigation of the suspected wire fraud event. The referral prompted an immediate review of the transaction and the initiation of efforts to trace and potentially recover the diverted funds.

## Timeline of Events

The investigation established that the sequence of events leading to the unauthorized transfer began on October 2, 2024. On that date, an email was received by the controller at Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. The message purported to be from a known vendor contact at Obsidian Metals Partners LP. The email provided new wire instructions for all future invoice settlements, directing payments to an account held in the name of Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC. The communication bypassed established vendor validation protocols at Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. Review of the email headers later revealed that the sender address originated from a lookalike domain differing by a single character from the legitimate domain used by Obsidian Metals Partners LP. The deception was not identified by the customer at the time of receipt.

Subsequent communications from the fraudulent sender domain occurred between October 2, 2024, and November 7, 2024. These messages urged expedited payment of an outstanding invoice, citing alleged supply chain disruptions and threatening to withhold a pending shipment. The language employed was characterized by a high degree of urgency, a tactic frequently observed in business email compromise schemes. The communications culminated on November 7, 2024, when the sender insisted that funds must be received before the close of business to ensure the release of materials essential for a contract with Cedarline Exports Holdings Ltd., a significant client of Fairmount Logistics Trading Co.

In response to the escalating demands, the controller at Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. initiated an outbound wire transfer on November 7, 2024. The transfer was entered into the Cortex Bank and Trust online banking portal shortly before the established wire cutoff time. The urgency conveyed by the fraudulent emails caused the controller to override internal dual-approval controls, authorizing the payment without secondary review. The wire, in the amount of $1,590,970.21, was transmitted to the account held by Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC. The beneficiary name on the wire instructions did not correspond to the invoicing vendor, Obsidian Metals Partners LP. The discrepancy was not noted prior to the execution of the transfer.

The fraud was discovered on November 12, 2024. A representative of the legitimate Obsidian Metals Partners LP contacted Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. to inquire about the overdue invoice. During this conversation, the controller realized that the payment of $1,590,970.21 had been diverted to an unauthorized beneficiary. The customer immediately notified their relationship manager at Cortex Bank and Trust. The bank’s fraud operations unit initiated a recall request through the wire transfer system on the same day.

The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request on November 12, 2024. Subsequent communication from the receiving bank confirmed that the majority of the funds had already been dispersed from the beneficiary account. A hold was placed on the remaining balance. On December 6, 2024, the receiving institution informed Cortex Bank and Trust that $461,381.36 had been successfully frozen and would be returned to Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. The residual loss sustained by the customer as a result of the unauthorized transfer was calculated at $1,129,588.85. The investigation confirmed that the entirety of the $1,590,970.21 wire transfer was induced by deception and represented diverted funds. The timeline of events, from the initial lookalike email to the realization of the loss, is consistent with established typologies for business email compromise and wire fraud.

## Funds Tracing

The investigation reviewed Cortex Bank and Trust account 52-52289-1, held by Fairmount Logistics Trading Co., for the period August 12, 2024 through December 9, 2024. The tracing of funds commenced with the originating debit on the subject account. On November 7, 2024, a single outbound wire transfer was initiated by an authorized signer for Fairmount Logistics Trading Co., debiting account 52-52289-1 in the amount of $1,590,970.21. The payment instructions cited a beneficiary name of Obsidian Metals Partners LP. The debit occurred late in the business day, shortly before the cutoff time for processing outgoing wire transfers, a timing often observed when actors attempt to limit a sending institution's opportunity to recall a payment before settlement.

The wire transfer of $1,590,970.21 was routed through the domestic clearing system to a receiving depository financial institution located in a mid-Atlantic state. The beneficiary account at the receiving institution was held in the name of Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC, not Obsidian Metals Partners LP as stated on the transfer instructions. The discrepancy between the named beneficiary and the actual account holder was not detected during the initial processing of the payment. The receiving institution confirmed that the funds credited the Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC account on the morning of November 8, 2024.

Following the credit to the Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC account, the receiving institution documented immediate onward movement of a significant portion of the funds. The reviewing analyst obtained records from the receiving institution detailing this subsequent activity. On November 8, 2024, three outbound domestic wire transfers were initiated from the Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC account, totaling a mid-six-figure sum. These transfers were directed to accounts at three separate domestic financial institutions. The beneficiaries of these three transfers were not identified in the records provided by the initial receiving institution.

On November 12, 2024, an additional outbound transfer was initiated from the Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC account. This transfer, in a low-six-figure amount, was an international wire directed to a financial institution in a western European jurisdiction. The beneficiary named on this international transfer was Cedarline Exports Holdings Ltd. The receiving institution reported that this transfer was processed and settled before Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary of the fraudulent outbound wire was identified as Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC. Cortex Bank and Trust does not hold an account for this entity. Information regarding the receiving account and the beneficiary was obtained through collaboration with the receiving institution and through public record research. The receiving institution provided information indicating the account for Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC was established on August 12, 2024. The stated business purpose at the time of account opening was the procurement and leasing of specialized construction machinery.

Public record research conducted on Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC yielded limited results. The entity was registered in a jurisdiction known for corporate secrecy, and the registration occurred on August 12, 2024, the same date the account was established at the receiving institution. No physical business address or website could be located for Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC. The lack of an established operational history and the absence of a discernible digital footprint are inconsistent with the profile of a legitimate equipment leasing enterprise.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

A review of documentary evidence was conducted to determine the circumstances surrounding the initiation and authorization of the $1,590,970.21 outbound wire. Email correspondence provided by the authorized signer for Fairmount Logistics Trading Co. was analyzed. The initial email thread, originating on September 25, 2024, appeared to be a routine communication from the customer's established vendor regarding an upcoming invoice. However, a subsequent email received on October 2, 2024, directing payment to a new beneficiary, was identified as originating from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the vendor's actual domain. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer did not identify this discrepancy prior to initiating the transfer.

The invoice attached to the October 2, 2024 email was reviewed. The document was formatted similarly to previous invoices received from the vendor, detailing expected shipments. However, the payment instructions on the invoice directed funds to an account held in the name of Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC, a beneficiary name that did not match the invoicing vendor. The customer's authorized signer indicated during an interview that they did not question the discrepancy in the beneficiary name, assuming the vendor was utilizing a subsidiary or a third-party processor for the transaction.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Upon receiving notification of the suspected wire fraud on November 12, 2024, the investigating analyst initiated immediate recovery protocols. A SWIFT MT192 request for cancellation was transmitted to the receiving institution, accompanied by an electronic communication via the secure interbank messaging channel detailing the suspected fraudulent nature of the $1,590,970.21 outbound wire transfer. The communication specified that the transfer, initiated from the account of Fairmount Logistics Trading Co., was induced by a compromised business email, evidenced by the use of a lookalike sender domain and urgency language intended to bypass established dual-approval controls.

The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request on the same business day and confirmed that a hold had been placed on the beneficiary account held in the name of Falcon Crest Equipment Enterprises LLC. Subsequent communication from the receiving institution's fraud department indicated that a portion of the funds had already been disbursed or transferred prior to the receipt of the cancellation request. The receiving institution confirmed that $461,381.36 remained in the account and was successfully frozen pursuant to the recall request.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that on November 26, 2024, an unauthorized actor successfully induced the customer to originate an outbound wire transfer of $1,590,970.21. The instruction appeared to originate from a known vendor's email address but utilized a lookalike sender domain differing by a single character. The beneficiary name on the wire instruction, Obsidian Metals Partners LP, did not match the vendor named on the supporting invoice provided by the customer. The instruction contained urgency language that successfully overrode the customer's internal dual-approval control, and the transfer was initiated minutes before the Cortex Bank and Trust wire cutoff time. The activity is consistent with a business email compromise resulting in wire fraud. The customer was unable to recall the transfer before execution. The reviewing analyst determined that the activity meets the threshold for suspicious activity reporting. The matter is referred_to_fincen.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit

Date opened: August 21, 2024
Subject: Fieldstone Exports Group LLC (business), account 49-18811-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: criminal_referral

## Case Summary

On May 16, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit initiated an investigation into an outbound funds transfer from an account held by Fieldstone Exports Group LLC. The investigation was triggered by a fraud claim filed by the customer on the same date, asserting that a wire transfer executed on May 14, 2024, was induced by a compromised business communication. The account involved is Cortex Bank and Trust account 49-18811-1. The subject transfer was an outbound domestic wire. The amount of the disputed transfer was $1,184,300.40. The investigation was opened to determine the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the transfer and to evaluate whether the customer’s claim of business email compromise was supported by the transactional evidence and the communication records provided by the customer.

The primary focus of the initial review was to trace the origin of the payment instructions and to verify the authenticity of the authorization. The customer, Fieldstone Exports Group LLC, reported that the transfer was intended to settle an invoice for a regular vendor. However, the customer subsequently discovered that the payment instructions had been altered. The investigation was required to analyze the communication channels through which the payment instructions were received and processed. The objective was to ascertain whether the instructions originated from the legitimate vendor or a malicious actor who had intercepted or spoofed the communication. The review period for the investigation was defined as May 2, 2024, through August 27, 2024, to encompass the period leading up to the transaction, the transaction date, and the subsequent recovery efforts.

The investigation required a detailed examination of the authentication protocols employed by the customer when initiating the transfer. The reviewing analyst was tasked with determining whether the customer adhered to established internal controls, such as dual approval, or whether these controls were bypassed or overridden. The review also sought to identify any anomalies in the payment instructions, such as discrepancies in the beneficiary name or account details compared to historical payment records for the intended vendor. The investigation aimed to establish a timeline of events, beginning with the receipt of the invoice and concluding with the execution of the wire transfer. This timeline was critical for understanding the sequence of actions that led to the disbursement of funds.

Furthermore, the investigation was responsible for evaluating the feasibility of recovering the funds. Upon receipt of the fraud claim, the Financial Intelligence Unit immediately initiated a recall request to the receiving institution. The investigation tracked the progress of this recovery effort to determine the final loss amount. The review of the recovery process involved analyzing the responses from the receiving institution and assessing the status of the funds within the beneficiary account. The investigation aimed to provide a comprehensive account of the transaction, the deceptive methods employed, the vulnerabilities exploited, and the financial impact on the customer, culminating in a determination of the appropriate regulatory reporting and external referral actions. The initial findings indicated a significant discrepancy between the intended recipient and the actual beneficiary of the funds transfer. The investigation proceeded to analyze the specific details of the communication that induced the payment and the characteristics of the transfer itself.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The investigation originated on July 3, 2024, when the principal of Fieldstone Exports Group LLC contacted a relationship manager at Cortex Bank and Trust to dispute a funds transfer debited from the customer's commercial checking account. The customer alleged that a wire transfer initiated on May 20, 2024, in the amount of $1,184,300.40, was directed to a beneficiary account that Fieldstone Exports Group LLC did not intend to pay. According to the customer's initial statement, the payment was intended to settle an outstanding invoice for industrial equipment purchased from an established vendor, Highfield Industrial Supply LLC. The customer asserted that the funds were instead diverted to a different entity and that Highfield Industrial Supply LLC had subsequently contacted them regarding the unpaid invoice, prompting the inquiry.

The relationship manager documented the customer's claim that the payment instructions were received via email from a contact they believed to be a representative of Highfield Industrial Supply LLC. The customer reported that the email included revised payment instructions, directing the funds to a new beneficiary account. The customer stated that they complied with these revised instructions, initiating the wire transfer of $1,184,300.40 from their account at Cortex Bank and Trust. The customer further alleged that they only became aware of the discrepancy when the legitimate vendor, Highfield Industrial Supply LLC, followed up on the overdue payment in early July.

Following the customer's report, the relationship manager immediately escalated the matter to the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit for review. The reviewing analyst initiated an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the May 20, 2024, wire transfer. Initial review of the customer's account activity confirmed the debit of $1,184,300.40 on the date in question. The transaction details indicated that the funds were wired to an account held at another domestic financial institution. The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary name on the wire transfer instructions did not match Highfield Industrial Supply LLC, the vendor the customer intended to pay.

The reviewing analyst contacted the receiving financial institution on July 3, 2024, to request a hold on the funds and to initiate a wire recall. The receiving institution acknowledged the request and subsequently confirmed that a portion of the funds, amounting to $236,860.08, remained in the beneficiary account and had been frozen pending further investigation. The receiving institution also provided the name of the beneficiary account holder, which was identified as Emberline Commodities Group LLC. The reviewing analyst noted that this entity name did not align with the vendor Highfield Industrial Supply LLC, nor did it correspond to Harborview Textiles LLC, another known counterparty previously associated with Fieldstone Exports Group LLC's account activity.

The customer provided the relationship manager with copies of the email correspondence that contained the revised payment instructions. The reviewing analyst examined these emails and observed that the sender's email address closely resembled the legitimate domain of Highfield Industrial Supply LLC but differed by a single character. The analyst also noted that the email correspondence included language emphasizing the urgency of the payment, which appeared to have influenced the customer to expedite the transfer, potentially bypassing their internal dual-approval controls. The reviewing analyst further observed that the wire transfer was initiated by the customer just minutes before the daily wire cutoff time on May 20, 2024.

Based on the customer's allegation of diverted funds and the initial findings regarding the mismatched beneficiary name, the lookalike sender domain, and the urgency language in the email correspondence, the reviewing analyst determined that the activity was consistent with a business email compromise scheme resulting in wire fraud. The investigation proceeded to analyze the full scope of the customer's account activity during the review period and to document the details of the suspected fraud for potential reporting.

## Timeline of Events

On May 2, 2024, the relationship manager received a phone call from an individual identifying themselves as a representative of Highfield Industrial Supply LLC. The caller inquired about the process for updating vendor payment instructions for Fieldstone Exports Group LLC, stating that Highfield Industrial Supply LLC was currently undergoing an internal systems migration and required all future payments to be directed to a new account. The relationship manager advised the caller that such requests must be submitted in writing by an authorized signer on the account, accompanied by supporting documentation on company letterhead.

On May 3, 2024, the relationship manager received an email purportedly from the authorized signer for Fieldstone Exports Group LLC. The email address, while appearing legitimate at first glance, was later determined to originate from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the customer’s established contact information. The email contained an attached letter, bearing the logo of Highfield Industrial Supply LLC, directing that a pending invoice payment be remitted to a new beneficiary account at another domestic financial institution. The letter cited an urgent need to expedite the payment to avoid supply chain disruptions.

The relationship manager, relying on the emailed instructions and the attached letter, initiated the wire transfer on May 8, 2024. The transfer, in the amount of $1,184,300.40, was processed and sent to the requested beneficiary account. However, subsequent review of the wire details revealed that the beneficiary name on the transfer instructions, Emberline Commodities Group LLC, did not align with the invoicing vendor, Highfield Industrial Supply LLC. Furthermore, the transfer was initiated minutes before the daily wire cutoff, a timing often associated with attempts to bypass internal review processes.

On May 14, 2024, the authorized signer for Fieldstone Exports Group LLC contacted the relationship manager to inquire about the status of the expected payment to Highfield Industrial Supply LLC, as the vendor had reported non-receipt. This contact prompted an immediate review of the transaction. The reviewing analyst confirmed the discrepancies in the email domain and the beneficiary name. The relationship manager subsequently contacted the authorized signer, who confirmed that no such payment instructions had been issued and that the email address used to initiate the transfer was fraudulent.

On May 16, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request for the wire transfer with the receiving institution. The receiving institution acknowledged the request and placed a hold on the remaining funds in the beneficiary account. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $236,860.08.

On May 20, 2024, the reviewing analyst formally escalated the matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit for further investigation. The investigation confirmed that the initial contact on May 2, 2024, and the subsequent email on May 3, 2024, were part of a coordinated effort to induce the transfer of funds by deception. The investigation established that the total sum diverted through this scheme was $1,184,300.40.

On May 30, 2024, the receiving institution informed Cortex Bank and Trust that the remaining funds in the beneficiary account had been depleted prior to the hold being placed. The residual loss to the customer was determined to be $947,440.32. The investigation noted that the urgency language used in the fraudulent email, combined with the timing of the transfer request, appeared designed to circumvent the customer's established dual-approval control for large outgoing wires. The investigation also identified a third entity, Harborview Textiles LLC, linked to the fraudulent email domain, although its specific role in the scheme remains unclear.

## Funds Tracing

The funds tracing for the incident at Cortex Bank and Trust originated with the debit to the operating account of Fieldstone Exports Group LLC. The transaction was a single outbound domestic wire transfer executed on May 16, 2024. The transfer amount was $1,184,300.40. The debit resulted in an immediate reduction of the available balance in the Fieldstone Exports Group LLC account. The beneficiary institution identified in the wire instructions was a domestic regional bank. The beneficiary name provided on the instructions was Emberline Commodities Group LLC.

The reviewing analyst noted that the wire instructions were processed shortly before the daily wire cutoff time on May 16, 2024. The urgency language used in the fraudulent instructions appeared designed to bypass normal verification procedures, specifically the dual-approval control normally required for transfers of this magnitude at Fieldstone Exports Group LLC. The beneficiary name, Emberline Commodities Group LLC, did not correspond to any known vendor or counterparty previously associated with the customer, nor did it match the invoicing vendor, Highfield Industrial Supply LLC.

Upon discovery of the suspected fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately contacted the beneficiary institution to request a hold on the funds. The beneficiary institution confirmed receipt of the $1,184,300.40 wire transfer. A subsequent hold was successfully placed on a portion of the funds remaining in the Emberline Commodities Group LLC account. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $236,860.08.

Information provided by the beneficiary institution indicated that the remaining balance of the initial transfer had already been disbursed prior to the hold request. The residual loss to the customer was determined to be $947,440.32. The beneficiary institution reported that these funds were transferred out of the Emberline Commodities Group LLC account through a series of rapid, successive transactions. The onward movement consisted primarily of domestic ACH transfers and smaller wire transfers to various secondary accounts held at different domestic financial institutions. The beneficiary institution was unable to provide a comprehensive breakdown of all secondary recipients due to the volume and speed of the subsequent transfers.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The receiving account was held at a domestic financial institution in the name of Emberline Commodities Group LLC. The investigation established that this entity was incorporated in a state known for its business-friendly registry requirements, with an incorporation date that preceded the fraudulent transfer by less than thirty days. Public records research identified no physical presence for this entity beyond a registered agent address, which was shared with numerous unaffiliated businesses. A review of commercial databases returned no trade credit history, no liens, and no established vendor relationships for Emberline Commodities Group LLC. The stated business purpose on the incorporation documents was broad, describing general commodities trading and export services, which provided no specific insight into the entity's actual operations.

A review of the account activity at the receiving institution, obtained through an information-sharing request, revealed a transactional pattern inconsistent with an established commodities trading firm. The account was opened shortly after the entity's incorporation. The initial funding of the account consisted of a nominal deposit, followed by a period of inactivity until the receipt of the $1,184,300.40 wire transfer from Fieldstone Exports Group LLC. The funds transfer from Cortex Bank and Trust represented the first significant credit to the Emberline Commodities Group LLC account.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The reviewing analyst conducted an interview with the principal of Fieldstone Exports Group LLC regarding the initiation of the outbound transfer. The principal stated that the payment instructions were received via email, purportedly from Highfield Industrial Supply LLC, a vendor with whom the customer has an established commercial relationship. The customer indicated that the email communication possessed the customary formatting and signatory details associated with previous correspondence from this vendor. The principal further related that the email contained language stressing the urgency of the payment to secure a pending shipment, which prompted the customer to expedite the transfer process.

Subsequent analysis of the email headers provided by the customer revealed a discrepancy in the sender's domain name. The domain utilized in the communication directing the payment differed by one character from the legitimate domain associated with Highfield Industrial Supply LLC. This lookalike domain is consistent with a business email compromise scheme designed to deceive the recipient. The customer acknowledged that the discrepancy was not identified prior to the execution of the transfer.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Upon identifying the fraudulent transfer on May 16, 2024, the reviewing analyst immediately initiated a wire recall through the Fedwire system. The recall request, transmitted to the receiving institution, cited suspected fraud as the basis for the reversal of the $1,184,300.40 outbound wire. The request explicitly noted that Fieldstone Exports Group LLC had been the victim of a business email compromise scheme and that the beneficiary, Highfield Industrial Supply LLC, was not the intended recipient of the funds. The recall message requested that the receiving institution place an immediate freeze on the beneficiary account and return the full amount to Cortex Bank and Trust. The investigation file indicates that the recall was transmitted prior to the close of the business day on May 16, 2024.

Simultaneous with the Fedwire recall, Cortex Bank and Trust's fraud recovery team contacted the receiving institution's fraud department by telephone to alert them to the urgent nature of the recall request. A letter of indemnity was subsequently drafted and transmitted to the receiving institution on May 20, 2024. The letter formally indemnified the receiving institution against any claims arising from the return of the funds and provided a detailed summary of the suspected fraudulent activity, including the use of a lookalike sender domain and the discrepancy between the beneficiary name and the invoicing vendor. The communication log indicates multiple follow-up inquiries were made by the fraud recovery team to the receiving institution regarding the status of the recall and the indemnity request.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Fieldstone Exports Group LLC was the victim of a business email compromise resulting in a fraudulent funds transfer. On May 14, 2024, the customer initiated a wire transfer of $1,184,300.40, believing they were settling an invoice with Emberline Commodities Group LLC. The investigation determined that the instruction was received from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the legitimate vendor's domain. The fraudulent email contained urgency language that circumvented the customer's internal dual-approval control. Furthermore, the beneficiary name on the transfer instruction did not match the invoicing vendor, directing the funds instead to Highfield Industrial Supply LLC. The transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time. While Cortex Bank and Trust was able to recover a portion of the funds frozen at the receiving institution, the customer sustained a substantial residual loss. The investigation concluded that the activity is consistent with wire fraud. A determination was made on August 14, 2024, that the incident warrants a criminal_referral.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2404
Date opened: October 2, 2024
Subject: Bluewater Equipment Inc. (business), account 14-16674-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: ongoing

## Case Summary

This matter was escalated to the Financial Intelligence Unit on July 11, 2024, following a customer dispute regarding an outgoing domestic wire transfer. The dispute originated with the commercial banking relationship manager for Bluewater Equipment Inc., who contacted the fraud operations group the previous day, July 10, 2024. The relationship manager reported that the customer had authorized a funds transfer on July 3, 2024, in the amount of $1,728,111.71, believing the payment was directed to an established vendor, Obsidian Marine Services LLC. The customer subsequently determined that the vendor had not received the funds and that the payment instructions utilized for the wire transfer were fraudulent. The Financial Intelligence Unit commenced an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire, the disposition of the funds, and whether the activity warranted the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report.

The subject of the investigation is Bluewater Equipment Inc., a commercial customer of Cortex Bank and Trust. The customer maintains a single demand deposit account with the institution, account number 14-16674-1. The account is utilized for general operating expenses and the receipt of revenue related to the sale and leasing of heavy machinery. The customer profile indicates a typical transaction volume consistent with a mid-sized commercial enterprise, with regular outgoing wire transfers to established domestic and international suppliers. The account history prior to the transaction in question did not exhibit activity indicative of financial crime or significant deviation from anticipated patterns.

The investigation focuses on a specific transaction initiated on July 3, 2024. On that date, a user with appropriate entitlements on the customer’s online banking profile initiated a domestic wire transfer of $1,728,111.71. The payment instructions directed the funds to an account held at another domestic financial institution. The beneficiary name provided on the wire instructions was Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC. The customer asserted to the relationship manager that this payment was intended to settle an outstanding invoice from Obsidian Marine Services LLC. The customer further stated that the payment instructions were received via email communication that they believed originated from a known contact at Obsidian Marine Services LLC.

The primary objective of the investigation was to ascertain the legitimacy of the July 3, 2024 wire transfer and to identify the mechanism by which the fraudulent payment instructions were introduced and executed. The reviewing analyst sought to determine if the customer’s internal controls were compromised or if the deception relied on external factors such as social engineering or business email compromise. Furthermore, the investigation aimed to establish the flow of funds following their departure from Cortex Bank and Trust, in order to assist in potential recovery efforts and to identify the ultimate recipient of the diverted funds.

The scope of the review encompassed the period from May 20, 2024, through September 23, 2024, to allow for the examination of account activity leading up to the fraudulent transfer and any subsequent related transactions. The analyst reviewed account statements, wire transfer logs, online banking access records, and customer communications provided by the relationship manager. The investigation also included a review of the beneficiary entity, Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC, and an assessment of its relationship, if any, to the customer or the intended vendor. The initial assessment categorized the risk tier associated with this matter as low, based on the isolated nature of the incident and the established relationship with the commercial customer. The investigation remained ongoing at the time of this report’s preparation.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On August 12, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust commercial banking operations unit received an urgent communication from the authorized signer for Bluewater Equipment Inc. The customer reported a suspected fraud involving a large wire transfer that had been initiated from their account, 14-16674-1, on the previous business day. According to the customer, the transfer was intended for a legitimate vendor but had been directed to an unknown third party.

The customer stated that the wire, in the amount of $1,728,111.71, was intended as payment for an outstanding invoice. However, upon reviewing their account activity, the customer noticed that the beneficiary name on the transfer did not match the vendor they had intended to pay. The customer immediately contacted the bank to report the discrepancy and request that the funds be recalled.

The commercial banking operations unit initiated a preliminary review of the transaction. The review identified several anomalies associated with the wire request. The request had been received via email from a sender whose domain name closely resembled, but was not identical to, the legitimate vendor's domain. The email address contained a single-character variation that was not immediately apparent. Furthermore, the email communication included urgent language, insisting that the payment was overdue and demanding immediate processing to avoid penalties. This urgency appeared to have bypassed the dual-approval control normally required for transfers of this magnitude.

The preliminary review also noted that the wire transfer was initiated late in the afternoon, just minutes before the bank's daily wire cutoff time. This timing is frequently observed in fraudulent schemes, as it minimizes the opportunity for immediate review and intervention by bank personnel. Based on these observations, the commercial banking operations unit escalated the matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit for a comprehensive investigation.

The Financial Intelligence Unit accepted the referral and commenced a review of the circumstances surrounding the $1,728,111.71 wire transfer. The investigation sought to confirm the customer's allegation that the funds had been induced out of their account by deception and moved to a beneficiary they never intended to pay. The initial focus of the investigation was to gather all relevant documentation, including the email correspondence, the wire transfer request form, and any associated invoices.

The bank immediately contacted the receiving institution to request a freeze on the funds and initiate a recall. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the recall request and subsequently reported that a portion of the funds had been secured. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $397,465.69. However, the receiving institution indicated that the remainder of the funds had already been disbursed or transferred to other accounts.

The Financial Intelligence Unit established a review period from May 20, 2024, through September 23, 2024, to encompass the events leading up to the fraudulent wire transfer and any subsequent activity related to the account. The investigation aimed to determine the extent of the fraud, identify the involved parties, and assess any potential vulnerabilities in the bank's controls or the customer's internal procedures. The initial assessment categorized the risk tier assigned to this case as low, pending further investigation into the specific mechanisms of the suspected fraud. The investigation remains ongoing as the Financial Intelligence Unit continues to analyze the gathered evidence and communicate with the receiving institution regarding the potential recovery of the remaining funds.

## Timeline of Events

On May 20, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust account held by Bluewater Equipment Inc. received an invoice, subsequently identified as fraudulent, for a large sum. The invoice, which was ostensibly from Obsidian Marine Services LLC, directed payment to Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC. A review of historical account activity indicated that Obsidian Marine Services LLC was an established vendor for Bluewater Equipment Inc. A review of the email transmitting the invoice revealed that the sender domain, which appeared at a glance to be that of Obsidian Marine Services LLC, was a lookalike differing by one character.

On May 30, 2024, an email was received by a Bluewater Equipment Inc. employee from the same lookalike domain, urging immediate payment of the invoice. The email contained urgency language intended to override the dual-approval control normally required for disbursements by Bluewater Equipment Inc. The email stated that failure to remit payment would result in an interruption of services provided by the purported vendor.

On June 13, 2024, a wire transfer in the amount of $1,728,111.71 was initiated from the Bluewater Equipment Inc. account at Cortex Bank and Trust. The transfer was directed to an account held by Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC at another financial institution. The wire transfer was initiated minutes before the daily wire cutoff time at Cortex Bank and Trust. The beneficiary name, Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC, did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Obsidian Marine Services LLC.

On July 3, 2024, Bluewater Equipment Inc. contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report the suspected fraud. The customer stated that they had been contacted by the legitimate Obsidian Marine Services LLC regarding an unpaid invoice and that a review of their records confirmed that the payment had been remitted to an incorrect beneficiary. Cortex Bank and Trust initiated an investigation and contacted the receiving institution to request the return of funds.

On July 10, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received notification from the receiving institution that a hold had been placed on the remaining funds in the beneficiary account. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $397,465.69.

On July 11, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust advised Bluewater Equipment Inc. of the partial recovery of funds. The residual loss to the customer was determined to be $1,330,646.02.

On July 17, 2024, a review of the transaction history for the Bluewater Equipment Inc. account at Cortex Bank and Trust was completed. The review identified no other transactions involving Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC.

On July 31, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust submitted a request to the receiving institution for additional information regarding the beneficiary account and the disposition of the funds that were not recovered.

On August 12, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received a response from the receiving institution indicating that the beneficiary account had been established shortly before the receipt of the wire transfer and that the funds had been subsequently transferred to multiple accounts at other institutions, including some held in the name of Clearspan Freight Corp. The investigation remains ongoing as Cortex Bank and Trust works with the receiving institution and law enforcement to trace the movement of the unrecovered funds and identify the responsible parties.

## Funds Tracing

A review of Cortex Bank and Trust's transaction records established that on July 10, 2024, a wire transfer in the amount of $1,728,111.71 was originated from the account of Bluewater Equipment Inc. The debit posted to the customer's account at 4:54 PM Eastern Time, minutes before the bank's wire processing cutoff. The transfer was routed through the Federal Reserve Wire Network (Fedwire). The beneficiary institution was identified as a large national bank. The beneficiary account name specified on the wire instructions was Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC. This name did not match the vendor, Obsidian Marine Services LLC, to whom Bluewater Equipment Inc. believed it was remitting payment for a scheduled equipment delivery.

Upon notification of the suspected fraud on July 11, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust transmitted an urgent recall request to the beneficiary institution via the Fedwire service message system, citing fraud. The beneficiary institution responded on July 17, 2024, indicating that the funds had already been credited to the account of Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC. The beneficiary institution further advised that a hold had been placed on the remaining balance in that account. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $397,465.69. This sum represents the entirety of the funds recovered from the initial fraudulent transfer.

The residual loss to Bluewater Equipment Inc., representing the portion of the initial transfer that could not be recovered, is $1,330,646.02. Further information regarding the disposition of the unrecovered funds was sought from the beneficiary institution through a USA PATRIOT Act Section 314(b) information-sharing request, initiated on July 31, 2024. The beneficiary institution provided a response on August 12, 2024, detailing the outflow of funds from the Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC account between July 10 and July 11, 2024.

According to the information provided by the beneficiary institution, the majority of the $1,330,646.02 was dissipated rapidly through a series of outbound domestic wire transfers. The funds were not converted to cash or cashier's checks at the beneficiary institution. The records provided indicate that four separate wire transfers were initiated from the Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC account on the morning of July 11, 2024, before the fraud hold could be instituted. These transfers were directed to accounts held at three different regional banks.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The funds transfer on July 10, 2024, directed $1,728,111.71 to Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC at an external financial institution. The beneficiary account details, provided in the compromised email chain, had not been used in previous transactions between Bluewater Equipment Inc. and Obsidian Marine Services LLC. The reviewing analyst conducted research into Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC to determine its business nature and the legitimacy of the account receiving the funds.

Public records research indicated that Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC was incorporated on May 30, 2024, slightly over a month before the fraudulent transfer occurred. The business registry listing provided a residential address for the principal place of business, which was not consistent with the commercial nature of the equipment leasing services invoiced. No corresponding operational footprint, such as a business website, commercial facility, or industry registration, was identified for Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC during open-source research. The lack of a verifiable commercial presence for the beneficiary entity is indicative of a shell company created to receive diverted funds.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

A review of the customer's communication logs and the documentation provided by the customer's management team was conducted to understand the sequence of events leading to the outbound wire transfer of $1,728,111.71. The customer supplied a series of email exchanges, ostensibly between their accounts payable department and a representative of Obsidian Marine Services LLC. The emails pertained to a purportedly overdue invoice for equipment leasing and maintenance services. The reviewing analyst noted that the sender's email address in the final, urgent communication directing payment did not match the established contact information for Obsidian Marine Services LLC. The domain name in the sender's address was a lookalike, differing by a single character from the legitimate domain used in previous, verified correspondence. The invoice attached to this final email was consistent in formatting and detail with prior invoices from Obsidian Marine Services LLC, but the remittance instructions directed payment to Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC, not Obsidian Marine Services LLC.

The relationship manager for Bluewater Equipment Inc. was interviewed regarding their interactions with the customer concerning this transaction. The relationship manager stated that they were contacted by the customer's controller on July 10, 2024, requesting assistance with an urgent wire transfer. The controller indicated that the payment was critical to avoid a disruption in services from Obsidian Marine Services LLC. The relationship manager recalled that the controller seemed unusually stressed and emphasized the need for immediate execution. The relationship manager confirmed that the wire request was submitted through the bank's online portal but noted that the customer requested an expedited review and release, bypassing their customary internal dual-approval process. The relationship manager stated they advised the controller of the risks associated with overriding established controls but ultimately processed the request based on the controller's authorization.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Following the identification of the fraudulent outbound wire transfer on July 10, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust personnel initiated immediate recovery protocols. An urgent SWIFT MT192 message requesting cancellation and return of the funds was transmitted to the receiving institution. Concurrently, a formal letter of indemnification was drafted and transmitted via secure channels to the fraud investigations unit at the receiving bank, citing a suspected business email compromise resulting in the misdirection of a $1,728,111.71 payment intended for Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC but credited to an account held by Obsidian Marine Services LLC. The reviewing analyst noted that the initial recovery request was hampered by the late hour of the original transfer, which occurred minutes before the daily wire cutoff time.

The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the indemnification request on July 11, 2024. Their initial communication indicated that the beneficiary account, held in the name of Obsidian Marine Services LLC, had been placed on a precautionary debit hold pending internal review. Subsequent communication from the receiving institution, received on July 17, 2024, confirmed that a portion of the transferred funds had already been disbursed prior to the imposition of the hold. The receiving institution reported that they were able to secure a partial recovery, freezing $397,465.69 within the beneficiary account. The reviewing analyst observed that the rapid dissipation of funds is consistent with typical wire fraud typologies, where illicit actors rapidly transfer or withdraw misappropriated funds to frustrate recovery efforts.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Bluewater Equipment Inc. was the victim of a business email compromise resulting in a fraudulent wire transfer on July 10, 2024. The reviewing analyst determined that a bad actor compromised the email account of a vendor, Obsidian Marine Services LLC, and sent payment instructions using a lookalike domain. The instructions directed a payment of $1,728,111.71 to an account held by Riverbend Management Enterprises LLC at an external institution. The customer initiated the transfer, overriding dual-approval controls due to urgency language in the fraudulent email. The funds were transferred minutes before the wire cutoff. The discrepancy in the beneficiary name was not identified until July 17, 2024, when Obsidian Marine Services LLC inquired about the outstanding invoice. Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request on that date. The investigation fixed September 17, 2024, as the date the fraudulent nature of the transfer was conclusively established, following confirmation from the receiving institution that the beneficiary account had been frozen with a partial recovery. The disposition of this matter is ongoing, pending further communication with the receiving institution and law enforcement regarding the residual loss to the customer.
