Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2405
Date opened: August 22, 2024
Subject: Ephraim Eriksson (individual), account 54-87990-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: closed_no_action

## Case Summary

The matter was referred to the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit following a customer complaint regarding a disputed outbound domestic wire transfer. The investigation was opened on August 9, 2024, to determine the circumstances surrounding the initiation of a funds transfer that the customer, Ephraim Eriksson, alleged was executed on the basis of deceptive instructions. The investigation focused on activity in Cortex Bank and Trust account 54-87990-1, a commercial checking account held by Ephraim Eriksson operating as a sole proprietorship. The primary objective of the review was to establish whether the wire transfer instructions originated from an authorized party, whether the funds were directed to a legitimate beneficiary intended by the customer, and whether the transaction exhibited characteristics indicative of wire fraud or business email compromise. The transaction under review occurred during a review period defined as April 24, 2024 through September 2, 2024. The investigation sought to evaluate the communication channels utilized to transmit the payment instructions, the authentication protocols employed during the transaction initiation, and the relationship, if any, between the customer and the beneficiary named in the wire transfer order.

The referral indicated that Ephraim Eriksson reported discovering the discrepancy during a routine reconciliation of the account. The customer asserted that a wire transfer in the amount of $104,055.79 was remitted to an unknown entity based on instructions received via email that appeared to be from a known vendor, Beacon Machinery Corp. The customer alleged that the email correspondence directed payment for an outstanding invoice to a new beneficiary account, differing from the payment instructions previously established for Beacon Machinery Corp. The investigation was tasked with reviewing the email correspondence provided by the customer, analyzing the wire transfer details, and assessing the overall transaction flow to ascertain the validity of the customer's claims. The review included an examination of the beneficiary information, the receiving institution, and any subsequent attempts to recover the funds. The investigation also evaluated the customer's adherence to established security procedures and the bank's internal controls regarding the processing of outbound wire transfers.

The scope of the investigation involved a detailed reconstruction of the events leading up to the initiation of the disputed wire transfer. The reviewing analyst examined the communication logs, transaction records, and account history for Cortex Bank and Trust account 54-87990-1 to identify any anomalies or deviations from the customer's historical activity profile. The investigation assessed the characteristics of the email containing the revised payment instructions, focusing on the sender's address, the language employed, and the timing of the request relative to the wire processing cutoff times. The review also considered the beneficiary names provided in the disputed instructions, specifically Pinnacle Ridge Freight Holdings Ltd. and Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC, to determine if these entities had any prior relationship with the customer or the known vendor, Beacon Machinery Corp. The investigation sought to determine whether the funds were induced out of the account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay, and to quantify the extent of the financial loss, taking into account any funds successfully frozen at the receiving institution. The investigation aimed to provide a comprehensive analysis of the incident to support a determination regarding the necessity of filing a Suspicious Activity Report.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit initiated this review following a referral from the bank’s fraud operations department on May 21, 2024. The referral detailed an allegation from Ephraim Eriksson, the sole authorized signer on Cortex Bank and Trust account 54-87990-1. Ephraim Eriksson asserted that a funds transfer he authorized and initiated from that account on May 17, 2024, was induced by fraudulent representations. The customer claimed he believed he was remitting payment to a known vendor, Beacon Machinery Corp., for an outstanding invoice. However, he later determined the funds were directed to an entity he did not intend to pay, Pinnacle Ridge Freight Holdings Ltd., based on altered payment instructions received via email.

According to the information provided by Ephraim Eriksson to the fraud operations department, the customer received an email on May 14, 2024, appearing to originate from his contact at Beacon Machinery Corp. The email contained an invoice and requested payment by wire transfer. The customer alleged that he subsequently received a follow-up email on May 17, 2024, urging immediate payment of the invoice to avoid delays in a scheduled equipment delivery. The customer stated that he acted on this urgent request and initiated an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $104,055.79 on the same day. He reported that he later discovered the email address from which the urgent payment request and altered wiring instructions were sent was a lookalike domain, differing from the legitimate vendor’s domain by a single character.

The referral indicated that Ephraim Eriksson became aware of the suspected fraud when the legitimate vendor, Beacon Machinery Corp., contacted him on May 21, 2024, regarding the unpaid invoice. The customer stated that upon reviewing the payment details, he realized the beneficiary name on the wire transfer, Pinnacle Ridge Freight Holdings Ltd., did not match the invoicing vendor, Beacon Machinery Corp. He further noted that the beneficiary account information provided in the fraudulent email differed from the payment details previously established for Beacon Machinery Corp. The customer asserted that he had no prior business relationship with Pinnacle Ridge Freight Holdings Ltd. and did not authorize a payment to that entity.

Upon receiving the customer's claim, the fraud operations department initiated a wire recall request on May 21, 2024, attempting to recover the $104,055.79 transferred on May 17, 2024. The receiving institution responded to the recall request, confirming that they were able to secure a portion of the transferred funds. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $32,257.29. The remaining funds had already been dispersed from the beneficiary account prior to the receipt of the recall notice. Consequently, the residual loss to the customer was determined to be $71,798.50. The fraud operations department subsequently escalated the matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit for a comprehensive review of the transaction and the surrounding circumstances, citing the customer's allegation of deception and the subsequent partial recovery of funds as the basis for the referral. The review was scoped to encompass the period from April 24, 2024 through September 2, 2024, to evaluate the customer's account activity prior to and following the disputed transaction.

## Timeline of Events

On April 24, 2024, Ephraim Eriksson received an email purporting to be from a representative of Beacon Machinery Corp., a known vendor with whom Mr. Eriksson had a documented history of transactions. Analysis of this communication subsequently revealed that the sender domain utilized a lookalike address, differing from the legitimate Beacon Machinery Corp. domain by a single character. This email contained an invoice for $104,055.79, corresponding to a scheduled payment for equipment previously ordered by Mr. Eriksson. The email included revised wire transfer instructions, directing payment to a beneficiary account held in the name of Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC. The communication emphasized the need for immediate payment to secure a promised delivery date, employing urgency language that pressured the recipient to bypass established internal protocols.

Two days later, on April 26, 2024, Mr. Eriksson initiated an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $104,055.79 from his Cortex Bank and Trust account, numbered 54-87990-1. The transfer was executed minutes before the established wire cutoff time for that business day. The beneficiary information provided by Mr. Eriksson matched the revised instructions contained in the fraudulent email, designating Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC as the recipient. The beneficiary name did not correspond to the invoicing vendor, Beacon Machinery Corp. This discrepancy was not identified by Mr. Eriksson at the time the transfer was initiated. The urgency conveyed in the fraudulent communication appears to have overridden the customer's customary dual-approval control process for outbound funds transfers.

The transfer of $104,055.79 was processed and the funds were transmitted to the receiving institution. No further activity related to this specific transaction occurred until May 14, 2024. On that date, Mr. Eriksson contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to inquire about the status of his payment to Beacon Machinery Corp., having received a past-due notice from the legitimate vendor. This contact initiated a review of the transaction by Cortex Bank and Trust personnel. The customer stated that he believed he had remitted payment according to the revised instructions received on April 24, 2024.

Following the customer's inquiry, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request to the receiving institution on May 17, 2024. The bank sought the return of the $104,055.79 wire transfer, citing suspected fraud. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request but indicated that the funds had already been partially dispersed. A hold was placed on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account.

On May 28, 2024, the receiving institution confirmed that $32,257.29 of the original wire amount had been successfully frozen in the account associated with Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC. The receiving institution reported that the remaining funds had been transferred to various other entities, including an account held by Pinnacle Ridge Freight Holdings Ltd., prior to the receipt of the recall request. Cortex Bank and Trust continued to monitor the situation and maintained communication with the receiving institution regarding the status of the frozen funds.

The investigation established that the total diverted amount was $104,055.79. The recovery efforts resulted in the securing of $32,257.29. Consequently, the residual loss incurred by the customer was determined to be $71,798.50. The matter was escalated within the Financial Intelligence Unit for further review on June 7, 2024. The review focused on the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire transfer and the subsequent discovery of the fraudulent activity. The customer's account activity was monitored for any further suspicious transactions during the remainder of the review period, which concluded on September 2, 2024. The findings of the investigation were documented in preparation for final disposition.

## Funds Tracing

The funds tracing phase of the investigation commenced with an analysis of the originating debit from Cortex Bank and Trust account 54-87990-1, held by Ephraim Eriksson. On May 14, 2024, a wire transfer in the amount of $104,055.79 was initiated from this account. The transaction record indicates that the transfer was submitted for processing shortly before the established wire cutoff time for that business day. The urgency of the transfer request, as documented in subsequent communications provided by the customer, resulted in the transaction bypassing the customary dual-approval control process generally applicable to outgoing wires of this magnitude. This procedural deviation was noted as a factor facilitating the rapid movement of the funds out of the originating account.

The outgoing wire transfer of $104,055.79 was directed to an account at a domestic receiving financial institution. The stated beneficiary on the wire instructions was Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC. However, a review of the invoicing documentation subsequently supplied by Ephraim Eriksson revealed that the intended recipient of the payment, based on the commercial transaction described in the invoice, was Beacon Machinery Corp. The disparity between the intended payee based on the invoice and the actual beneficiary designated in the wire instructions is a characteristic element of business email compromise schemes, where communication channels are intercepted and altered to misdirect funds. The investigation established that the communication directing the payment to Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC originated from a lookalike sender domain that differed from the legitimate domain associated with Beacon Machinery Corp. by a single character.

Upon identification of the suspected fraud, a recall request was transmitted to the receiving financial institution holding the account for Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC. A response from the receiving institution confirmed the receipt of the wire transfer but indicated that a significant portion of the funds had already been disbursed prior to the receipt of the recall notice. The receiving institution was successful in freezing $32,257.29 within the beneficiary account. The status of these frozen funds remains subject to the internal policies and procedures of the receiving institution, as well as any potential legal or regulatory actions.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary of the outbound wire transfer was identified in the payment instructions as Beacon Machinery Corp. Review of the transfer details indicated that the receiving account was held at a domestic financial institution. The beneficiary name provided on the transfer instructions did not align with the name of the invoicing vendor, which the customer's records identified as Pinnacle Ridge Freight Holdings Ltd. Public record research conducted on Beacon Machinery Corp. revealed that the entity was incorporated in a domestic jurisdiction. The incorporation date was not established in the available public records; however, the entity's registration status was active. The registered address for Beacon Machinery Corp. was a commercial mail receiving agency, and no physical operating address could be verified through independent research. A search of the address did not identify any other businesses operating from that location. The stated business purpose of Beacon Machinery Corp., as indicated by its name, suggested operations in the heavy equipment sector, which appeared incongruous with the services purportedly rendered by Pinnacle Ridge Freight Holdings Ltd., a freight and logistics provider.

Analysis of the transaction history of the receiving account, obtained through collaboration with the receiving institution, revealed a pattern of activity that was inconsistent with the expected operations of an established commercial entity. The account exhibited minimal transactional activity prior to the receipt of the $104,055.79 wire transfer from the Cortex Bank and Trust customer, Ephraim Eriksson. Following the credit of these funds, the account experienced a rapid depletion of the balance. The debits consisted primarily of outgoing wire transfers and ACH payments to various third parties. The counterparties receiving these funds included Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC, among others. The business purposes of these counterparties could not be fully ascertained through public record research, but their names suggested operations in import/export and general commerce. The rapid outward movement of funds, often in amounts slightly below the $10,000 currency transaction reporting threshold or the $3,000 funds transfer recordkeeping threshold, is a pattern frequently observed in the laundering of illicit proceeds. The volume and velocity of the outgoing transfers did not appear commensurate with standard commercial operations, particularly given the lack of corresponding operational expenses, such as payroll or utility payments, within the account history.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The reviewing analyst conducted an interview with Ephraim Eriksson on May 17, 2024 to discuss the circumstances surrounding the $104,055.79 wire transfer. Eriksson stated that the wire transfer was intended as payment for heavy equipment purchased from Beacon Machinery Corp., a vendor with whom he had an established business relationship. He indicated that he received an email, ostensibly from his regular contact at Beacon Machinery Corp., containing updated payment instructions. Eriksson provided the reviewing analyst with a copy of this email communication. A review of the email headers revealed that the sender's email address originated from a domain that was a lookalike, differing from the legitimate vendor's domain by a single character. This finding is consistent with a business email compromise scheme, wherein a threat actor intercepts or mimics legitimate communications to divert funds.

Eriksson further explained that the email containing the updated payment instructions included language stressing the urgency of the payment, citing impending supply chain disruptions if the funds were not received immediately. He stated that this urgency prompted him to initiate the transfer quickly, overriding the dual-approval control process typically employed for outgoing wires of this magnitude. This action circumvented internal controls designed to mitigate fraud risk. The reviewing analyst obtained copies of the invoice submitted by Eriksson to support the payment. An examination of the invoice revealed that while the formatting and logo appeared consistent with previous invoices from Beacon Machinery Corp., the beneficiary name on the invoice was Vantage Point Imports Enterprises LLC. This discrepancy, where the beneficiary name does not match the invoicing vendor, is a known indicator of potential fraud, suggesting the funds were being misdirected.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Cortex Bank and Trust dispatched a SWIFT MT192 message requesting cancellation and return of the fraudulent transfer on June 7, 2024. The request cited suspected fraud and asked the receiving institution to place a hold on the beneficiary account in the name of Pinnacle Ridge Freight Holdings Ltd. The receiving institution, located in the United Kingdom, responded via SWIFT MT199 on the following business day, confirming that a freeze had been placed on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution indicated that a portion of the funds had already been moved or withdrawn prior to the receipt of the recall request.

The receiving institution later confirmed that $32,257.29 remained in the beneficiary account and had been secured. Cortex Bank and Trust subsequently transmitted a formal letter of indemnity to the receiving institution on May 9, 2023, requesting the return of the secured funds. The letter of indemnity provided the necessary legal assurances required by the receiving institution to release the frozen funds back to Cortex Bank and Trust. The receiving institution processed the return, and Cortex Bank and Trust received the recovered amount on June 18, 2024. The recovered funds were credited back to the account of Ephraim Eriksson on the same day.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that the customer, Ephraim Eriksson, was the victim of a business email compromise scheme resulting in the diversion of $104,055.79. Analysis of email correspondence provided by the customer revealed that an unknown actor had registered a lookalike domain differing by one character from the customer's established supplier. The threat actor then used this domain to intercept an ongoing email thread regarding an outstanding invoice. The fraudulent email directed payment to a new beneficiary, Beacon Machinery Corp., and employed urgency language that bypassed the customer's internal dual-approval controls. The customer initiated the funds transfer minutes before the wire cutoff on August 16, 2024. The beneficiary name did not match the invoicing vendor, a discrepancy the customer failed to identify prior to authorizing the transfer. Cortex Bank and Trust was able to recall a portion of the funds from the receiving institution, reducing the residual loss to the customer. As the customer was the victim of the fraud and no evidence suggested complicity, the investigation is closed_no_action.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2406
Date opened: September 25, 2024
Subject: Adrian Wolcott (individual), account 10-17979-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: referred_to_fincen

## Case Summary

This investigation was initiated on August 19, 2024, following an escalation from the branch operations manager regarding a customer complaint of a diverted funds transfer. The customer, Adrian Wolcott, holds a commercial checking account at Cortex Bank and Trust (account number 10-17979-1). The escalation detailed a single outbound wire transfer in the amount of $236,220.57, which Mr. Wolcott reported was sent to a fraudulent beneficiary account on July 31, 2024. The escalation narrative indicated that Mr. Wolcott believed he was paying an invoice to a known vendor, Orchard Gate Metals LLC, but subsequently learned the vendor never received the funds. The branch operations manager placed a hold on the account and submitted a request for the Financial Intelligence Unit to review the transaction and the circumstances surrounding the authorization.

The primary objective of this investigation was to determine whether the July 31, 2024 wire transfer of $236,220.57 was the result of a business email compromise or other deceptive scheme, and to establish the sequence of events that led to the funds being diverted. The investigation sought to evaluate the communication between Mr. Wolcott and the purported vendor, the authorization process for the wire transfer, and the characteristics of the beneficiary account. The review aimed to assess the validity of the customer's claim of fraud and to identify any indicators of suspicious activity that would warrant regulatory reporting or further action by Cortex Bank and Trust.

A preliminary review of the transaction details for the July 31, 2024 wire transfer revealed several anomalies that necessitated further investigation. The beneficiary name on the wire instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Orchard Gate Metals LLC. The funds were directed to an entity named Ardent Exports Trading Co. Additionally, a review of the payment instructions provided by the customer to the branch staff indicated that the beneficiary account was held at a domestic financial institution, but the account name did not align with the vendor Mr. Wolcott intended to pay. The investigation sought to clarify why the customer authorized a payment to a beneficiary that differed from the invoicing party.

The escalation also noted that the wire transfer was initiated late in the business day on July 31, 2024. A review of the processing timestamp showed that the request was submitted minutes before the bank's established wire cutoff time. Furthermore, the escalation narrative indicated that the customer had received an email urging immediate payment, which bypassed the customer's customary dual-approval control for large outgoing transfers. The investigation sought to analyze the communication that prompted this expedited and non-standard authorization process.

The investigation plan included a detailed examination of Mr. Wolcott's account activity during the review period, with a specific focus on the days leading up to the July 31, 2024 transaction. The review was designed to identify any prior communication or transactions involving Orchard Gate Metals LLC, Ardent Exports Trading Co., or any other related entities, such as Limestone Consulting Trading Co., which was identified during the initial review of the customer's transaction history. The investigation also aimed to coordinate with the receiving financial institution to attempt the recovery of the $236,220.57 and to gather any available information regarding the beneficiary account and its ultimate owner. The objective was to synthesize these findings to determine the nature of the transaction and whether the activity observed constituted a reportable event under the Bank Secrecy Act.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On July 31, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust commercial relationship management team escalated an inquiry from the authorized signers on the operating account for Adrian Wolcott, account number 10-17979-1. The customer contacted their relationship manager to report that a high-value outgoing domestic wire transfer executed the previous day had been sent to a beneficiary not intended by the customer, and that the customer believed their payment process had been compromised by a third party. The wire in question was dispatched on July 30, 2024, and was directed to an account at a domestic commercial bank held in the name of Orchard Gate Metals LLC. The customer asserted to the relationship manager that this payment was intended to settle an outstanding invoice for industrial equipment supplied by a known vendor, Ardent Exports Trading Co. The customer further stated that they held no business relationship with Orchard Gate Metals LLC, had never transacted with that entity previously, and did not authorize a payment to that beneficiary.

The customer stated that the authorization to release the funds was provided based on payment instructions received via email on July 30, 2024. The customer supplied a copy of this email to the relationship manager. Initial review by the relationship manager noted that the email appeared to originate from a contact at Ardent Exports Trading Co., but the sender's domain name differed from the vendor's known domain by a single character. The customer reported that this discrepancy was not noticed by their accounts payable staff prior to initiating the transfer. The email correspondence provided by the customer included instructions to remit payment to a new, previously unutilized account and stressed the necessity of immediate payment to avoid a halt in pending shipments. The customer stated that this urgency prompted their staff to bypass internal dual-approval protocols for establishing new vendor payment details.

The outgoing transfer was initiated on July 30, 2024, shortly before the end-of-day wire processing cutoff. The payment instructions provided to Cortex Bank and Trust designated Orchard Gate Metals LLC as the beneficiary, which did not correspond to the name of the invoicing vendor, Ardent Exports Trading Co. The customer indicated that their staff did not identify this mismatch when entering the payment details into the bank's commercial banking portal. The relationship manager submitted the escalation to the Financial Intelligence Unit on July 31, 2024, requesting an investigation into the circumstances of the wire transfer and an assessment of the potential for funds recovery.

Following the initial escalation, the relationship manager submitted a formal wire recall request to the receiving institution on July 31, 2024, citing suspected fraud. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request but indicated that the funds had been credited to the beneficiary's account. Subsequent communication from the receiving institution confirmed that a portion of the funds had been secured, but the majority of the transferred amount was no longer available in the beneficiary account. The customer was advised of the partial recovery status by the relationship manager. The escalation was assigned to a reviewing analyst within the Financial Intelligence Unit to conduct a comprehensive review of the transactional activity and the related communications to determine the extent of the suspected compromise and to evaluate the activity against known typologies of wire fraud. The analyst was tasked with determining whether the activity warranted the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report based on the customer's assertion that they were induced to initiate a transfer to an unintended beneficiary through deceptive communications.

## Timeline of Events

On July 24, 2024, Adrian Wolcott contacted Cortex Bank and Trust via secure message to inquire about the status of a scheduled outgoing wire transfer. The customer stated the transfer was intended for a regular supplier, Orchard Gate Metals LLC, to settle a routine invoice. The reviewing analyst noted the customer provided a copy of the invoice, which appeared legitimate and was consistent with historical billing patterns from Orchard Gate Metals LLC. However, the payment instructions on the provided invoice directed funds to an account at a different financial institution in the name of Ardent Exports Trading Co. The customer stated he had received these revised payment instructions via email from a known contact at Orchard Gate Metals LLC on July 17, 2024.

The reviewing analyst obtained a copy of the July 17 email correspondence. The email originated from a domain that closely resembled the legitimate domain of Orchard Gate Metals LLC, differing by only one transposed character. The sender's display name matched the known contact at Orchard Gate Metals LLC. The email contained urgent language, instructing the customer to bypass the dual-approval control process typically used for supplier payments and immediately wire the funds to the new account, citing a supposed change in the supplier's banking arrangements and a critical supply chain deadline. The customer stated he had complied with these instructions due to the stated urgency and the apparent authenticity of the email.

On July 30, 2024, Adrian Wolcott initiated an outgoing wire transfer in the amount of $236,220.57. The transfer was directed to the account specified in the fraudulent email, held in the name of Ardent Exports Trading Co. The reviewing analyst noted the transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time for that business day. The customer later stated he had received a follow-up email from the fraudulent address on July 30, reiterating the urgency of the payment and confirming receipt of the funds, which further delayed his realization of the fraud.

On August 19, 2024, Adrian Wolcott contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report the suspected fraud. The customer stated he had been contacted by the legitimate Orchard Gate Metals LLC regarding the outstanding invoice, at which point he realized the July 17 email and subsequent payment instructions were fraudulent. The customer provided documentation confirming the true payment instructions for Orchard Gate Metals LLC, which differed from those used in the July 30 wire transfer.

Upon receiving the customer's report, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated a recall request for the $236,220.57 wire transfer. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the recall request but indicated the funds had already been credited to the beneficiary account. Following further communication, the receiving institution was able to freeze a portion of the funds, amounting to $21,259.85, that remained in the beneficiary account. The reviewing analyst noted the remaining funds had been subsequently transferred to other accounts or withdrawn, resulting in a residual loss to the customer of $214,960.72. The receiving institution provided limited information regarding the subsequent disposition of the funds, citing privacy regulations. The customer was advised to file a report with local law enforcement and provided with the necessary documentation to support their investigation. The reviewing analyst also noted a prior, unrelated inquiry from Adrian Wolcott on June 18, 2024, regarding a potential investment opportunity with Limestone Consulting Trading Co., which the customer ultimately decided against pursuing after consultation with his financial advisor. This prior inquiry was deemed unrelated to the current fraud incident.

## Funds Tracing

The originating transaction was a single outgoing wire transfer debited from the Cortex Bank and Trust checking account ending in 17979-1, held by Adrian Wolcott. The transaction occurred on May 30, 2024, in the amount of $236,220.57. The wire details indicated the beneficiary was Ardent Exports Trading Co., an entity not previously observed in the customer's transaction history. The stated purpose of the wire was the settlement of an invoice purportedly issued by Orchard Gate Metals LLC. The discrepancy between the invoiced vendor and the wire beneficiary was not identified prior to the execution of the transfer. The transfer was initiated shortly before the daily wire processing cutoff time, a factor that limited the window for pre-transmission review. The reviewing analyst documented that the transfer was induced by a communication utilizing a lookalike sender domain, differing from the legitimate vendor's domain by a single character. This communication also employed urgency language, which resulted in the circumvention of established dual-approval protocols for outgoing wires. The funds were transmitted via the Federal Reserve wire system.

The funds were received on May 30, 2024, by a domestic financial institution, where they were credited to an account held in the name of Ardent Exports Trading Co. Following the realization that the payment instructions were fraudulent, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request through the Federal Reserve system on June 18, 2024. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request and placed a hold on the beneficiary account. However, by the time the hold was effectuated, the majority of the funds had already been disbursed from the receiving account. The receiving institution reported that $21,259.85 remained in the account and was subsequently frozen pending further investigation and potential indemnification proceedings.

The reviewing analyst sought information regarding the onward movement of the funds disbursed prior to the hold. Information provided by the receiving institution, acting under section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act, indicated that the disbursed funds were transferred in multiple, smaller increments to an account at a third domestic financial institution. The beneficiary of these subsequent transfers was identified as Limestone Consulting Trading Co. These onward transfers occurred between May 31, 2024, and May 14, 2023, effectively draining the Ardent Exports Trading Co. account prior to the execution of the hold.

Further inquiries were directed to the third financial institution holding the Limestone Consulting Trading Co. account. The response received on July 24, 2024, detailed that the funds received from Ardent Exports Trading Co. were rapidly withdrawn. The primary method of withdrawal was the purchase of official bank checks, which were subsequently deposited at various other financial institutions. Additionally, a portion of the funds was withdrawn in cash in amounts consistently structured below the $10,000 regulatory reporting threshold, a pattern consistent with attempts to evade Currency Transaction Report requirements. The precise destination of the official checks and the ultimate beneficiaries of the cash withdrawals could not be conclusively determined by the reviewing analyst, as the trail extended beyond the visibility of Cortex Bank and Trust and the cooperating institutions.

The total amount diverted from the Adrian Wolcott account was $236,220.57. Following the freezing of the remaining balance at the initial receiving institution, the residual loss to the customer was determined to be $214,960.72. The investigation established that the funds moved through at least three domestic financial institutions and were ultimately dissipated through a combination of structured cash withdrawals and the purchase of official checks. The rapid movement of funds, the use of multiple intermediary entities, and the ultimate conversion to cash and negotiable instruments are consistent with typologies associated with the laundering of proceeds derived from wire fraud. The trail of the funds beyond the Limestone Consulting Trading Co. account remains unresolved.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

Investigation into the recipient of the diverted funds centered on an entity operating under the name Orchard Gate Metals LLC. The account held by this entity received the $236,220.57 transfer originating from Adrian Wolcott’s account at Cortex Bank and Trust on May 30, 2024. Public records research confirmed that Orchard Gate Metals LLC was registered as a domestic limited liability company. However, the registration date was recorded as May 29, 2024, exactly one day prior to the receipt of the wire transfer from the subject. This proximity between entity formation and the receipt of a large incoming wire transfer is consistent with the establishment of a shell company intended solely for the receipt and rapid dispersal of illicitly obtained funds.

Further analysis of the receiving entity’s business profile revealed significant inconsistencies. Orchard Gate Metals LLC purportedly operated as a wholesale distributor of specialized metal alloys. Open-source intelligence gathered during the review period yielded no digital footprint for this business. There was no corporate website, no listing in industry directories, and no evidence of a physical commercial presence at the registered address, which was identified as a mail forwarding service. The absence of any operational history or visible commercial activity for a business claiming to engage in six-figure wholesale transactions is anomalous and suggests the stated business purpose was fictitious.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

On July 31, 2024, an interview was conducted with Adrian Wolcott, the authorized signer on Cortex Bank and Trust account 10-17979-1. The customer stated that a wire transfer requested on July 30, 2024, was intended for an established vendor, Orchard Gate Metals LLC. The customer asserted that instructions for the transfer were received via email on July 24, 2024, from an individual purporting to be the vendor's accounts receivable contact. The customer provided copies of the email correspondence and the attached invoice to the investigating analyst.

A review of the email correspondence provided by the customer revealed significant anomalies. The sender's email address utilized a domain name that was a close variation of the legitimate Orchard Gate Metals LLC domain, differing by a single character. The emails from this lookalike domain contained instructions directing payment to a new beneficiary, Ardent Exports Trading Co., at a different financial institution. The emails emphasized an urgent need for payment, citing potential supply chain disruptions if the funds were not received immediately. The customer stated that this urgency language prompted the circumvention of established dual-approval procedures for wire transfers. The attached invoice, while appearing similar to previous invoices from Orchard Gate Metals LLC, listed Ardent Exports Trading Co. as the payee and provided the new account details. The customer confirmed that no independent verification of the new payment instructions was conducted prior to initiating the wire transfer.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

On August 19, 2024, the reviewing analyst submitted a formal request for indemnification and return of funds to the receiving institution via the Fedwire system. The request detailed the circumstances of the wire fraud affecting the account of Adrian Wolcott, specifically noting the fraudulent outbound wire amount of $236,220.57. The communication emphasized that the transfer was induced by a compromised business email compromise, as evidenced by a lookalike sender domain differing by one character, and that the beneficiary name, Limestone Consulting Trading Co., did not match the invoicing vendor, Orchard Gate Metals LLC. The request also cited the urgency language overriding the dual-approval control, which had facilitated the funds transfer initiated minutes before the wire cutoff on July 31, 2024.

The receiving institution acknowledged the request on the same day. However, their initial response indicated that the funds in the beneficiary account were no longer fully available. The receiving institution stated that they had placed a hold on the remaining balance in the Limestone Consulting Trading Co. account, but a substantial portion of the funds had already been withdrawn or transferred out. The receiving institution requested additional documentation to substantiate the fraud claim, which the reviewing analyst provided, including a copy of the fraudulent invoice and the relevant email correspondence showing the lookalike sender domain.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that the customer, Adrian Wolcott, remitted funds intended for an established vendor to an unrelated beneficiary account held by Orchard Gate Metals LLC. The relationship manager confirmed with the customer that the payment instructions were received via email from an address that spoofed the vendor's domain, differing by a single character. The email communication contained language stressing urgency, which the customer cited as the reason for overriding their internal dual-approval control for outgoing wires. Based on the review of the communication and the destination of the funds, the reviewing analyst concluded that the customer was the victim of a business email compromise scheme. The total sum established as diverted was $236,220.57. Following the discovery of the fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution to request a return of funds. The receiving institution was able to freeze a portion of the funds, resulting in a residual loss to the customer. The investigation determined that the fraudulent activity was completed on September 9, 2024. The activity is consistent with wire fraud. The case is closed and referred_to_fincen.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2407
Date opened: September 18, 2024
Subject: Limestone Capital Group LLC (business), account 42-11419-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: criminal_referral

## Case Summary

This investigation was initiated on August 21, 2024, following an escalation from the commercial banking relationship manager assigned to Limestone Capital Group LLC. The relationship manager reported that the customer had contacted the bank earlier that day, stating they had discovered a significant payment was misdirected to an unknown beneficiary. The matter was referred to the Financial Intelligence Unit for review and analysis of the transaction, which involved Cortex Bank and Trust account 42-11419-1. The investigation focused on determining the circumstances surrounding a single outbound wire transfer in the amount of $3,552,197.05, establishing whether the customer was the victim of wire fraud, and assessing the bank's exposure and reporting obligations.

The review period for this investigation was defined as May 21, 2024, through September 2, 2024. The primary objective was to examine the authorization, origination, and processing of the outbound wire transfer to ascertain if the funds were induced out of the customer account by deception and moved to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay. The initial escalation indicated that Limestone Capital Group LLC believed they were remitting payment for a scheduled capital call, but later determined the instructions they received were not from the intended recipient. The investigation sought to reconstruct the communication sequence that led to the execution of the payment order.

The transaction under review was a domestic wire transfer of $3,552,197.05, initiated from Cortex Bank and Trust account 42-11419-1. The investigation was tasked with identifying the beneficiary of this transfer and evaluating the communication channels through which the payment instructions were delivered to the customer. A key focus of the inquiry was to analyze the email correspondence provided by the customer to identify any indicators of a business email compromise or other deceptive practices that may have influenced the authorization of the wire transfer.

The escalation noted that the customer had expected to remit funds to an entity known to them, but the executed wire instructions directed the payment elsewhere. The investigation was required to review the beneficiary details provided in the wire instructions and compare them against the customer's known vendors and counterparties, which included Obsidian Capital Partners LP, Aperture Capital LLC, and Pinnacle Ridge Management Group LLC. The goal was to establish whether the customer had a legitimate business relationship with the receiving entity or if the payment was diverted as the result of a fraudulent scheme.

Furthermore, the investigation was directed to review the internal processing of the wire transfer to determine if any internal controls were bypassed or overridden during the authorization process. The reviewing analyst was tasked with examining the timing of the transfer request and the circumstances surrounding its approval, particularly in relation to the bank's established procedures for high-value commercial wire transfers. The investigation also sought to establish the timeline of events, including key dates such as May 21, 2024, May 22, 2024, May 30, 2024, June 7, 2024, June 14, 2024, June 25, 2024, June 28, 2024, and July 10, 2024, to construct a chronological record of the activity leading up to the disputed transaction. The central question the Financial Intelligence Unit had to answer was whether the $3,552,197.05 wire transfer constituted suspicious activity indicative of wire fraud, thereby requiring the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report and potential referral to law enforcement.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On June 25, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit received an internal escalation from the Commercial Banking division. The relationship manager for Limestone Capital Group LLC reported a suspected business email compromise resulting in a misdirected outgoing wire transfer. The relationship manager stated that the customer’s chief financial officer contacted the bank by telephone to report the loss earlier that same day.

The escalation indicated that on June 14, 2024, Limestone Capital Group LLC originated an outgoing domestic wire transfer in the amount of $3,552,197.05. The customer asserted to the relationship manager that these funds were intended for Obsidian Capital Partners LP in settlement of a capital call. The customer alleged that a malicious actor intercepted the communication chain and provided fraudulent payment instructions.

According to the initial report from the relationship manager, the customer’s accounts payable department received an email appearing to originate from Obsidian Capital Partners LP. The email contained wire instructions directing the payment of $3,552,197.05 to an account held at a different domestic financial institution in the name of Aperture Capital LLC. The customer indicated that the email emphasized an urgent deadline for the capital call funding.

The customer informed the relationship manager that the accounts payable department processed the wire transfer to Aperture Capital LLC on June 14, 2024, believing they were satisfying the obligation to Obsidian Capital Partners LP. The customer realized the error on June 25, 2024, when Obsidian Capital Partners LP contacted them regarding the outstanding capital call.

The relationship manager’s escalation noted that the customer identified a discrepancy in the sender’s email address upon subsequent review. The domain used in the email containing the fraudulent wire instructions differed from the legitimate domain of Obsidian Capital Partners LP by a single transposed character. The customer asserted that this lookalike domain, combined with the urgency language in the email, led to the circumvention of their internal dual-approval controls for wire transfers.

The escalation further noted that the beneficiary name on the fraudulent wire instructions, Aperture Capital LLC, did not correspond to the invoicing vendor, Obsidian Capital Partners LP. The customer stated to the relationship manager that this discrepancy was overlooked during the processing of the wire transfer due to the perceived urgency of the request.

Upon receiving the escalation, the reviewing analyst in the Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a review of the transaction. Bank records confirmed that the outgoing wire transfer of $3,552,197.05 was processed from the Limestone Capital Group LLC account ending in 11419-1 on June 14, 2024. The transfer was directed to an account at a domestic financial institution in the name of Aperture Capital LLC.

The reviewing analyst noted that the wire transfer was initiated shortly before the bank’s daily wire cutoff time on June 14, 2024. The timing of the transaction, coupled with the customer’s allegations regarding the lookalike domain and the mismatched beneficiary name, prompted further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the transfer and the potential involvement of the beneficiary, Aperture Capital LLC, or other entities such as Pinnacle Ridge Management Group LLC, which was identified in the customer’s broader account activity.

The Financial Intelligence Unit commenced an investigation to verify the customer’s claims, analyze the transaction activity of Limestone Capital Group LLC, and assess the potential for recovery of the funds. The investigation sought to determine whether the activity was consistent with a business email compromise scheme and whether the funds transferred on June 14, 2024, were diverted for illicit purposes.

## Timeline of Events

The events precipitating the diversion of funds from Cortex Bank and Trust account 42-11419-1, held by Limestone Capital Group LLC, began on May 21, 2024. On that date, an employee of Limestone Capital Group LLC responsible for accounts payable received an email from a sender purporting to represent a regular vendor, Obsidian Capital Partners LP. The email contained an invoice and requested a change to the vendor's payment instructions. The reviewing analyst determined that the sender domain in the email differed from the legitimate domain of Obsidian Capital Partners LP by a single character. The employee at Limestone Capital Group LLC did not identify this discrepancy and engaged in a series of email exchanges with the fraudulent sender.

On May 22, 2024, the fraudulent sender reiterated the request for updated payment instructions, citing an upcoming audit and insisting that the payment be expedited to the new account. The employee at Limestone Capital Group LLC confirmed receipt of the new instructions and indicated that the payment would be processed accordingly. The correspondence reviewed by the analyst showed the fraudulent sender applying pressure, emphasizing the importance of immediate payment to avoid disruptions in service.

The critical event occurred on May 30, 2024. The employee at Limestone Capital Group LLC initiated an outbound wire transfer of $3,552,197.05 to the new account specified by the fraudulent sender. The beneficiary named on the wire instructions was Aperture Capital LLC, which did not match the invoicing vendor, Obsidian Capital Partners LP. Furthermore, the transfer was initiated mere minutes before the bank's daily wire cutoff time. The urgency language employed by the fraudulent sender had the effect of overriding the dual-approval control process typically employed by Limestone Capital Group LLC for large transactions. The funds were successfully transmitted to the receiving institution.

The deception remained undetected for a significant period. On June 7, 2024, a representative from the legitimate Obsidian Capital Partners LP contacted Limestone Capital Group LLC to inquire about the overdue payment. It was at this juncture that the employee who had processed the wire transfer realized the payment instructions had been fraudulent. Limestone Capital Group LLC immediately contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report the fraud and request a recall of the wire.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated standard recall procedures on June 14, 2024. Communication was established with the receiving institution, which confirmed that the funds had been received and partially disbursed. The receiving institution placed a hold on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account, which amounted to $461,785.62. This sum represented the portion of the $3,552,197.05 fraudulent outbound wire that had not yet been withdrawn or transferred elsewhere.

Further investigation into the beneficiary account revealed that it was controlled by an entity named Pinnacle Ridge Management Group LLC. The relationship between Aperture Capital LLC, the named beneficiary on the wire, and Pinnacle Ridge Management Group LLC, the account holder, remains unclear, as no legitimate business connection was identified during the review.

On June 25, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received formal notification from the receiving institution that the $461,785.62 frozen in the beneficiary account would be returned. The funds were credited back to the Limestone Capital Group LLC account 42-11419-1 on June 28, 2024.

Despite the recovery of a portion of the funds, the residual loss to the customer remained substantial. The difference between the original fraudulent wire of $3,552,197.05 and the recovered amount of $461,785.62 resulted in a loss of $3,090,411.43 to Limestone Capital Group LLC.

The investigation continued into the summer months, with the bank compiling the necessary documentation to detail the fraud. By July 10, 2024, the initial evidence gathering phase was complete, focusing on the email correspondence and the transaction records. The final analysis of the events and the preparation of the investigation report concluded on August 21, 2024, finalizing the timeline of the incident.

## Funds Tracing

The movement of funds from Cortex Bank and Trust account 42-11419-1, held by Limestone Capital Group LLC, was traced following the execution of the fraudulent outbound wire transfer on June 14, 2024. The total amount diverted in this incident was $3,552,197.05. The funds left the customer account at Cortex Bank and Trust and were directed to a domestic beneficiary institution. The instruction provided by the threat actor directed the funds to an account purportedly held by Aperture Capital LLC. The reviewing analyst confirmed the immediate destination of the funds was a commercial banking institution within the United States.

Upon identifying the fraudulent nature of the June 14, 2024 transfer, Cortex Bank and Trust staff initiated standard recovery protocols. Communication with the beneficiary institution was established to request the freezing and return of the funds. The beneficiary institution confirmed receipt of the $3,552,197.05 wire transfer. Subsequent tracing efforts focused on the activity within the beneficiary account following the credit. The beneficiary institution reported that the funds were not held in the receiving account for a significant duration.

Information obtained from the beneficiary institution indicated that a portion of the funds was rapidly dispersed. The tracing confirmed that the beneficiary institution was able to freeze a portion of the transferred amount. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $461,785.62. This freeze action prevented the onward movement of these specific funds. The remaining balance of the initial transfer had already been moved prior to the freeze taking effect. The residual loss to the customer, representing the funds that could not be secured at the first hop, was calculated at $3,090,411.43.

The investigation attempted to trace the $3,090,411.43 that was transferred out of the initial beneficiary account. The beneficiary institution disclosed that these funds were dispersed through a series of subsequent wire transfers. The onward movement involved multiple secondary beneficiary institutions, both domestic and international. The specific details of these secondary transfers, including the names of the receiving institutions and the beneficiary account holders, were not fully available to Cortex Bank and Trust. The tracing of the funds beyond the initial beneficiary institution relies on the limited information provided by that institution during the recovery attempt.

It is inferred, based on common typologies associated with this type of fraud, that the dispersed funds were likely moved through a network of accounts designed to obfuscate the origin and ownership of the funds. The reviewing analyst noted that the rapid dispersion of funds is consistent with efforts to hinder recovery. The trail of the $3,090,411.43 effectively ends at the point of the secondary transfers from the initial beneficiary account, as Cortex Bank and Trust lacks the visibility to track the funds through subsequent hops. No information was available to confirm if the funds were ultimately converted to cash, cryptocurrency, or other instruments.

The investigation established the initial movement of the $3,552,197.05 from Cortex Bank and Trust to the first beneficiary institution. The tracing confirmed the successful freeze of $461,785.62 at that institution. The onward movement of the remaining $3,090,411.43 is documented only to the extent that it was transferred out of the initial receiving account. The ultimate destination and disposition of the unrecovered funds remain unknown due to the limitations of visibility beyond the first hop in the transfer chain. The tracing efforts confirm the diversion of the funds and the partial success of the recovery actions.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The investigation reviewed the beneficiary of the outbound funds transfer of $3,552,197.05 to determine the nature of the entity and its relationship to the subject, Limestone Capital Group LLC. The receiving account was held at an external financial institution in the name of Aperture Capital LLC. Open-source research indicated that Aperture Capital LLC was registered as a limited liability company in a jurisdiction known for corporate secrecy. The formation date was recorded as May 30, 2024, slightly over a month prior to the receipt of the funds from Limestone Capital Group LLC on July 10, 2024. The stated business purpose in public records was broadly defined as consulting and investment advisory services. No physical address was identified for the business operations; the registered address corresponded to a mail forwarding service.

A review of the beneficiary account activity, obtained through a 314(b) information-sharing request with the receiving institution, revealed a pattern of transactions inconsistent with a recently established consulting firm. Prior to the receipt of the $3,552,197.05 from Cortex Bank and Trust, the account had minimal activity, characterized by a few low-dollar deposits and debits consistent with account maintenance fees. This low volume of activity abruptly shifted following the deposit of the funds from Limestone Capital Group LLC.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The reviewing analyst conducted an interview with the principal of Limestone Capital Group LLC regarding the initiation of the outbound wire transfer. The principal confirmed that they had received an email communication on May 21, 2024, appearing to be from Obsidian Capital Partners LP, directing a capital call payment. The principal stated that the email correspondence was consistent in tone and formatting with previous communications from Obsidian Capital Partners LP. The principal further advised that they had maintained a business relationship with Obsidian Capital Partners LP for several years and had no reason to suspect the communication was fraudulent. The principal noted that the email communication contained language emphasizing the urgency of the capital call payment and requesting immediate processing. The principal stated that this urgency prompted them to initiate the wire transfer on May 22, 2024, bypassing the customary dual-approval control established for Limestone Capital Group LLC accounts at Cortex Bank and Trust. The principal confirmed that they authorized the transfer of $3,552,197.05 to an account held by Aperture Capital LLC, believing it to be an account associated with Obsidian Capital Partners LP. The principal stated that they did not verify the beneficiary account information with Obsidian Capital Partners LP prior to initiating the transfer.

The reviewing analyst obtained and reviewed the email correspondence provided by the principal of Limestone Capital Group LLC. The email headers indicated that the sender address was a lookalike domain differing by one character from the legitimate domain used by Obsidian Capital Partners LP. The email communication contained an invoice appearing to be issued by Obsidian Capital Partners LP, but the beneficiary name on the invoice was Aperture Capital LLC. The reviewing analyst noted that the invoice format was similar to previous invoices from Obsidian Capital Partners LP, but the banking details provided were distinct from those previously used for capital call payments. The email communication also contained language emphasizing the urgency of the capital call payment and requesting immediate processing. The reviewing analyst obtained and reviewed the authentication logs for the online banking session during which the wire transfer was initiated. The logs indicated that the wire transfer was initiated by the principal of Limestone Capital Group LLC on May 22, 2024, minutes before the wire cutoff time. The logs also confirmed that the transfer was authorized without the customary dual-approval control, consistent with the principal's statement regarding the urgency of the request.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

On May 30, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust sent a formal request for recall and indemnification to the receiving institution via the interbank messaging system. The message identified the outbound wire as having been induced by fraud and requested that the receiving institution freeze the funds and return them to Cortex Bank and Trust. The receiving institution acknowledged the request on the same date and initiated an investigation into the beneficiary account.

The receiving institution confirmed on June 7, 2024, that it had placed a hold on the beneficiary account. However, the receiving institution also indicated that the majority of the funds had already been transferred out of the account or withdrawn prior to the hold being placed. The investigation established that the funds diverted by the fraudulent outbound wire amount totaled $3,552,197.05.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Limestone Capital Group LLC was the victim of a business email compromise targeting a scheduled capital call. On August 21, 2024, the subject initiated an outbound wire transfer of $3,552,197.05 to Obsidian Capital Partners LP. The transfer request was received via email, ostensibly from the subject's managing partner, and contained language directing staff to bypass dual-approval controls to meet an impending deadline. The reviewing analyst determined the sender domain differed from the legitimate domain by a single character. The beneficiary name on the wire instructions did not match the vendor named on the associated invoice. The transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time. On September 6, 2024, the subject notified Cortex Bank and Trust that the transfer was fraudulent and the intended beneficiary, Aperture Capital LLC, had not received the funds. Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution and successfully froze a portion of the funds, resulting in a residual loss to the customer of $3,090,411.43. Due to the nature of the activity, the disposition is criminal_referral.
