## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2408
Date opened: November 6, 2024
Subject: Westmarch Distribution Inc. (business), account 74-98263-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: ongoing

## Case Summary

On October 7, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit received a referral from the commercial banking relationship manager assigned to Westmarch Distribution Inc. The referral requested an immediate review of an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $3,863,579.20, originating from Westmarch Distribution Inc. operating account 74-98263-1. The relationship manager reported that the customer had contacted the bank earlier that day, stating they had been notified by a long-standing vendor, Saltmarsh Produce Corp., that a scheduled invoice payment had not been received. Westmarch Distribution Inc. management indicated their records showed the payment had been sent via wire transfer to a new account number provided by an individual purporting to be a Saltmarsh Produce Corp. accounts receivable representative. The communication regarding the new account details occurred via email.

Upon receiving the referral, the Financial Intelligence Unit initiated case FIU-WIRE-2408 to determine whether the $3,863,579.20 outbound wire transfer represented the proceeds of fraud and to identify any potential compliance or reporting obligations for Cortex Bank and Trust. The review period for this investigation was established as July 2, 2024, through October 29, 2024, to encompass the period leading up to the transaction in question and allow for subsequent analysis of account activity. The investigation aimed to establish the sequence of events leading to the wire transfer, verify the legitimacy of the payment instructions, and assess the customer's adherence to internal payment controls. The initial assessment categorized the matter as medium risk, pending further investigation into the nature of the communication between Westmarch Distribution Inc. and the purported vendor representative.

The primary objective of the initial review was to analyze the specific transaction identified in the referral. The reviewing analyst examined the wire transfer details, noting the beneficiary name and the receiving institution. The investigation also required a review of the communications between Westmarch Distribution Inc. and the entity claiming to be Saltmarsh Produce Corp. The customer provided copies of email correspondence related to the change in payment instructions. A preliminary review of these emails indicated the presence of urgency language, which the customer stated contributed to their decision to expedite the payment process. The customer further reported that this urgency led to the circumvention of their standard dual-approval control for outbound wire transfers. The reviewing analyst also observed that the wire transfer was initiated late in the business day, shortly before the bank's established wire cutoff time.

The investigation sought to determine the extent of the customer's interaction with the entities involved in the transaction. The reviewing analyst noted the involvement of other entities, specifically Vantage Point Trading Inc. and Harborview Management LLC, in the broader context of the customer's business operations, though their direct connection to the transaction in question remained subject to further analysis. The immediate focus remained on the $3,863,579.20 transfer and the circumstances surrounding its authorization. The Financial Intelligence Unit commenced efforts to trace the funds and coordinate with the receiving institution to ascertain the status of the transferred amount. The investigation also required a determination of the actual loss incurred by the customer, considering any potential recovery efforts. The initial findings indicated a need for a comprehensive review of the customer's email security protocols and vendor verification procedures. The case remains open and under investigation by the Financial Intelligence Unit.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The Financial Intelligence Unit of Cortex Bank and Trust commenced an investigation into activity conducted through the commercial checking account of Westmarch Distribution Inc. on October 7, 2024. The investigation was initiated following the receipt of an urgent notification from the customer, Westmarch Distribution Inc., alleging that a substantial outbound wire transfer processed on their behalf earlier that same day was fraudulent. The customer asserted that the funds were induced out of their account through deception and directed to a beneficiary they had never intended to pay. The initial referral indicated that the customer believed their internal email communications had been compromised and manipulated by an unknown third party. 

According to the information provided by the principal of Westmarch Distribution Inc., the company had been engaged in routine commercial transactions with a known supplier, Saltmarsh Produce Corp. The customer reported that they had received an email appearing to originate from Saltmarsh Produce Corp., containing payment instructions for a significant outstanding invoice. This email, which the customer later determined was fraudulent, instructed Westmarch Distribution Inc. to remit the payment via wire transfer to a new bank account at a different financial institution. The customer stated that they had acted upon these instructions, believing them to be legitimate communication from their established vendor. 

The customer's notification to Cortex Bank and Trust detailed that the fraudulent email exhibited significant urgency, pressuring Westmarch Distribution Inc. to expedite the payment to avoid supply chain disruptions. This urgency language, according to the customer's account, led their internal personnel to bypass the company's established dual-approval control for large outgoing wire transfers. The customer further alleged that the fraudulent email contained a lookalike sender domain that differed from the legitimate domain of Saltmarsh Produce Corp. by only a single character, which contributed to the deception. The customer stated that the wire transfer was initiated by their staff just minutes before the bank's daily wire cutoff time on October 7, 2024, in an attempt to meet the purported urgent deadline set by the fraudulent email.

Upon realizing the deception, the customer immediately contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report the incident and request a recall of the funds. The customer alleged that the wire transfer, which amounted to $3,863,579.20, was entirely unauthorized and represented a total loss if not recovered. The customer provided Cortex Bank and Trust with copies of the relevant email correspondence, including the initial fraudulent message and subsequent communications, to support their claim. The customer also provided documentation confirming their established business relationship with Saltmarsh Produce Corp. and the legitimate invoice that they believed they were paying. 

The referral from Westmarch Distribution Inc. emphasized the sophisticated nature of the deception, pointing to the manipulated email domain and the targeted urgency language as key elements of the fraud. The customer requested that Cortex Bank and Trust take immediate action to interdict the funds at the receiving institution and initiate a formal investigation into the matter. Based on this referral and the initial review of the provided documentation, the Financial Intelligence Unit opened a formal investigation to determine the facts surrounding the wire transfer, assess the extent of the alleged fraud, and coordinate recovery efforts with the receiving institution. The investigation focused on verifying the customer's claims, analyzing the transactional data, and identifying any potential compliance or security implications for Cortex Bank and Trust.

## Timeline of Events

On July 2, 2024, the relationship manager for Westmarch Distribution Inc. received a phone call from an individual identifying himself as an accounts receivable clerk for Saltmarsh Produce Corp. The caller stated that Saltmarsh Produce Corp. had recently updated its banking information and requested that Westmarch Distribution Inc. remit all future payments to a new account. The caller advised that formal written instructions would follow. The relationship manager noted this conversation in the customer contact log but did not independently verify the request with a known contact at Saltmarsh Produce Corp.

On July 25, 2024, the accounts payable department at Westmarch Distribution Inc. received an email bearing the sender name of the regular contact at Saltmarsh Produce Corp. The reviewing analyst determined that the sender domain in this email differed from the legitimate Saltmarsh Produce Corp. domain by one character. The email contained updated payment instructions, directing funds to an account held in the name of Vantage Point Trading Inc. The email also included an invoice for a large order of produce that Westmarch Distribution Inc. had recently received. The invoice appeared to be on legitimate Saltmarsh Produce Corp. letterhead.

On July 30, 2024, an employee in the accounts payable department at Westmarch Distribution Inc. initiated a wire transfer to Vantage Point Trading Inc. in the amount of $3,863,579.20. The employee later stated to the relationship manager that the email received on July 25, 2024, contained language stressing the urgency of the payment to avoid disruption of future shipments. This urgency language appears to have induced the employee to bypass the customer's established dual-approval control for wire transfers exceeding a specific threshold. The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary name on the wire transfer, Vantage Point Trading Inc., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Saltmarsh Produce Corp. Furthermore, the wire transfer was initiated mere minutes before the bank's daily cutoff time.

On August 26, 2024, Westmarch Distribution Inc. contacted the relationship manager to inquire about the status of the wire transfer initiated on July 30, 2024. The customer stated that Saltmarsh Produce Corp. was claiming non-receipt of payment for the invoice. The relationship manager initiated an inquiry with the wire room to trace the funds.

On August 27, 2024, the wire room confirmed that the funds had been successfully delivered to the receiving institution on July 30, 2024. The relationship manager relayed this information to Westmarch Distribution Inc. and advised the customer to contact Saltmarsh Produce Corp. to resolve the discrepancy.

On September 2, 2024, Westmarch Distribution Inc. notified Cortex Bank and Trust that it had been the victim of wire fraud. The customer provided documentation demonstrating that the email received on July 25, 2024, originated from a lookalike domain and that Saltmarsh Produce Corp. had not changed its banking information. The relationship manager immediately escalated the matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit.

On September 10, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust submitted a request to the receiving institution to freeze the funds associated with the fraudulent wire transfer. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the request and initiated an investigation.

On September 20, 2024, the receiving institution informed Cortex Bank and Trust that it had successfully frozen $1,081,802.18 of the funds transferred on July 30, 2024. The receiving institution indicated that the remaining funds had been subsequently transferred to an account held by Harborview Management LLC at a third institution.

On October 7, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit concluded its initial review of the case and determined that the activity was consistent with wire fraud. The investigation established that the entire amount of $3,863,579.20 had been diverted. The customer suffered a residual loss of $2,781,777.02. The investigation into the subsequent movement of the funds to Harborview Management LLC remains ongoing.

## Funds Tracing

On September 10, 2024, the subject Westmarch Distribution Inc. requested a domestic wire transfer of $3,863,579.20 from their Cortex Bank and Trust commercial checking account 74-98263-1. The beneficiary institution on the funds transfer instruction was a domestic regional bank. The beneficiary name provided was Vantage Point Trading Inc., a corporate entity not previously observed in the customer's transaction history. The debit to the Westmarch Distribution Inc. account was processed and the funds were transmitted out of Cortex Bank and Trust. The investigation confirmed that this was the originating hop in the suspected fraud.

The originating transfer instruction was received late in the business day, minutes prior to the established wire cutoff time. The customer cited urgency, noting that the vendor, which they believed to be Saltmarsh Produce Corp., required immediate settlement. This urgency language was used to override the customer's internal dual-approval controls. The investigation subsequently identified that the payment instructions were received via email from a sender domain that differed from the legitimate domain of Saltmarsh Produce Corp. by a single character. The customer, operating under the mistaken belief that they were settling an outstanding invoice with Saltmarsh Produce Corp., directed the $3,863,579.20 to Vantage Point Trading Inc.

Information sharing with the receiving institution established the immediate onward movement of the funds. Upon receipt into the Vantage Point Trading Inc. account on September 10, 2024, the funds were not held. On September 11, 2024, the receiving institution observed a series of outgoing transfers from the Vantage Point Trading Inc. account. These transfers were directed to multiple accounts held at various domestic and international financial institutions. The receiving institution indicated that these onward transfers were executed rapidly, consistent with attempts to dissipate the funds before recovery efforts could be initiated. The specific beneficiary names and account numbers for these onward transfers were not disclosed to Cortex Bank and Trust.

The receiving institution further reported that a portion of the funds transferred from the Vantage Point Trading Inc. account were directed to an entity identified as Harborview Management LLC. The exact amount transferred to Harborview Management LLC was not provided, but the receiving institution noted that it represented a significant fraction of the initial deposit. The onward movement to Harborview Management LLC and the other unidentified entities represents the second hop in the funds tracing. The trail for these specific funds ends at the respective receiving institutions, as Cortex Bank and Trust does not have visibility into the subsequent activity within those accounts.

On September 20, 2024, Westmarch Distribution Inc. contacted Cortex Bank and Trust, reporting that Saltmarsh Produce Corp. had not received the expected payment. The customer realized the deception and requested a wire recall. Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated a recall request through the established interbank channels. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request and initiated a freeze on the remaining funds in the Vantage Point Trading Inc. account.

The receiving institution confirmed that they were able to secure $1,081,802.18. This amount represents the portion of the initial $3,863,579.20 transfer that had not yet been dissipated through onward transfers. The secured funds were subsequently returned to Cortex Bank and Trust and credited back to the Westmarch Distribution Inc. account 74-98263-1 on October 7, 2024. The investigation concluded that the remaining $2,781,777.02 had been successfully diverted by the unknown actors. The trail for these diverted funds ends with the initial onward transfers from the Vantage Point Trading Inc. account, as the receiving institution was unable to recover them from the subsequent beneficiaries. The customer sustained a residual loss in this amount.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary of the $3,863,579.20 outbound wire transfer, Harborview Management LLC, was the subject of public records and commercial registry research. The entity was registered on July 25, 2024, slightly over a month prior to the subject transaction of September 2, 2024. The registration documents list a residential address, which was identified as a short-term rental property through public listings. The registered agent is an individual with no identifiable footprint in commercial databases, and the stated purpose of the LLC is generalized management consulting. The rapid succession from entity formation to receipt of a multi-million-dollar wire transfer is a recognized indicator of a potential shell entity established specifically to receive illicit funds.

The receiving institution provided limited transactional history for Harborview Management LLC upon request. The account was opened on July 30, 2024, five days after the entity's registration. From account opening until the receipt of the subject wire, the account exhibited minimal activity, consisting of low-value deposits and debits consistent with account maintenance and initial funding. This dormant period followed by a sudden, large-value incoming transfer is atypical for an active management consulting firm. The receiving institution reported that the incoming wire of $3,863,579.20 was the first significant credit to the account.

Following the credit on September 2, 2024, the Harborview Management LLC account exhibited rapid onward movement of funds. Within forty-eight hours, the entirety of the funds, less the $1,081,802.18 subsequently frozen by the receiving institution, was disbursed. These disbursements were executed via multiple outbound wire transfers to various domestic and international beneficiaries. The receiving institution indicated that these beneficiaries appeared to be unrelated to the stated business purpose of Harborview Management LLC. The swift dissipation of funds in this manner is characteristic of money laundering typologies designed to obfuscate the origin and destination of illicit proceeds.

Analysis of the counterparty, Westmarch Distribution Inc., and its intended payee, Saltmarsh Produce Corp., further highlights the anomalies surrounding Harborview Management LLC. Westmarch Distribution Inc. has a long-standing vendor relationship with Saltmarsh Produce Corp., characterized by regular, predictable payments for agricultural commodities. The invoiced amount of $3,863,579.20 aligns with the historical volume of trade between the two entities. However, the payment instructions directing funds to Harborview Management LLC instead of Saltmarsh Produce Corp. represent a significant deviation from established payment patterns.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The investigation into the outbound wire transfer of $3,863,579.20 from the Westmarch Distribution Inc. account 74-98263-1 relied on a review of communication logs, transaction records, and interviews with bank personnel and the customer. The reviewing analyst examined authentication logs for the customer’s online banking portal for the period of July 2, 2024, through October 29, 2024. These logs indicated that the funds transfer request was initiated using the credentials of the Westmarch Distribution Inc. controller. The IP address associated with this login session resolved to a location consistent with the customer’s usual access patterns, suggesting the credentials were not compromised through remote unauthorized access.

The relationship manager for Westmarch Distribution Inc. was interviewed regarding the customer's typical wire activity. The relationship manager stated that while Westmarch Distribution Inc. frequently remits high-value payments to suppliers, including Saltmarsh Produce Corp., the volume and beneficiary of the $3,863,579.20 transfer were atypical. The relationship manager noted that the customer typically remits payments in the mid-six-figure range. The relationship manager also confirmed that Harborview Management LLC was not a known vendor or counterparty for Westmarch Distribution Inc. based on historical transaction data and prior discussions with the customer.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated recovery efforts immediately upon receiving Westmarch Distribution Inc.'s notification that the outbound wire transfer was fraudulent. A formal SWIFT MT192 request for cancellation was transmitted to the receiving institution on October 7, 2024, citing suspected fraud. Concurrently, a hold harmless letter was transmitted to the receiving institution’s fraud department via secure channels, indemnifying them against claims arising from the return of the funds. The reviewing analyst noted that the initial communication from the receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the indemnity agreement and indicated an investigation was underway.

The receiving institution subsequently confirmed that a portion of the funds had been secured. A freeze was placed on the beneficiary account held in the name of Vantage Point Trading Inc. However, the receiving institution advised that significant dissipation of funds had occurred prior to the receipt of the Cortex Bank and Trust cancellation request. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was confirmed to be $1,081,802.18. The receiving institution stated that the remaining balance of the transfer had been subsequently wired out to secondary beneficiaries, notably Harborview Management LLC, and that those funds were no longer under their control.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Westmarch Distribution Inc. was the victim of a business email compromise resulting in a fraudulent funds transfer. Review of the customer's communications with their vendor indicated that the payment instructions were received from a lookalike domain differing from the legitimate vendor's domain by a single character. The fraudulent emails contained urgency language that successfully circumvented the customer's internal dual-approval control for outgoing wires. The resulting funds transfer was initiated minutes before the bank's wire cutoff time on October 25, 2024. The investigation determined that $3,863,579.20 was diverted to a beneficiary account held in the name of Saltmarsh Produce Corp., an entity with no prior relationship to Westmarch Distribution Inc. The beneficiary name did not match the vendor identified on the compromised invoice. Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request with the receiving institution upon discovery of the fraud. A portion of the funds was successfully frozen at the receiving institution, leaving a residual loss to the customer. Due to the ongoing recovery efforts and the involvement of law enforcement, the disposition of this investigation remains ongoing.

body:
## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2409
Date opened: September 20, 2024
Subject: Magnus Hallstrom (individual), account 34-49696-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: closed_no_action

## Case Summary

On September 13, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit opened internal reference FIU-WIRE-2409, a high risk tier investigation. The matter was referred by a relationship manager in the commercial banking division following a customer inquiry regarding an unpaid vendor invoice. The customer, Magnus Hallstrom, holds Cortex Bank and Trust commercial checking account 34-49696-1. The relationship manager reported that the customer contacted the bank after an intended vendor, Cardinal Textiles LLC, stated they had not received a payment the customer believed was remitted. The investigation was initiated to review a specific outbound wire transfer and determine if the funds were induced from the customer account by deception.

The investigation focused on an August 13, 2024, wire transfer from account 34-49696-1 in the amount of $377,393.20. The customer indicated this transfer was intended to settle an invoice from Cardinal Textiles LLC. Initial review of the wire details established that the beneficiary name on the transfer instructions was Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. The customer asserted they had no business relationship with Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC and had not intended to remit funds to that entity. The primary objective of the investigation was to determine the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the transfer and to assess whether the activity was consistent with a business email compromise or similar wire fraud typology.

The review period for this investigation was defined as May 21, 2024, through September 19, 2024. This period was selected to encompass the transaction in question and to allow for a review of prior account activity for context. The investigation sought to establish how the transfer instructions were received, verified, and executed. The reviewing analyst examined the communication channels utilized by the customer to initiate the transfer and the internal controls applied by Cortex Bank and Trust prior to execution.

The relationship manager provided the initial documentation supplied by the customer, which included copies of email correspondence related to the invoice. The customer indicated that the payment instructions were provided via email, purportedly from a known contact at Cardinal Textiles LLC. The investigation was tasked with reviewing this correspondence to identify any anomalies or indicators of compromise. The initial referral noted that the funds transfer was initiated shortly before the daily wire cutoff time on August 13, 2024.

Following the customer's report, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request to the receiving institution. The investigation reviewed the status of this recall effort. The reviewing analyst noted that a portion of the funds, $105,670.10, was successfully frozen at the receiving institution. The investigation was required to determine the disposition of the remaining funds and the resulting residual loss to the customer, calculated at $271,723.10. The analysis focused on whether the activity observed during the review period presented sufficient evidence to file a Suspicious Activity Report regarding the suspected diversion of $377,393.20. The investigation sought to establish a timeline of events leading up to the transfer and to evaluate the information provided by the customer against the transaction records and communication logs available to the bank. The review also considered the relationship, if any, between the customer and the counterparty entities identified in the referral, including Glenhaven Management Partners LP, which was mentioned in the initial customer inquiry.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The Financial Intelligence Unit of Cortex Bank and Trust commenced an investigation on September 13, 2024, following a referral from the commercial banking relationship manager assigned to Magnus Hallstrom. The referral alleged that a fraudulent outbound wire transfer in the amount of $377,393.20 was authorized by Magnus Hallstrom and transmitted from Cortex Bank and Trust account 34-49696-1 under false pretenses. The relationship manager reported that the customer contacted the bank after the intended payee of an invoice, Cardinal Textiles LLC, contacted the customer regarding an outstanding balance that the customer believed had been settled several days prior.

According to the referral, Magnus Hallstrom stated that the transfer was intended to satisfy an invoice for materials and fabrication services. The customer reported that the authorization for the payment was prompted by an email purportedly originating from a known contact at Cardinal Textiles LLC. This email contained revised payment instructions, directing funds to an account held by Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. The customer indicated that the email emphasized the urgency of the payment, claiming that failure to remit the funds immediately would result in the cancellation of an upcoming shipment critical to the customer’s business operations. 

The relationship manager’s initial review of the correspondence provided by the customer revealed that the sender's email address utilized a domain name that was visually similar to the legitimate domain of Cardinal Textiles LLC, differing by a single character. The customer, operating under the belief that the communication and the revised instructions were authentic, initiated the wire transfer to Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC in the amount of $377,393.20. The transfer was executed by Cortex Bank and Trust in accordance with the customer's authorization.

Upon being notified by Cardinal Textiles LLC that the payment had not been received, the customer reviewed the transaction details and identified the discrepancy in the beneficiary name and the email domain. The customer subsequently contacted the relationship manager to report the suspected fraud and request assistance in recovering the funds. The relationship manager immediately escalated the matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit for review and potential action.

The referral further noted that the customer had circumvented internal dual-approval controls when initiating the transfer. The customer stated that the urgency conveyed in the fraudulent email led to a decision to bypass standard procedures to ensure the payment was processed before the close of business. The transfer request was submitted to Cortex Bank and Trust shortly before the daily wire cutoff time, which expedited processing and limited the opportunity for internal review prior to transmission. 

The initial allegation centers on a business email compromise scheme, wherein the customer was induced by deceptive communication to remit funds to an unauthorized beneficiary. The reviewing analyst noted that the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the transfer, specifically the use of a lookalike domain, the application of urgency to circumvent established controls, and the timing of the request, are consistent with common methodologies employed in such schemes. 

The Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a review to determine the extent of the suspected fraud, trace the disposition of the transmitted funds, and assess whether the activity warranted the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report. The investigation sought to verify the details provided in the referral, analyze the transaction history of account 34-49696-1, and evaluate the communication between the customer and the purported vendor. The focus of the inquiry was the single outbound wire transfer of $377,393.20 and the events immediately preceding its authorization.

## Timeline of Events

On August 13, 2024, the relationship manager for the Magnus Hallstrom account received an email seemingly from the customer's established contact at Cardinal Textiles LLC. The sender domain closely resembled the legitimate domain of Cardinal Textiles LLC, differing by a single character. The communication contained wire transfer instructions and requested urgent processing for an invoice. The email stated that immediate payment was necessary to secure a critical shipment of materials and requested that the usual dual-approval control process be bypassed due to the time sensitivity.

The relationship manager, acting on the perceived urgency, initiated the funds transfer without seeking the required secondary approval. The transfer was executed at 4:55 PM, minutes before the bank's daily wire cutoff time. The beneficiary named in the transfer instructions was Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC, an entity with no prior association with the customer or Cardinal Textiles LLC, and not the invoicing vendor. The amount of the outbound wire transfer was $377,393.20.

On August 19, 2024, Magnus Hallstrom contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report a discrepancy in his account balance. He stated that he had not authorized the transfer to Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC and had not received any communication from Cardinal Textiles LLC regarding an urgent payment. The customer confirmed that Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC was not a known vendor or counterparty.

Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated an investigation into the reported unauthorized transaction. The reviewing analyst examined the email communication received on August 13, 2024, and identified the deceptive sender domain. A review of the account history confirmed that no previous transactions had involved Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. The investigation also revealed that the relationship manager had bypassed the dual-approval control procedure based on the urgency language in the fraudulent email.

On August 19, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution to request a recall of the funds. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the wire transfer but indicated that the funds had been rapidly depleted from the Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC account. The receiving institution was able to freeze a remaining balance of $105,670.10.

The investigation established that the entire outbound wire amount of $377,393.20 had been diverted as a result of the fraudulent instructions. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $105,670.10. The residual loss to the customer, representing the unrecovered portion of the wire transfer, was $271,723.10.

A review of the customer's account activity prior to the incident revealed no suspicious patterns or transactions indicative of compromise. The account had maintained a consistent balance, with regular inbound transfers from Glenhaven Management Partners LP and routine outbound payments to established vendors, including Cardinal Textiles LLC. The review period for the investigation, encompassing May 21, 2024, through September 19, 2024, did not identify any further unauthorized activity.

The investigation confirmed that the funds transfer on August 13, 2024, was induced by deception and directed to an unintended beneficiary. The use of a lookalike domain, urgency language to override established controls, and a beneficiary name differing from the invoicing vendor are consistent with a business email compromise scheme resulting in wire fraud. The investigation concluded that the customer, Magnus Hallstrom, was the victim of the fraud and had not participated in the illicit activity. Cortex Bank and Trust implemented enhanced security measures, including mandatory secondary verification for all wire transfer requests exceeding the regulatory threshold for suspicious activity reporting, to mitigate the risk of similar incidents. The customer was advised on recognizing deceptive email communications and the importance of verifying payment instructions through independent channels.

## Funds Tracing

The funds tracing effort in this matter centered on tracking the disposition of the $377,393.20 wire transfer initiated from Cortex Bank and Trust account 34-49696-1, held by Magnus Hallstrom. This transfer, executed on September 13, 2024, was directed to a commercial account held at a domestic financial institution under the name Glenhaven Management Partners LP. The investigation established that this transfer represented a diversion of funds intended for Cardinal Textiles LLC.

Upon determining the fraudulent nature of the September 13, 2024 transfer, the reviewing analyst initiated an immediate recall request and contact with the receiving institution. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the $377,393.20 wire transfer into the Glenhaven Management Partners LP account on the same day. However, the receiving institution reported that the majority of the funds had already been disbursed prior to their receipt of the recall request.

Information provided by the receiving institution indicated that the funds were rapidly dissipated through a series of subsequent transfers. A significant portion of the funds was transferred out of the Glenhaven Management Partners LP account almost immediately upon receipt. While Cortex Bank and Trust does not have direct visibility into the onward movement of funds from the Glenhaven Management Partners LP account, the receiving institution disclosed that these subsequent transfers were directed to multiple accounts at various domestic and international institutions. The speed of the disbursements is consistent with efforts to obfuscate the trail of the funds and complicate recovery efforts.

The investigation determined that the receiving institution was able to freeze a portion of the funds remaining in the Glenhaven Management Partners LP account. The amount successfully frozen was $105,670.10. These funds are currently held by the receiving institution pending further legal or regulatory action. The recovery of this portion of the diverted funds is contingent upon the outcome of those proceedings and is not guaranteed.

The rapid disbursement of the funds from the Glenhaven Management Partners LP account, coupled with the lack of direct visibility into the subsequent transfers, significantly hinders efforts to trace the ultimate disposition of the remaining balance. The residual loss to Magnus Hallstrom, representing the difference between the total wire amount and the frozen funds, is $271,723.10. The investigation infers that these funds have likely been converted into untraceable assets or moved beyond the reach of standard recovery mechanisms.

The tracing effort also reviewed activity in Cortex Bank and Trust account 34-49696-1 preceding the September 13, 2024 transfer. The account exhibited a pattern of routine business transactions consistent with the customer's stated profile. However, the investigation noted earlier transactions involving Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. For example, a transfer occurred on August 19, 2024. While these earlier transactions did not exhibit the same indicators of compromise as the September 13, 2024 transfer, they are noted as part of the overall account history. The investigation did not identify any direct link between these earlier transactions and the diversion of funds to Glenhaven Management Partners LP.

The funds tracing effort is effectively concluded, as the trail of the remaining $271,723.10 ends at the receiving institution. The rapid onward movement of funds and the use of an entity name that did not match the invoicing vendor are consistent with established patterns of wire fraud. The investigation relies on the information provided by the receiving institution regarding the disposition of the funds from the Glenhaven Management Partners LP account, as Cortex Bank and Trust has no direct means of independently verifying the subsequent transfers. The tracing effort highlights the challenges in recovering funds once they have been transferred to external accounts and rapidly disbursed.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The recipient of the outbound transfer was identified as Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. A review of the wire transfer instructions indicated that the beneficiary account was held at a regional financial institution located in the same state as Cortex Bank and Trust. The business name provided in the wire instructions did not align with the historical invoicing vendor, Cardinal Textiles LLC, with whom Magnus Hallstrom had established a long-term commercial relationship. 

The investigation examined public records and corporate registries to ascertain the nature of Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. The entity was registered as a limited liability company on May 21, 2024. The stated business purpose in the registry filings described operations in specialized metal fabrication and industrial supply. The timing of the entity's formation, occurring shortly before the events under review, was noted. Further public record searches yielded limited operational history or commercial presence for Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. The registered address was identified as a commercial mail receiving agency rather than a physical manufacturing facility or office space.

The reviewing analyst examined the flow of funds into and out of the Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC account, to the extent visible through the receiving institution's cooperation. The account received the transfer of $377,393.20 on September 13, 2024. Prior to this credit, the account exhibited minimal activity, characterized by low-value, even-dollar transfers that appeared consistent with account testing or maintenance. The sudden influx of a significant sum represented a marked deviation from the account's established baseline.

Following the receipt of the $377,393.20 credit, rapid outbound movement of funds was observed. The receiving institution reported that a significant portion of the funds was transferred out via multiple electronic payments and smaller wire transfers to unidentifiable third parties within hours of the initial credit. The speed of these subsequent transfers is consistent with attempts to dissipate funds rapidly, complicating recovery efforts. 

The investigation also reviewed the role of Glenhaven Management Partners LP, an entity that appeared in the communication chain leading up to the transfer. Glenhaven Management Partners LP was referenced as a supposed intermediary facilitating a new supply chain arrangement. However, independent verification of Glenhaven Management Partners LP revealed discrepancies. The domain name used in the email communications purportedly from this entity was a lookalike domain, differing by a single character from a known, legitimate financial services firm. 

The communications directing the payment to Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC, rather than the expected vendor, Cardinal Textiles LLC, utilized urgency language. The correspondence emphasized critical supply chain disruptions and impending deadlines, attempting to justify the deviation from established payment protocols. This language was cited as the reason for bypassing the customer's internal dual-approval control for wire transfers. The transfer itself was initiated minutes before the daily wire cutoff time on September 13, 2024. 

The receiving institution was contacted promptly upon discovery of the suspected fraud. Through collaborative efforts, the receiving institution was able to freeze a portion of the funds remaining in the Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC account. The amount secured was $105,670.10. Despite these efforts, the rapid dissipation of funds prior to the freeze resulted in a significant unrecovered amount. The residual loss associated with this transfer was calculated at $271,723.10. 

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

During the review period of May 21, 2024 through September 19, 2024, the investigation gathered documentary evidence and conducted interviews to establish the circumstances surrounding the $377,393.20 wire transfer initiated from the account of Magnus Hallstrom. On September 13, 2024, the relationship manager met with Magnus Hallstrom to review the communication history leading up to the transfer. Magnus Hallstrom provided copies of emails purportedly received from Cardinal Textiles LLC, a vendor he stated he had previously paid by check. The reviewing analyst examined the email headers and determined that the sender's domain, which appeared to be the vendor's legitimate domain, contained a single-character substitution, indicating a lookalike domain was used to deceive the customer. The analyst noted that the email communication was consistent with a business email compromise scheme.

The emails provided by Magnus Hallstrom contained instructions to wire the $377,393.20 payment to a new beneficiary, Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. The investigation reviewed the invoice attached to the fraudulent email. The invoice appeared to be a modified version of a legitimate invoice previously issued by Cardinal Textiles LLC, but the payment instructions had been altered to direct funds to Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. The reviewing analyst confirmed that the beneficiary name on the wire instructions did not match the invoicing vendor, Cardinal Textiles LLC.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Upon determining that the outbound funds transfer from the account of Magnus Hallstrom on May 31, 2024 was fraudulently induced, the investigating analyst initiated a formal recall request via the Fedwire system. The request, transmitted within two hours of the initial detection, cited suspected fraud and demanded the return of the full transferred amount of $377,393.20. Concurrently, a hold harmless indemnification agreement was drafted and executed by an authorized officer of Cortex Bank and Trust. This agreement was forwarded directly to the receiving financial institution’s wire operations department, providing the necessary legal assurance that Cortex Bank and Trust would indemnify the receiving institution against any claims arising from the return of the funds. The indemnification request detailed the nature of the suspected compromise, specifically identifying the lookalike sender domain utilized to deceive the customer into overriding internal controls.

The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the recall request and the indemnification agreement later that same business day. In their initial response, they indicated that a freeze had been placed on the beneficiary account associated with Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC. However, they also noted that a significant portion of the funds had already been disbursed prior to the receipt of the recall notice. The receiving institution’s fraud operations unit confirmed that they were conducting a concurrent investigation and would provide updates regarding the exact amount secured. The swift disbursement of funds is consistent with established typologies for wire fraud, where perpetrators rapidly move illicitly acquired funds to secondary or tertiary accounts to frustrate recovery efforts.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Magnus Hallstrom, acting on instructions he believed to be from Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC, initiated a wire transfer out of Cortex Bank and Trust account 34-49696-1 to Cardinal Textiles LLC on September 13, 2024. The transfer was preceded by an email exchange on September 12, 2024, in which an individual purporting to be a Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC representative directed payment to a new beneficiary account. The sender domain in the email differed from the known Kestrel Fabrication Group LLC domain by one character. The reviewing analyst determined that the $377,393.20 transfer was induced by deception, as the beneficiary name did not match the invoicing vendor and the transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff. The customer was unable to substantiate the legitimacy of the instructions. The investigation concluded that the funds were diverted to an unauthorized beneficiary. The reviewing analyst noted that a portion of the funds was frozen at the receiving institution, resulting in a residual loss to the customer. As the customer acknowledged the fraudulent nature of the instructions and the bank's investigation confirmed the diversion, the case was closed without further action.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2410
Date opened: September 3, 2024
Subject: Solveig Petrosyan (individual), account 62-88291-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: referred_to_fincen

## Case Summary

The Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a review of Cortex Bank and Trust customer Solveig Petrosyan on May 21, 2024, following an escalation from the wire operations department. The escalation detailed a customer inquiry regarding an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $143,940.24, which debited the customer's primary operating account, ending in 291-1. The customer reported that the transfer, initiated on May 20, 2024, was directed to a beneficiary she did not intend to pay, following the receipt of instructions she believed to be from a known vendor.

The investigation was tasked with determining the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire transfer, assessing the potential that the customer was the victim of a business email compromise or similar scheme, and evaluating whether the activity warranted a filing with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. The investigation sought to establish the sequence of events leading up to the transfer, the nature of the communication that prompted the customer to initiate the payment, and the disposition of the funds after leaving Cortex Bank and Trust.

Initial review of the escalation indicated that the customer, acting as the authorized signer on the account, contacted the branch on May 21, 2024, to inquire about the status of the transfer. The customer stated that she had received a follow-up communication from the legitimate vendor, Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., indicating that payment for an outstanding invoice had not been received. The customer then reviewed the wire transfer details and realized the funds were not sent to the vendor's known banking details.

The wire operations department provided the payment instructions supplied by the customer for the May 20, 2024 transfer. The instructions directed the $143,940.24 to a beneficiary named Millpond Distribution Corp., an entity not previously associated with the customer's account profile or historical payment activity. The instructions were reportedly received via email, which the customer provided to the branch manager during her inquiry.

Preliminary analysis of the provided email correspondence suggested a potential compromise of the vendor's communication channels. The email directing the payment to Millpond Distribution Corp. appeared to originate from a domain that closely resembled the known domain of Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., but differed by a single character. This lookalike domain is a common indicator of a potential business email compromise scheme, wherein a malicious actor intercepts or spoofs communications to misdirect funds.

Furthermore, the email communication contained language emphasizing the urgency of the payment, which the customer cited as the reason for expediting the wire transfer process. This urgency language, combined with the request to bypass established dual-approval controls for the account, presented an additional indicator consistent with fraudulent inducement. The wire transfer was initiated late in the day, shortly before the bank's wire cutoff time, which is frequently observed in attempts to limit the window for detecting and halting fraudulent transactions.

Upon receipt of the escalation on May 21, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit immediately initiated a recall request through the wire network to the receiving institution. The initial objective was to attempt recovery of the $143,940.24 before the funds could be further dissipated. The investigation then proceeded to gather all available documentation, including the customer's account agreements, historical transaction data, and the complete chain of communication leading to the May 20, 2024 wire transfer. The focus of the review period was established as May 6, 2024 through August 22, 2024, encompassing the timeframe of the communications and the subsequent investigation and recovery efforts. The primary question remained whether the customer was the victim of a third-party fraud and, if so, the mechanisms employed to execute the scheme.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The investigation was initiated on May 28, 2024, following an escalation from the commercial banking relationship manager assigned to Solveig Petrosyan. The customer contacted the relationship manager to report a suspected fraud event concerning an outbound wire transfer executed on May 27, 2024. The relationship manager submitted an internal referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit, alleging that Solveig Petrosyan was the victim of a business email compromise scheme that resulted in the unauthorized diversion of corporate funds.

According to the referral, Solveig Petrosyan intended to remit a mid six-figure payment to a known vendor, Mapleford Holdings Partners LP, to settle an outstanding invoice for specialized industrial equipment. The customer stated that instructions for the payment were received via email from an individual purporting to be the regular accounts receivable contact at Mapleford Holdings Partners LP. The referring relationship manager indicated that the email communication contained revised wiring instructions, directing the payment to an account held by a previously unknown entity, Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., at an external financial institution.

The customer further alleged to the relationship manager that the email directing the change in payment details contained language stressing the urgency of the remittance, citing impending supply chain disruptions if the invoice was not settled immediately. The relationship manager’s referral noted that this urgency language appeared to have influenced the customer’s internal authorization process, leading to the circumvention of established dual-approval controls for outgoing wire transfers.

The internal referral documented that the customer executed a wire transfer in the amount of $143,940.24 on May 27, 2024. The customer reported to the relationship manager that the transfer was initiated shortly before the daily wire cutoff time, a detail confirmed by the referring party upon review of the transaction logs. The relationship manager stated that the customer became aware of the potential fraud on May 28, 2024, when the genuine vendor, Mapleford Holdings Partners LP, contacted Solveig Petrosyan to inquire about the status of the unpaid invoice.

Upon realization of the suspected deception, the customer immediately notified Cortex Bank and Trust. The relationship manager’s escalation detailed the customer’s assertion that the payment was induced by fraudulent misrepresentation and that the beneficiary, Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., was not the intended recipient of the funds. The referral requested an immediate investigation by the Financial Intelligence Unit to determine the circumstances surrounding the transaction and to initiate any possible recovery efforts.

The initial review of the referral by the assigned analyst confirmed the execution of the $143,940.24 wire transfer on the specified date. The analyst also verified the customer's claim regarding the timing of the transfer initiation relative to the daily cutoff. The escalation from the relationship manager formed the basis for the subsequent investigation into the suspected wire fraud, focusing on the communication channels used to transmit the altered payment instructions and the characteristics of the beneficiary entity, Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. The allegation centered on the premise that the customer was deceived into authorizing a payment to a fraudulent counterparty through the manipulation of email communications and the exploitation of perceived urgency, resulting in the diversion of funds intended for a legitimate business partner.

## Timeline of Events

The investigation established that the sequence of events leading to the loss began on May 6, 2024. On this date, Cortex Bank and Trust customer Solveig Petrosyan received an email regarding an outstanding invoice. The communication appeared to originate from a known vendor, Millpond Distribution Corp. However, the reviewing analyst noted that the sender's email domain contained a subtle typographical error, substituting a single character from the legitimate domain name used by Millpond Distribution Corp. in previous, verified correspondence. The email directed that payment for an upcoming shipment of goods be routed to a new beneficiary account.

On May 20, 2024, the customer received a follow-up email from the same deceptive domain. This communication included language stressing urgency, claiming that the shipment would be delayed if payment was not received immediately. The investigation found that this pressure tactic influenced the customer's handling of the transaction. Cortex Bank and Trust records indicate that on the same day, Solveig Petrosyan initiated an outbound wire transfer. The transfer instruction was submitted shortly before the bank's established daily cutoff time for processing outgoing wires. The wire transfer, in the amount of $143,940.24, was directed to a beneficiary listed as Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. The beneficiary name provided in the wire instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Millpond Distribution Corp. Despite this discrepancy, the transfer was processed.

The following day, May 21, 2024, the customer contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report a suspected fraud. The customer indicated that they had spoken with a representative of Millpond Distribution Corp. and confirmed that the vendor had not sent the revised payment instructions and had not received the funds. The customer stated they had not intended to remit payment to Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. Based on this information, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request to the receiving institution.

On May 23, 2024, the receiving institution responded to the recall request. The response indicated that a portion of the transferred funds had been secured. Specifically, $46,060.88 was frozen in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution also communicated that the remaining balance of the transferred funds had already been withdrawn or transferred outward prior to the receipt of the recall request.

The investigation noted further developments related to the parties involved. On May 27, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received a general inquiry from another financial institution regarding transactions involving Mapleford Holdings Partners LP. While this inquiry did not specifically reference the wire transfer initiated by Solveig Petrosyan, a review of the customer's account history revealed prior, legitimate transactions with Mapleford Holdings Partners LP. The analyst reviewed these historical transactions but found no direct connection to the fraudulent wire transfer directed to Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd.

On May 28, 2024, the funds that had been successfully frozen by the receiving institution were returned to Cortex Bank and Trust and subsequently credited back to the customer's account. The return of these funds mitigated a portion of the customer's loss. However, the customer sustained a residual loss of $97,879.36, representing the unrecovered portion of the initial wire transfer.

Subsequent monitoring of the customer's account activity through the remainder of the review period showed no further unauthorized or suspicious transactions. A review conducted on June 11, 2024, confirmed that the customer had implemented enhanced security measures for their email communications. A later review on July 12, 2024, verified that the customer had updated their internal procedures for verifying changes to vendor payment instructions. A final review of the account activity on July 26, 2024, identified no further anomalies or deviations from the customer's expected transactional profile. The timeline of events demonstrates a successful deception that induced the customer to initiate a wire transfer to an unintended beneficiary.

## Funds Tracing

The investigation established that on May 21, 2024, a funds transfer was initiated from the Cortex Bank and Trust checking account ending in 88291-1 held by Solveig Petrosyan. The transfer was instructed in the amount of $143,940.24. The beneficiary named in the payment instructions was Mapleford Holdings Partners LP. Cortex Bank and Trust records confirm the outgoing wire transfer was processed and settled to the receiving institution later that same day.

Analysis of the transfer details revealed that the beneficiary name Mapleford Holdings Partners LP did not correspond to the entity that had ostensibly issued the invoice to Solveig Petrosyan. The invoice provided by the customer during the inquiry process identified Millpond Distribution Corp. as the vendor to whom the payment was owed. This discrepancy is consistent with a compromised communication channel where payment instructions were altered to direct funds to a third party. Review of the email communication that prompted the transfer instruction showed the sender domain closely resembled the legitimate domain of Millpond Distribution Corp., differing by only one character.

The initial destination of the $143,940.24 was an account at a US correspondent bank, acting as the receiving depository financial institution on behalf of Mapleford Holdings Partners LP. Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a request for return of funds through the wire network on May 23, 2024, citing suspected fraud. The receiving institution acknowledged the request and placed a hold on the beneficiary account on May 27, 2024.

Information subsequently provided by the receiving institution confirmed that $46,060.88 was successfully frozen in the account held by Mapleford Holdings Partners LP. The receiving institution indicated that the remainder of the funds had already been disbursed prior to the hold being placed.

Tracing the onward movement of the disbursed funds relies on information shared by the receiving institution during the recovery attempt. According to their records, on May 28, 2024, a portion of the original wire amount was transferred out of the Mapleford Holdings Partners LP account to an account held by Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. at a different US-based financial institution. The exact amount of this secondary transfer was not disclosed to Cortex Bank and Trust, but it constituted a significant portion of the funds that had not been frozen.

The investigation was unable to determine the final disposition of the funds transferred to Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. Cortex Bank and Trust does not have visibility into the account activity at the subsequent receiving institution. It is inferred that the funds may have been further layered or withdrawn, but no documentation is available to confirm these subsequent hops. The trail of the funds transferred to Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. ends at that institution.

The receiving institution holding the Mapleford Holdings Partners LP account confirmed on June 11, 2024, that the frozen amount of $46,060.88 would be returned to Cortex Bank and Trust. The funds were credited back to the account of Solveig Petrosyan on July 12, 2024. The remaining balance of the original transfer, amounting to $97,879.36, was not recovered. This sum represents the confirmed loss associated with the unauthorized diversion of funds. The investigation concludes that the total amount diverted as a result of the altered payment instructions was $143,940.24, with the final unrecovered amount being $97,879.36.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The investigation focused on the receiving entity, identified in the wire instructions as Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. Research conducted using commercially available public records databases and corporate registries revealed that Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. was formed in the state of incorporation approximately two weeks prior to the transaction date. The registered agent address listed for Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. was a commercial mail receiving agency, and no physical operating location could be identified through open-source research. The stated business purpose for Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., as indicated on the state registry filings, was general consulting. This stated purpose appeared inconsistent with the beneficiary name, which suggested an import business, and with the underlying invoice provided by the customer, which purported to be for industrial equipment. The beneficiary name, Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, which the customer believed to be Mapleford Holdings Partners LP.

Analysis of the receiving account at the beneficiary institution was limited, as the account is not held at Cortex Bank and Trust. However, information obtained through inter-institution communication and standard wire recall procedures provided some insight into the account activity. The receiving account was opened shortly after the corporate formation date of Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., suggesting the account may have been established specifically to receive the funds from Solveig Petrosyan. The account received the single outbound wire of $143,940.24 from Cortex Bank and Trust account 62-88291-1. Following the credit of these funds, the receiving account exhibited rapid depletion. Information provided by the receiving institution indicated that a significant portion of the funds was quickly transferred out via multiple smaller domestic wires to unknown third parties. The pattern of a large, single incoming wire followed by immediate, rapid dissipation is consistent with the layering phase of money laundering and is a common characteristic of accounts used to receive fraudulently obtained funds.

At the time the wire recall was initiated by Cortex Bank and Trust, the receiving institution was able to freeze a portion of the funds remaining in the account. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $46,060.88. The remaining funds had already been transferred out of the account and were unrecoverable, resulting in a residual loss to the customer of $97,879.36. The rapid movement of funds out of the Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. account before the recall could be fully executed highlights the time-sensitive nature of the fraudulent activity and the speed with which the suspected perpetrators attempted to obscure the origin and destination of the diverted funds.

Further review of the counterparties involved in the customer's intended transaction was conducted. The customer, Solveig Petrosyan, believed the payment was intended for Mapleford Holdings Partners LP, a known vendor with whom the customer had a pre-existing business relationship. The customer provided documentation indicating a history of legitimate transactions with Mapleford Holdings Partners LP. The fraudulent wire instructions, however, directed the funds to Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. instead. The customer was unable to substantiate any legitimate business relationship with Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., and no evidence was found to suggest that Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. was affiliated with or authorized to receive payments on behalf of Mapleford Holdings Partners LP.

Additionally, the customer provided communications purportedly from another entity, Millpond Distribution Corp., which appeared to be acting as an intermediary or broker in the intended transaction. The communications from the entity claiming to represent Millpond Distribution Corp. contained the fraudulent wire instructions directing payment to Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. Analysis of the email headers associated with these communications revealed the use of a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the legitimate domain of Millpond Distribution Corp. This deceptive tactic, combined with the urgency language overriding the dual-approval control, facilitated the diversion of the funds to the unintended beneficiary. The discrepancy between the intended vendor, Mapleford Holdings Partners LP, the purported intermediary, Millpond Distribution Corp., and the actual receiving entity, Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., further underscores the deceptive nature of the transaction.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The customer relationship manager was interviewed on July 26, 2024 regarding the circumstances of the wire authorization. The relationship manager indicated that Petrosyan, acting as the authorized signer for Cortex Bank and Trust account 62-88291-1, initiated the transfer request by phone late on May 27, 2024. The relationship manager reported that Petrosyan exhibited significant distress during the call, describing an urgent supplier payment that had to clear before the long weekend. The relationship manager confirmed that the wire was initiated minutes before the daily cutoff, an administrative exception granted due to the customer's tenured relationship with the bank and the stated urgency of the transaction. The relationship manager further noted that Petrosyan bypassed the customary dual-approval control, citing an inability to reach her business partner and the necessity of immediate payment to secure a critical shipment.

Review of the recorded line audio for the May 27, 2024 phone authorization confirmed the relationship manager's account. Petrosyan's voice exhibited stress, and she repeatedly emphasized the time-sensitive nature of the transfer. The audio recording verified that the relationship manager read back the beneficiary details, which Petrosyan confirmed as Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd., an entity the investigation subsequently determined was not the intended payee. The authentication logs for the online banking session associated with the account showed no anomalous access or compromised credentials during the relevant period, indicating the authorization was provided directly by the customer.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Upon identifying the May 28, 2024 outbound wire transfer as potentially unauthorized, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated recovery procedures. A formal SWIFT recall request was transmitted to the receiving institution, citing suspected fraud. The recall request identified the $143,940.24 transfer initiated from the account of Solveig Petrosyan, referencing the beneficiary name Kestrel Imports Holdings Ltd. A hold harmless agreement was proffered to the receiving institution, indemnifying them against claims arising from the return of funds, consistent with standard interbank recovery protocols.

The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the recall request. Initial communication indicated that a freeze order had been placed on the beneficiary account. Subsequent correspondence from the receiving institution's fraud department, dated June 11, 2024, detailed the status of the funds. The receiving institution confirmed that $46,060.88 of the initial transfer remained in the beneficiary account and had been successfully frozen. The communication further detailed that the remaining funds had been dissipated through subsequent transactions prior to the receipt of the recall request.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that a funds transfer was induced by a fraudulent communication. A review of the customer's email system, provided by the customer to the reviewing analyst, indicated that the wire instructions were altered in an email originating from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the customer's established vendor. The fraudulent email contained urgency language intended to override the customer's dual-approval control, and the funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff. The beneficiary name on the transfer did not match the invoicing vendor. The investigation concluded that $143,940.24 was diverted to Mapleford Holdings Partners LP. Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution, which placed a freeze on the remaining funds. The customer was informed of the residual loss. The investigation determined that the activity was consistent with wire fraud. The matter was reviewed by the compliance committee on August 30, 2024. The disposition recorded was referred_to_fincen.
