body:
## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2411
Date opened: April 26, 2024
Subject: Greystone Commodities Group LLC (business), account 76-51297-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: criminal_referral

## Case Summary

On January 25, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a review of a suspected wire fraud incident involving Greystone Commodities Group LLC. The matter was referred by the relationship manager following a customer inquiry regarding an unpaid vendor invoice. Greystone Commodities Group LLC holds commercial operating account 76-51297-1 at Cortex Bank and Trust. The investigation focused on an outgoing domestic wire transfer in the amount of $3,687,955.67, executed on January 16, 2024. The primary objective of the investigation was to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire, determine whether the funds were induced by fraudulent means, and evaluate any potential recovery options. The review period for this investigation spans from January 2, 2024, through May 6, 2024, to encompass the events leading up to the transfer and subsequent recovery efforts.

The referral indicated that Greystone Commodities Group LLC intended the $3,687,955.67 payment to settle a routine invoice from a known supplier, Cornerstone Commodities LLC. However, the customer reported that Cornerstone Commodities LLC had not received the funds, prompting an internal review by the customer's accounts payable department. The customer subsequently contacted Cortex Bank and Trust, alleging that the payment instructions had been manipulated. The investigation sought to verify the customer's claims and identify the actual beneficiary of the funds. The reviewing analyst examined the communication channels and authorization procedures utilized for the January 16, 2024, wire transfer.

Initial analysis of the wire transfer instructions revealed discrepancies between the intended beneficiary, Cornerstone Commodities LLC, and the entity that received the funds. The investigation noted that the receiving account was held by Kestrel Trading Trading Co., an entity with no established business relationship with Greystone Commodities Group LLC. The reviewing analyst investigated the method by which the altered payment instructions were communicated to Greystone Commodities Group LLC's accounts payable department. The investigation explored the possibility of a business email compromise or other deceptive practices that may have influenced the customer's authorization of the transfer.

The investigation also reviewed the internal controls and authorization processes at Greystone Commodities Group LLC to determine how the fraudulent instructions bypassed established procedures. The reviewing analyst assessed whether standard verification protocols were followed prior to the initiation of the wire transfer. Furthermore, the investigation examined the timing of the transfer, noting its proximity to the daily processing cutoff, to determine if urgency was a factor in the execution of the transaction. The objective was to reconstruct the sequence of events that culminated in the unauthorized diversion of funds.

Following the identification of the suspected fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated efforts to trace the funds and coordinate with the receiving institution. The investigation documented the timeline of these recovery efforts, including the issuance of indemnification requests and communications with the beneficiary bank. The reviewing analyst assessed the effectiveness of the initial response and the amount of funds that were successfully secured. The investigation determined that $700,711.58 was frozen at the receiving institution, leaving a substantial residual loss of $2,987,244.09. The investigation sought to analyze the movement of the remaining funds after they credited the account of Kestrel Trading Trading Co., exploring potential connections to other entities, including Mapleford Industrial Supply Inc. The findings of this investigation are detailed in the subsequent sections of this report, culminating in the recorded outcome of a criminal referral.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On February 26, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit was notified by the commercial relationship manager for Greystone Commodities Group LLC regarding a suspected business email compromise. The relationship manager reported that an authorized signer for the customer had contacted the branch earlier that day to report a fraudulent outbound wire transfer. The customer alleged that a wire in the amount of $3,687,955.67 had been induced by deception and sent to a beneficiary not intended by the company. The relationship manager submitted an internal referral form outlining the customer’s claim and initiated a wire recall request through the payments operations department.

The customer stated that the wire, executed on February 19, 2024, was intended to settle an outstanding invoice with a known vendor, Cornerstone Commodities LLC. According to the referral, the customer’s accounts payable department received an email on February 13, 2024, purportedly from their regular contact at Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The email contained revised payment instructions, directing funds to a new beneficiary account held at a different financial institution. The customer alleged that the email appeared legitimate and contained an invoice matching the expected amount for a recent delivery of materials.

The referral indicated that the customer only discovered the suspected fraud on February 26, 2024, when the genuine vendor, Cornerstone Commodities LLC, inquired about the past-due invoice. Upon reviewing the email communication, the customer identified that the sender’s domain name differed from the legitimate vendor’s domain by a single character. The customer asserted that the funds were diverted to an unauthorized beneficiary as a result of this deceptive communication.

Following the receipt of the internal referral, the reviewing analyst examined the wire transfer records for the Greystone Commodities Group LLC account. The records confirmed an outbound wire of $3,687,955.67 on February 19, 2024. The beneficiary named on the wire transfer was Kestrel Trading Co. The analyst noted that the beneficiary name did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Cornerstone Commodities LLC, as claimed by the customer in their report to the relationship manager.

The analyst reviewed the communication provided by the customer in support of their claim. The email, dated February 13, 2024, requested expedited payment and urged the customer to bypass their standard dual-approval process for vendor payments to ensure timely processing of the invoice. The email emphasized the necessity of immediate settlement to avoid disruptions in future supply shipments. The analyst observed that the wire transfer was initiated late in the business day on February 19, 2024, occurring just minutes before the bank's established wire cutoff time.

The payments operations department, acting on the wire recall request initiated by the relationship manager, contacted the receiving institution to attempt recovery of the funds. The receiving institution responded to the recall notice on March 4, 2024. They confirmed receipt of the wire and indicated that a portion of the funds had already been withdrawn or transferred from the beneficiary account. The receiving institution stated that they were able to secure a remaining balance in the Kestrel Trading Co. account.

The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $700,711.58. The receiving institution advised Cortex Bank and Trust that they would initiate the process to return the secured funds, pending receipt of a formal hold harmless agreement. The relationship manager communicated this development to the customer, advising them of the partial recovery and the pending return of the frozen funds. The remaining unrecovered balance represented a residual loss to the customer.

The Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a formal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the wire transfer based on the internal referral and the customer's allegation of business email compromise. The investigation focused on reviewing the transactional activity within the Greystone Commodities Group LLC account during the review period to determine if the activity was consistent with the reported fraud and to assess the potential involvement of the named counterparties.

## Timeline of Events

The sequence of events leading to the loss began on January 8, 2024. On this date, an email was received by an accounts payable clerk at Greystone Commodities Group LLC. The email purported to be from a known vendor, Kestrel Trading Trading Co. The sender address, however, utilized a domain name that differed from the legitimate domain by a single character. This email contained revised payment instructions for an outstanding invoice, directing future payments to a new bank account. The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary name on the revised instructions, Cornerstone Commodities LLC, did not match the name of the invoicing vendor.

Between January 8, 2024, and January 15, 2024, internal communications at Greystone Commodities Group LLC indicated that the accounts payable clerk updated the vendor payment profile with the new banking details. No secondary verification call to Kestrel Trading Trading Co. was evident in the records provided to Cortex Bank and Trust.

On January 16, 2024, a second email was received from the fraudulent sender. This communication requested expedited payment of a large, purportedly overdue invoice, utilizing language that emphasized urgency. The email stressed the need for immediate settlement to avoid disruption in the supply chain. This urgency language appeared designed to circumvent the customer's established dual-approval controls for large disbursements.

Later on January 16, 2024, at approximately 4:15 PM Eastern Standard Time, a wire transfer request was initiated by Greystone Commodities Group LLC through the Cortex Bank and Trust online banking portal. The request was for $3,687,955.67, with the beneficiary designated as Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The timing of this request was notable, occurring minutes before the daily wire processing cutoff time. The transaction was processed and the funds were transmitted to the receiving institution.

The diversion of funds was not immediately recognized. On January 25, 2024, Greystone Commodities Group LLC was contacted by the legitimate vendor, Kestrel Trading Trading Co., inquiring about the status of the unpaid invoice. This contact prompted an internal review by Greystone Commodities Group LLC, which revealed that the payment had been sent to the account specified in the fraudulent January 8, 2024 email.

Greystone Commodities Group LLC notified Cortex Bank and Trust of the suspected fraud on January 25, 2024. The relationship manager immediately escalated the matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit. Upon receipt of the notification, the reviewing analyst initiated a recall request through the wire transfer system, attempting to recover the $3,687,955.67.

Communication with the receiving institution over the subsequent days confirmed that the majority of the funds had already been disbursed from the beneficiary account. The receiving institution reported on February 13, 2024, that they were able to secure a remaining balance in the account. The sum frozen at the receiving institution was $700,711.58. The remaining balance, representing the residual loss to the customer, was $2,987,244.09.

Following the confirmation of the partial recovery, the Financial Intelligence Unit continued its review of the customer's account activity to determine if any other suspicious transactions had occurred. The review encompassed the period from January 2, 2024, through May 6, 2024. No further unauthorized transactions or related suspicious activity involving Cornerstone Commodities LLC or Mapleford Industrial Supply Inc. were identified during this review period. The investigation established that the initial diversion on January 16, 2024, was an isolated event within the customer's account history. The reviewing analyst compiled the findings and the timeline into the final case file for further review.

## Funds Tracing

The funds movement was initiated by a debit to the Cortex Bank and Trust checking account ending in 76-51297-1 held by Greystone Commodities Group LLC. This outgoing domestic wire transfer occurred on January 16, 2024. The amount transferred was $3,687,955.67. The instruction directed the funds to a beneficiary account held in the name of Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The beneficiary institution was identified as a large national bank headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. This initial hop is fully documented within Cortex Bank and Trust's wire transfer systems and confirmed by the receiving institution's acknowledgement.

Subsequent tracing efforts relied on information obtained from the beneficiary institution through collaborative inquiries following the report of suspected fraud. The beneficiary institution confirmed receipt of the $3,687,955.67 on January 16, 2024, crediting the account associated with Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The beneficiary institution's records indicate that the funds did not remain in the receiving account for an extended period.

On January 18, 2024, a significant portion of the funds was transferred outbound from the Cornerstone Commodities LLC account. The beneficiary institution reported a wire transfer of a low seven-figure sum to an account held by Kestrel Trading Trading Co. at a regional bank in the Midwest. The exact amount of this secondary transfer is not documented within Cortex Bank and Trust's records, but the beneficiary institution characterized it as representing the majority of the initial deposit. This hop is documented by the beneficiary institution's internal records and their communication with Cortex Bank and Trust.

The beneficiary institution also reported additional outbound activity from the Cornerstone Commodities LLC account. On January 25, 2024, another wire transfer was initiated, directing a mid six-figure sum to an account held by Mapleford Industrial Supply Inc. at a different national bank. As with the previous onward transfer, the specific dollar amount is not documented in Cortex Bank and Trust's systems, but the movement was confirmed by the beneficiary institution. The trail for these funds ends at the receiving institution for Mapleford Industrial Supply Inc., as further onward tracing was not possible based on the information provided. It is inferred that these funds were disbursed or converted at that point, but the specific mechanisms are unknown.

Following the initial inquiry, the beneficiary institution initiated a hold on the Cornerstone Commodities LLC account. This action was taken on February 13, 2024. As a result of this hold, a portion of the initial funds was secured. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $700,711.58. This figure represents the remaining balance in the Cornerstone Commodities LLC account at the time the hold was placed. The recovery of these funds is pending further legal and administrative processes between the institutions.

The remaining portion of the initial transfer, representing the residual loss to the customer, is $2,987,244.09. This amount reflects the difference between the initial fraudulent wire and the funds successfully frozen at the beneficiary institution. The onward movement of these unrecovered funds, comprising the transfers to Kestrel Trading Trading Co. and Mapleford Industrial Supply Inc., and any potential subsequent dissipation, cannot be definitively traced beyond the information provided by the initial beneficiary institution. The trail for the unrecovered portion essentially ends at the accounts of the secondary beneficiaries.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The outbound wire transfer was directed to an account held in the name of Cornerstone Commodities LLC, the designated beneficiary on the payment instructions received by Cortex Bank and Trust. The investigation sought to establish the bona fides of this entity and its relationship, if any, to the customer, Greystone Commodities Group LLC. The reviewing analyst reviewed the payment instructions and noted that the beneficiary name, Cornerstone Commodities LLC, did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, which was known to the customer as Kestrel Trading Trading Co. The customer indicated that the payment instructions were received via email from a contact purporting to represent Kestrel Trading Trading Co. The customer further stated that the email instructions included a directive to remit payment to Cornerstone Commodities LLC, described as a newly established subsidiary handling raw material procurement. The customer stated that the email correspondence included language emphasizing the urgency of the transaction, which the customer cited as the reason for overriding their internal dual-approval control for wire transfers.

The reviewing analyst reviewed the email correspondence provided by the customer. The sender's email address utilized a domain name that was a lookalike to the established domain of Kestrel Trading Trading Co., differing by a single character. The investigation determined that the domain utilized in the fraudulent email was registered on January 2, 2024, shortly before the initial contact with the customer. The reviewing analyst conducted open-source research on Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The entity was registered with the relevant secretary of state on January 8, 2024. The registered agent address was identified as a commercial mail receiving agency. No corresponding physical business location, website, or active online presence could be identified for Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The stated business purpose on the corporate registry filings was general trading, a broad designation that provided limited insight into the entity's actual operations.

A request for information was sent to the receiving institution pursuant to section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act. The receiving institution provided limited transactional information regarding the beneficiary account. The account was opened on January 16, 2024. The account opening documentation listed the business purpose as the import and export of industrial materials. The initial funding of the account consisted of a nominal cash deposit. Between January 18, 2024, and January 25, 2024, the account received several inbound wire transfers from various domestic and international originators. The originators included entities operating in disparate industries, and the stated purpose for these transfers, when provided, varied significantly. The reviewing analyst noted that the pattern of inbound transfers appeared inconsistent with the stated business purpose of a newly established entity engaged in the import and export of industrial materials.

Following the receipt of these inbound transfers, the funds were rapidly disbursed. Between February 13, 2024, and February 19, 2024, the account initiated multiple outbound wire transfers to entities located in jurisdictions known to be associated with elevated money laundering risk. A portion of the funds was also transferred to a domestic entity, Mapleford Industrial Supply Inc. The stated purpose for these outbound transfers was frequently omitted or described vaguely as vendor payments. The reviewing analyst noted that the rapid depletion of funds, combined with the lack of clear business purpose and the destinations of the outbound transfers, was consistent with the movement of illicit proceeds.

The fraudulent outbound wire transfer from Greystone Commodities Group LLC, in the amount of $3,687,955.67, was credited to the Cornerstone Commodities LLC account on February 26, 2024. The transfer was initiated by the customer minutes before the wire cutoff time. On March 4, 2024, following notification from Cortex Bank and Trust regarding the suspected fraud, the receiving institution placed a freeze on the beneficiary account. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $700,711.58. The receiving institution confirmed that the remaining funds had been disbursed prior to the placement of the freeze. The investigation concluded that the beneficiary entity, Cornerstone Commodities LLC, exhibited characteristics consistent with a shell company utilized to receive and dissipate the proceeds of wire fraud.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The relationship manager assigned to Greystone Commodities Group LLC was interviewed on March 4, 2024. The relationship manager stated that the customer principal, acting on behalf of Greystone Commodities Group LLC, contacted them by telephone on February 19, 2024. The customer principal inquired about the status of an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $3,687,955.67, which had been initiated from Cortex Bank and Trust account 76-51297-1. The relationship manager advised the customer principal that the transfer had been executed on January 25, 2024. The relationship manager reported that the customer principal expressed confusion, stating that the intended payee, Cornerstone Commodities LLC, had not received the funds. The relationship manager instructed the customer principal to provide the wire transfer confirmation details and any relevant correspondence regarding the payment.

On March 4, 2024, the relationship manager provided the investigating analyst with an email chain forwarded by the customer principal. The correspondence was between an employee of Greystone Commodities Group LLC and an individual purporting to represent Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The email chain originated on January 16, 2024, with the purported representative providing updated payment instructions for an upcoming invoice. The email address used by the purported representative utilized a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the known domain used by Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The analyst reviewed the email headers, which indicated that the message originated from an IP address not previously associated with Cornerstone Commodities LLC. The correspondence contained language emphasizing the urgency of the payment, citing a need to secure favorable pricing for a bulk order of materials.

The investigating analyst reviewed the invoice referenced in the email chain. The invoice, dated January 18, 2024, appeared to be issued by Cornerstone Commodities LLC. However, the beneficiary name provided in the updated payment instructions within the email chain was Kestrel Trading Trading Co. The analyst noted that Kestrel Trading Trading Co. did not match the invoicing vendor, Cornerstone Commodities LLC. Furthermore, a review of previous invoices from Cornerstone Commodities LLC revealed discrepancies in formatting and contact information compared to the invoice dated January 18, 2024.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Following the identification of the suspected fraudulent activity, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated immediate recovery efforts. The relationship manager contacted the customer on March 4, 2024, to confirm the legitimacy of the wire transfer instructions received on February 26, 2024. The customer advised that the payment was intended for Cornerstone Commodities LLC, a known vendor, but the wire instructions provided in the email correspondence directed funds to an account held by Kestrel Trading Trading Co. The customer further stated that they had not intended to authorize a payment to Kestrel Trading Trading Co. and that the email correspondence, which utilized a lookalike domain, was fraudulent. The customer was instructed to file a report with local law enforcement.

Upon confirmation from the customer that the payment instructions were fraudulent, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately transmitted a SWIFT MT192 request for cancellation to the receiving institution, requesting the return of the $3,687,955.67 wire transfer. The request cited suspected fraud and included an offer of standard indemnification. The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the recall request the following business day.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Greystone Commodities Group LLC remitted $3,687,955.67 to a beneficiary, Cornerstone Commodities LLC, whom the customer did not intend to pay. Review of the email correspondence provided by the customer confirmed that the payment instructions were received from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the customer's established vendor, Kestrel Trading Trading Co. The fraudulent instructions included urgency language that overrode the customer's internal dual-approval control. Furthermore, the beneficiary name on the wire instructions did not match the invoicing vendor, and the customer initiated the funds transfer minutes before the wire cutoff on April 16, 2024. The receiving institution froze a portion of the funds; however, the customer suffered a residual loss of $2,987,244.09. The activity is consistent with wire fraud resulting from a business email compromise. Based on the findings, the case disposition is criminal_referral.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2412
Date opened: August 7, 2024
Subject: Nadia Kaminski (individual), account 63-60985-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: ongoing

## Case Summary

On July 23, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust wire operations department referred a matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit concerning a large outbound domestic wire transfer originated by commercial customer Nadia Kaminski from account 63-60985-1. The referral noted that the customer had contacted the relationship manager earlier that day, stating that a vendor she believed she had paid three weeks prior was now inquiring about an overdue balance. The customer’s records indicated that a wire in the amount of $252,830.59 had been successfully transmitted from the Cortex Bank and Trust account, ostensibly to settle an invoice from Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC. The customer supplied a copy of the invoice and the email chain that had precipitated the wire request.

The relationship manager’s preliminary review of the account activity confirmed that an outbound domestic wire for $252,830.59 was processed from account 63-60985-1 on July 3, 2024. However, the beneficiary name on the outgoing wire instructions did not match the vendor name on the invoice the customer had provided. The wire instructions directed the funds to an account held in the name of Emberline Imports Corp., rather than Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC. The customer asserted she had no business relationship with Emberline Imports Corp. and had not intended to transmit funds to that entity. The customer stated that the wire instructions were derived from an email she received, which appeared to be from her established contact at Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC, providing updated payment details for the pending invoice.

The Financial Intelligence Unit opened internal case FIU-WIRE-2412 to investigate the circumstances surrounding the July 3, 2024, wire transfer. The investigation was tasked with determining whether the transaction represented a compromise of the customer’s email environment or the vendor’s systems, resulting in the fraudulent diversion of funds. The primary objective was to trace the communication flow that led to the wire origination, analyze the transaction details against established typologies for business email compromise, and assess the potential for recovery of the diverted funds. The investigation sought to confirm whether the customer was induced by deception to authorize a wire transfer to an unintended beneficiary, consistent with wire fraud.

The reviewing analyst initiated a review of the transaction history for account 63-60985-1, focusing on the period leading up to the disputed wire transfer. The account profile indicated that the customer routinely engaged in commercial transactions, including outbound wires for inventory and supplies. The analyst secured the wire origination records, the customer-provided email correspondence, and the invoice in question to begin the reconstruction of the events. The initial assessment indicated a high likelihood that the funds had been diverted based on fraudulent instructions, given the discrepancy between the intended vendor and the actual beneficiary of the wire transfer. The investigation would require a detailed examination of the digital artifacts and the transaction timeline to establish the mechanics of the suspected fraud.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The matter under review originated on July 23, 2024, when the relationship manager servicing the commercial account of Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC contacted the Financial Intelligence Unit to escalate a customer complaint. A principal of Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC reported that the company had been defrauded of $252,830.59 through a manipulated payment instruction. According to the relationship manager, the customer stated that they believed they were settling an outstanding invoice for specialized industrial components sourced from Emberline Imports Corp. The customer further alleged that the payment instructions for this invoice had been altered by an unknown party who had intercepted the vendor's email communications. The relationship manager submitted copies of the email thread and the relevant invoices to support the customer's claim.

The Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a review of the transaction history for Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC, focusing on the period surrounding the reported loss. The transaction in question was an outbound wire transfer of $252,830.59 executed on July 22, 2024. The beneficiary named on the wire transfer instructions was not Emberline Imports Corp., but rather an entity identified as Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. The customer alleged that they did not recognize Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. and had no established business relationship with that entity. The customer asserted that the funds were intended solely for Emberline Imports Corp. and that the payment was directed to Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. solely because of the fraudulent instructions received via email.

Following the initial escalation by the relationship manager, Cortex Bank and Trust received a formal wire recall request from the customer on July 23, 2024, citing fraud as the reason for the recall. The Financial Intelligence Unit immediately transmitted a recall notice to the receiving institution, requesting the return of the $252,830.59. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall notice but did not immediately confirm whether the funds were available for return. The Financial Intelligence Unit subsequently engaged with the receiving institution's fraud department to ascertain the status of the funds and to coordinate potential recovery efforts.

The customer provided additional context regarding the circumstances leading to the wire transfer. The principal of Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC stated that the email containing the altered payment instructions appeared to originate from a known contact at Emberline Imports Corp. However, the customer later determined that the sender's email address was a lookalike domain, differing from the legitimate vendor's domain by a single character. The fraudulent email included urgency language, pressuring the customer to expedite the payment to avoid delays in the shipment of the industrial components. The customer acknowledged that this perceived urgency contributed to the decision to bypass the company's internal dual-approval control for outbound wire transfers, which typically requires secondary authorization for transactions exceeding a specific threshold.

The transaction records confirmed that the wire transfer of $252,830.59 was initiated by Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC on July 22, 2024, shortly before the bank's daily wire cutoff time. The timing of the initiation, coupled with the bypassed internal controls and the discrepancy between the invoiced vendor and the wire beneficiary, aligned with the customer's allegation of a compromised communication channel and manipulated payment instructions. The initial review of the referral documentation and the transaction history indicated that the activity was consistent with a business email compromise scheme, wherein an attacker deceives a victim into directing funds to an account controlled by the attacker rather than the intended recipient. The Financial Intelligence Unit commenced a full investigation to trace the flow of funds and to evaluate the extent of the suspected fraud.

## Timeline of Events

The review of the events leading up to the fraudulent wire transfer began with a forensic examination of the customer's email communications. On May 21, 2024, the principal of the customer entity, Nadia Kaminski, received an email from an address purporting to belong to Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC, a known vendor. The email address used a lookalike sender domain that differed from the genuine Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC domain by a single character. This email included an invoice for an upcoming shipment and instructions to update the payment details for future remittances. The communication instructed that all future payments be directed to an account held in the name of Emberline Imports Corp.

The customer acknowledged receipt of these instructions on May 27, 2024, but did not immediately initiate a payment. A subsequent email from the fraudulent address was received on June 7, 2024. This communication contained language emphasizing the need for prompt payment to avoid delays in the shipment. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer did not attempt to verify the change in payment instructions through an independent channel.

On June 11, 2024, the customer received a further communication from the fraudulent address, again stressing the urgency of the payment. The customer’s internal controls require dual approval for outgoing wires exceeding a certain threshold. However, the customer later reported to Cortex Bank and Trust that the purported urgency of the request led them to bypass this internal control. The customer initiated a wire transfer on June 25, 2024, directed to the account specified in the fraudulent instructions. The reviewing analyst observed that the beneficiary name on the wire instruction, Emberline Imports Corp., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC.

The wire transfer was initiated by the customer minutes before the wire cutoff time on June 25, 2024. The outbound wire, in the amount of $252,830.59, was processed and transmitted by Cortex Bank and Trust. The funds were directed to the account held by Emberline Imports Corp. at the receiving institution.

The customer became aware of the discrepancy on July 3, 2024, when the genuine Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC contacted them regarding the outstanding invoice. The customer realized that the payment had been misdirected and contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report the suspected fraud. The customer provided copies of the email correspondence, which allowed the reviewing analyst to identify the lookalike domain and the altered payment instructions. The customer also confirmed that they had not intended to remit funds to Emberline Imports Corp.

Upon receiving the customer's report, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request to the receiving institution on July 11, 2024. The receiving institution responded on July 22, 2024, confirming receipt of the recall request. The receiving institution subsequently informed Cortex Bank and Trust that a portion of the funds remained in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution confirmed that $27,811.36 had been frozen and was secured pending further investigation and authorization for return.

The reviewing analyst noted that the remaining funds had been dissipated from the beneficiary account prior to the freeze being implemented. The investigation established that the total sum diverted as a result of the deceptive instructions was the full amount of the initial outbound wire. The customer was advised on July 23, 2024, regarding the status of the recall effort and the partial recovery of funds. The investigation into the circumstances of the transfer and the subsequent movement of funds remains ongoing.

## Funds Tracing

On July 22, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust executed an outbound domestic wire transfer from the operating account of Nadia Kaminski, account 63-60985-1. The transfer instructions directed the funds to a commercial checking account at a mid-tier regional bank located in the mid-Atlantic region. The stated beneficiary on the wire instructions was Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. However, subsequent investigation by the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit determined that the invoicing vendor intended by Nadia Kaminski was an entity known as Emberline Imports Corp. A discrepancy was noted in that the beneficiary name on the transfer instructions did not align with the intended recipient. The funds transfer was initiated by Nadia Kaminski shortly before the daily wire cutoff time on July 22, 2024, a timing anomaly that is often observed in fraud schemes to minimize the window for recall or cancellation.

The originating debit to account 63-60985-1 was for $252,830.59. This amount represents the entirety of the funds diverted through this suspected fraud scheme. The initial hop of the funds was from Cortex Bank and Trust to the designated receiving institution. Upon notification from Nadia Kaminski on July 23, 2024, regarding the suspected deception, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately issued a SWIFT MT192 recall request to the receiving institution.

The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request and initiated a review of the beneficiary account held in the name of Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the $252,830.59 transfer on July 22, 2024. However, the receiving institution reported that significant dissipation of the funds had already occurred prior to the placement of a hold on the account. The receiving institution was able to freeze a remaining balance.

The amount secured by the receiving institution was $27,811.36. This sum represents the only portion of the original transfer that has been recovered or frozen to date. Consequently, the unrecovered portion of the transfer stands at $225,019.23. This figure represents the residual exposure resulting from the incident.

Information provided by the receiving institution, acting on a request for information under Section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act, detailed the onward movement of the dissipated funds. According to the receiving institution, the balance of the funds, minus the frozen amount, was dispersed rapidly on the morning of July 23, 2024. The primary mechanism of dispersal was a series of outbound domestic wire transfers.

The most significant onward movement involved a wire transfer to an account held in the name of Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC at a different, large national banking association. The exact amount of this secondary transfer to Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC was not disclosed by the receiving institution, but it was described as constituting the majority of the dissipated funds. The receiving institution also noted several smaller outgoing transfers, utilizing peer-to-peer payment networks and automated clearing house debits, which further depleted the account balance. The ultimate beneficiaries of these smaller transactions were not identified in the information provided by the receiving institution.

The trail of the funds currently ends at the account held by Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC. Cortex Bank and Trust has limited visibility into the subsequent disposition of the funds once they were credited to that entity. It is inferred, based on common typologies associated with this type of suspected fraud, that the funds transferred to Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC may have been subjected to further obfuscation, potentially involving conversion to cryptocurrency, international remittance, or rapid cash withdrawal. However, without direct access to the transactional records of Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC, these subsequent hops cannot be definitively documented. The investigation is continuing to explore avenues for further tracing, including potential collaboration with law enforcement agencies.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The investigation reviewed the destination of the outgoing wire from Nadia Kaminski's Cortex Bank and Trust account 63-60985-1. The beneficiary of the $252,830.59 transfer executed on July 22, 2024, was listed as Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC. Corporate registry research indicated this entity was formed in the recipient institution's jurisdiction on May 21, 2024. The stated business purpose on the incorporation documents was wholesale trade of non-ferrous metals. The principal address listed was a commercial mailbox facility. No public-facing website, active social media presence, or third-party business directory listings were identified for Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC during the open-source review. The age of the entity relative to the transfer date, combined with the lack of an established digital footprint, is consistent with a shell company formed to receive and disperse funds.

Analysis of the information provided by the receiving institution regarding the beneficiary account revealed a pattern of activity inconsistent with the stated business purpose. The account was opened on May 27, 2024. Between the account opening date and July 22, 2024, the account received five incoming domestic wires. The originators of these prior wires were unrelated individuals and entities across various jurisdictions. The stated purpose of these incoming transfers, where recorded, varied widely and did not appear related to the wholesale trade of metals.

Following the receipt of the $252,830.59 wire from Nadia Kaminski on July 22, 2024, the funds were rapidly dispersed. On July 23, 2024, two outgoing international wires were executed from the Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC account. The first wire was directed to an account held by Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. at an offshore financial institution. The second wire was sent to Emberline Imports Corp. at a different offshore institution. Neither of these counterparties appears to have any business relationship with Nadia Kaminski or her known business activities. The rapid movement of funds out of the beneficiary account to offshore entities, immediately following receipt, is indicative of layering activity designed to obscure the ultimate destination of the diverted funds.

The receiving institution confirmed that $27,811.36 remained in the Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC account at the time the fraud was reported and the account was restricted. This amount represents a portion of the funds transferred from Nadia Kaminski's account, leaving a residual loss of $225,019.23. The rapid depletion of the account balance before the restriction could be placed is consistent with the operations of a money mule or a dedicated fraud receiving account.

Further review of the counterparties Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. and Emberline Imports Corp. yielded limited information. Both entities are registered in jurisdictions known for corporate secrecy. No clear business operations or physical footprints could be established for either entity through open-source intelligence gathering. The transfer of the diverted funds to these entities further complicates the tracing and potential recovery of the assets. The use of newly formed domestic entities to receive funds, followed by rapid international transfers to opaque corporate structures, is a recognized typology in business email compromise and related wire fraud schemes. The investigation into the ultimate beneficiaries of Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. and Emberline Imports Corp. remains active.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The investigation obtained and reviewed documentary evidence, including email correspondence, vendor invoices, and wire transfer requests, to establish the sequence of events leading to the suspected diversion of funds. An interview was conducted with Nadia Kaminski on July 23, 2024, to clarify the circumstances surrounding the authorization of the wire transfer. The customer stated that the authorization was provided based on an email she believed was sent by a known vendor, Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC. The customer asserted that the email contained payment instructions for an outstanding invoice and that the communication appeared legitimate at the time of receipt.

A review of the email correspondence provided by the customer revealed that the payment instructions were received on July 22, 2024. The email originated from a lookalike sender domain that differed from the legitimate domain of Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC by a single character. The message contained an attached invoice for $252,830.59, bearing the logo and formatting typically used by the vendor. However, the remittance instructions directed payment to an account held by Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd., rather than Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC. The customer confirmed during the interview that this beneficiary name did not match the invoicing vendor but stated she did not notice the discrepancy at the time the transfer was initiated.

The email correspondence also included urgency language, stating that payment must be received immediately to avoid supply chain disruptions. The customer reported that this language prompted her to initiate the wire transfer without adhering to her usual internal procedure of secondary verification for large payments, effectively overriding a dual-approval control. Authentication logs confirm that the customer initiated the wire request through the online banking portal on July 22, 2024. The request was submitted minutes before the wire cutoff time for that business day.

The investigation obtained copies of previous, legitimate invoices issued by Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC to the customer. A comparison of these documents with the invoice received on July 22, 2024, confirmed the discrepancy in the beneficiary name and the remittance account details. The legitimate invoices directed payment to an account held in the name of Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC, whereas the fraudulent invoice directed funds to Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. No legitimate business purpose was identified for the customer to remit funds to Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd.

Following the initiation of the transfer, Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution to request a hold on the funds. The receiving institution confirmed on July 23, 2024, that a portion of the funds, totaling $27,811.36, had been successfully frozen in the beneficiary account. The remaining funds had already been disbursed or transferred out of the account prior to the hold being placed.

A review of historical account activity for Nadia Kaminski did not reveal any prior transactions involving Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd. The investigation also identified a prior, unrelated inquiry from the customer on June 11, 2024, regarding a potential transaction with Emberline Imports Corp. However, no funds transfers to Emberline Imports Corp. were executed, and this inquiry is not believed to be related to the suspected fraud event on July 22, 2024. The documentary evidence, combined with the customer interview, is consistent with a business email compromise scenario where the customer was induced by deception to authorize a wire transfer to a beneficiary she did not intend to pay. The investigation into the incident and the recovery of the remaining funds is ongoing.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

On July 23, 2024, upon notification by Nadia Kaminski that the July 22, 2024 wire transfer was fraudulent, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a formal recall and indemnification request through the Fedwire system. The request identified the outgoing wire transfer of $252,830.59 to Emberline Imports Corp. as having been induced by fraud and requested the immediate return of the funds. The request cited the discrepancy between the intended beneficiary, Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC, and the actual recipient of the wire transfer. Cortex Bank and Trust also communicated directly with the receiving institution's fraud department by telephone, providing details regarding the compromised email communication and the lookalike domain used to transmit the altered payment instructions. The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the recall request on the same day.

The receiving institution subsequently informed Cortex Bank and Trust that the account held by Emberline Imports Corp. had been restricted, but that a significant portion of the funds had already been withdrawn or transferred outward prior to the receipt of the recall notice. The receiving institution confirmed that a hold had been placed on the remaining balance in the account. On July 25, 2024, the receiving institution formally responded to the indemnification request, stating that they were able to secure $27,811.36 of the original transfer amount. The receiving institution indicated that they were unable to recover the balance of the funds, as they had been moved to other accounts or withdrawn via cashier's checks.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that on July 23, 2024, the subject Nadia Kaminski initiated an outbound wire transfer of $252,830.59 to an account held in the name of Falcon Crest Metals Group LLC. The subject later reported to Cortex Bank and Trust that the payment was intended for a different vendor, Millpond Marine Services Holdings Ltd., to settle an outstanding invoice. A review of the email correspondence provided by the subject revealed that the payment instructions were altered by an unknown actor using a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the vendor's actual domain. The fraudulent email contained urgency language overriding the subject's customary dual-approval control, and the funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time. The beneficiary name on the wire instructions did not match the invoicing vendor. While Cortex Bank and Trust was able to secure a partial recovery after the receiving institution froze a portion of the funds, the residual loss to the customer remained substantial. The investigation fixed August 5, 2024 as the determinative date of the fraud discovery. The disposition of this matter is ongoing pending further communication with the receiving institution regarding the frozen funds.

## Report Header

This lookalike sender domain was not identified by the customer prior to initiating the transfer. The customer alleged that the urgency expressed in the email correspondence influenced their decision to process the payment quickly. The reviewing analyst noted that the email contained language stressing the immediate need for funds. The customer stated that they proceeded with the transfer based on this perceived urgency. The allegation presented by the customer indicated a scenario where deception was used to induce the transfer of funds out of the account.

The referral source was the customer, Lachlan Zimmerman, who directly contacted Cortex Bank and Trust. The customer's initial contact was the sole source of the allegation at the time the investigation commenced. No automated alerts or external inquiries prompted the review of this specific transaction. The customer’s description of events suggested that the transfer to Obsidian Holdings Partners LP was not authorized in the sense that the customer was deceived as to the true identity of the beneficiary. The customer maintained that they intended to pay a legitimate invoice but were misled by the fraudulent instructions. The reviewing analyst recorded the customer’s claims and began the process of verifying the transaction details. The customer's allegation that the funds were diverted through deception required further examination of the transaction's characteristics and the surrounding circumstances.

The reviewing analyst noted the specific details provided by the customer regarding the transfer. The customer identified the beneficiary name, Obsidian Holdings Partners LP, as unrecognized and not matching the invoicing vendor. The customer's communication indicated that the transfer was initiated on August 27, 2024. The customer alleged that the transfer was executed shortly after receiving the altered payment instructions. The reviewing analyst observed that the funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time on that date. The customer's referral provided the necessary context to evaluate the transaction against known typologies of wire fraud. The allegation centered on the customer's assertion that they were manipulated into sending funds to a fraudulent party.

## Timeline of Events

The investigation review period commenced on July 30, 2024, the date Lachlan Zimmerman opened Cortex Bank and Trust account 30-38528-1. Initial funding and early account activity appeared commensurate with the stated purpose of the account, which was described as operating capital for a nascent venture, though documentation establishing the nature of the business was limited. Account behavior remained unremarkable throughout early August. The first indication of anomalous activity occurred on August 9, 2024, when Lachlan Zimmerman received an email containing payment instructions. Review of the communication by the investigating analyst revealed the sender's email address utilized a lookalike domain, substituting a single character in the domain name of a known, legitimate vendor. The email directed payment for supposed consulting services to an entity named Bramblewood Management LLC.

On August 19, 2024, Lachlan Zimmerman initiated an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $212,736.55. The transaction was processed through the bank's online platform. The beneficiary was designated as Bramblewood Management LLC. The accompanying communication from the fraudster, later provided by the customer during the investigation, contained language stressing the urgency of the payment, which appeared designed to circumvent the customer's internal dual-approval controls. The transfer was initiated shortly before the daily wire cutoff time, a tactic frequently observed in attempts to minimize the window for intervention or recall. The funds were transmitted to an external receiving institution.

The customer contacted Cortex Bank and Trust on August 27, 2024, to report the transaction as unauthorized, stating that the intended recipient of the funds was a different vendor and that the payment instructions received on August 9, 2024, were fraudulent. The customer further indicated that the true vendor had not received the anticipated payment. The bank immediately initiated a recall request through the wire network.

On September 2, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received notification from the receiving institution regarding the recall request. The receiving institution confirmed that a portion of the funds, totaling $74,457.79, had been successfully frozen in the beneficiary account. The remaining balance of the transferred funds had already been depleted or otherwise moved beyond the reach of the receiving institution prior to the receipt of the recall notice.

Further review of the transaction details on September 16, 2024, highlighted a discrepancy between the beneficiary name on the wire transfer, Bramblewood Management LLC, and the name of the vendor the customer claimed to have intended to pay. The customer's internal records, submitted for review, indicated an ongoing relationship with a different entity, suggesting the invoice provided by the fraudster was entirely fabricated.

Additional analysis conducted on September 18, 2024, sought to identify any connections between the beneficiary entity, Bramblewood Management LLC, and the known entities Obsidian Holdings Partners LP and Redstone Imports Enterprises LLC, which had appeared in unrelated, low-value transactions within Lachlan Zimmerman's account history. No direct linkages or shared principals were identified between the entities, and the prior transactions did not exhibit characteristics indicative of fraudulent activity.

The customer confirmed on October 23, 2024, that the frozen funds in the amount of $74,457.79 had been successfully repatriated to Cortex Bank and Trust account 30-38528-1. The customer acknowledged the residual loss of $138,278.76, representing the portion of the initial transfer that could not be recovered. The investigation confirmed this amount as the total unrecovered loss resulting from the fraudulent instruction.

On October 29, 2024, the investigating analyst compiled the available documentation, including the fraudulent email correspondence, the customer's internal vendor records, and the communication with the receiving institution, to finalize the review of the transaction sequence. The timeline of events and the associated financial impact were documented for the purpose of completing the investigative review. The subsequent analysis of the customer's overall profile and the decision regarding any further reporting or action were deferred to the concluding sections of the report.

## Funds Tracing

The subject transaction occurred on August 27, 2024. A debit of $212,736.55 was posted to account 30-38528-1, held by Lachlan Zimmerman at Cortex Bank and Trust. The corresponding entry was an outgoing wire transfer initiated through the bank's online banking portal. The transaction was authenticated using standard credentials and processed through the Federal Reserve Wire Network.

The payment instructions directed the funds to a commercial checking account at a large domestic bank. The beneficiary name on the wire instruction was Bramblewood Management LLC. Cortex Bank and Trust records indicate this was the first transaction between the subject account and this beneficiary. The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary name did not align with the vendor name detailed in the underlying invoice provided by the customer during the subsequent inquiry. The wire transfer was initiated minutes before the daily cutoff, an attribute often observed in fraudulent transfers intended to limit the window for recall requests.

Information regarding the disposition of funds upon receipt at the beneficiary institution is limited to details obtained through interbank communication. Upon notification of the suspected fraud, a recall request was transmitted. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the $212,736.55 transfer. A hold was placed on the beneficiary account. The receiving institution later confirmed that $74,457.79 was successfully frozen and remained in the beneficiary account. These funds were subsequently returned to Cortex Bank and Trust and credited back to the subject account.

The remaining balance of the original transfer, calculated as $138,278.76, was no longer available in the beneficiary account at the time the hold was placed. The receiving institution declined to provide specific details regarding the onward movement of these funds, citing privacy regulations and their own ongoing internal investigation. Therefore, the specific methods used to dissipate the $138,278.76, whether through subsequent wire transfers, automated clearing house payments, cash withdrawals, or the purchase of monetary instruments, cannot be definitively established by Cortex Bank and Trust.

While direct tracing beyond the initial beneficiary account is not possible, analysis of the available information suggests a rapid dissipation of a significant portion of the transferred funds. The time elapsed between the crediting of the funds to the Bramblewood Management LLC account and the placement of the hold indicates that the onward movement occurred swiftly, a pattern consistent with the suspected typology.

The reviewing analyst noted the presence of urgency language in the compromised email communication that precipitated the transfer. This language appears to have been designed to circumvent the customer's internal dual-approval control, facilitating the rapid execution of the wire transfer. The use of a lookalike sender domain, differing by only one character from the legitimate vendor's domain, was also identified as a key element in deceiving the customer into initiating the payment.

The trail of funds, as documented by Cortex Bank and Trust, ends at the beneficiary account held by Bramblewood Management LLC. The $74,457.79 recovered represents the portion of the funds that were successfully intercepted before further movement could occur. The remaining $138,278.76 represents the unrecovered portion of the transfer. The investigation established this amount as the total sum diverted from the intended recipient and the residual loss incurred by the customer. No further information regarding the ultimate destination or beneficiaries of the dissipated funds is available to Cortex Bank and Trust. The investigation into the onward movement of the unrecovered funds relies entirely on the actions and disclosures of the receiving institution.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The receiving account at the counterparty institution was held in the name of Bramblewood Management LLC. Public records indicated that this entity was formed in the state of incorporation approximately four weeks prior to the receipt of the outbound wire transfer. A search of state registry databases returned no prior operating history for this entity. The registered agent address for Bramblewood Management LLC was identified as a commercial mail receiving agency. A review of open-source information, including internet searches and corporate registries, did not identify a website, physical operating location, or any commercial footprint for this entity. The business purpose stated at account opening could not be independently verified through public records.

The beneficiary name on the transfer instructions, Bramblewood Management LLC, did not match the vendor named on the invoice provided by the customer. The invoice, which precipitated the $212,736.55 wire transfer, was purportedly issued by Obsidian Holdings Partners LP. The customer indicated that the payment instructions received via email directed the funds to Bramblewood Management LLC, and that the discrepancy was not noticed prior to authorizing the transfer. The email containing the payment instructions originated from a domain that differed from the legitimate Obsidian Holdings Partners LP domain by a single character. The urgency language contained within the email communication, which the customer cited as the reason for bypassing established dual-approval controls, instructed that the payment be remitted to Bramblewood Management LLC to avoid immediate cessation of services.

Further analysis of the counterparty information revealed a connection to another entity, Redstone Imports Enterprises LLC. A review of the registered agent information for Bramblewood Management LLC indicated that the same commercial mail receiving agency address was used by Redstone Imports Enterprises LLC. Open-source searches for Redstone Imports Enterprises LLC yielded limited information, with no identifiable website or physical commercial location. The lack of verifiable commercial presence for both entities is consistent with shell company characteristics often observed in the receipt and subsequent dispersal of fraudulently obtained funds.

Following the initiation of the transfer on October 23, 2024, the receiving institution was contacted in an attempt to recall the funds. The receiving institution confirmed the receipt of the $212,736.55 wire transfer into the account held by Bramblewood Management LLC. A review of the transactional activity on the receiving account, as described by the counterparty institution, indicated a rapid dispersal of funds following the incoming credit. The receiving institution reported that a significant portion of the funds was transferred out of the account via multiple outbound wires to various external accounts shortly after the initial credit. The rapid movement of funds is a common typology associated with the obfuscation of illicit proceeds.

The receiving institution was able to freeze a portion of the funds remaining in the Bramblewood Management LLC account. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $74,457.79. The counterparty institution indicated that the remainder of the funds had already been dispersed and were no longer available for recovery. The pattern of credits and rapid debits on the receiving account, combined with the lack of verifiable business operations for Bramblewood Management LLC, suggests that the account was established primarily for the receipt and onward transfer of funds. The transactional behavior observed on the receiving account is not consistent with legitimate commercial activity. The failure to identify a legitimate business purpose for Bramblewood Management LLC, coupled with the rapid dispersal of funds, supports the assessment that the receiving account was utilized in the furtherance of a wire fraud scheme.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The investigation obtained the email thread between Lachlan Zimmerman and the purported vendor, which commenced on October 23, 2024. Analysis of the email headers revealed that the sender's domain closely resembled that of the legitimate vendor but differed by a single character. This discrepancy was not identified by Lachlan Zimmerman during the correspondence. The email chain contained escalating urgency language, culminating in a message on October 29, 2024, demanding immediate payment to avoid service disruption. The correspondence instructed Lachlan Zimmerman to remit funds to a new beneficiary, Obsidian Holdings Partners LP, rather than the established vendor.

Review of the invoice provided within the email thread on October 23, 2024, showed it was formatted similarly to previous legitimate invoices received from the vendor, detailing consulting services rendered. However, the remittance instructions directed payment to Obsidian Holdings Partners LP, a name that did not align with the invoicing vendor. This misalignment was a key element in the deception, as the invoice appeared authentic in its itemization but contained fraudulent payment details.

The relationship manager assigned to Lachlan Zimmerman was interviewed regarding the customer's typical wire activity. The relationship manager confirmed that Lachlan Zimmerman had an established pattern of remitting payments to the legitimate vendor, but no prior history of transactions with Obsidian Holdings Partners LP. The relationship manager noted that Lachlan Zimmerman had not sought clarification regarding the change in beneficiary name prior to initiating the transfer.

Authentication logs for Cortex Bank and Trust account 30-38528-1 were reviewed for October 29, 2024. The logs indicated that Lachlan Zimmerman accessed the online banking platform and initiated the wire transfer. The initiation occurred minutes before the bank's daily wire cutoff time. The system recorded the authorization of the $212,736.55 outbound wire transfer, confirming that the customer bypassed the recommended dual-approval control, citing the urgency conveyed in the fraudulent emails.

The investigation obtained a call recording from Cortex Bank and Trust's wire operations department on October 29, 2024. The recording captured a conversation between a wire operations representative and Lachlan Zimmerman. During the call, the representative attempted to verify the details of the $212,736.55 wire transfer due to the late initiation time and the new beneficiary, Obsidian Holdings Partners LP. Lachlan Zimmerman confirmed the payment details and reiterated the urgency of the transaction, referencing the potential service disruption mentioned in the email correspondence. The wire was subsequently processed based on this verbal confirmation.

Documentation from the receiving institution was obtained following the initiation of recall procedures. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the $212,736.55 wire transfer. Subsequent communication with the receiving institution established that a portion of the funds had already been moved or withdrawn prior to the recall request. The receiving institution placed a freeze on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $74,457.79.

Further inquiry with Lachlan Zimmerman confirmed that the remaining $138,278.76 was not recovered. Lachlan Zimmerman provided documentation indicating attempts to contact the legitimate vendor following the realization of the fraud, confirming that the vendor had not sent the email correspondence or the invoice received on October 23, 2024, and had no relationship with Obsidian Holdings Partners LP. The customer acknowledged that the urgency language in the email had prompted the immediate action and the circumvention of standard verification procedures. The investigation reviewed the customer's internal communication logs, which corroborated the timeline of events and the reliance on the fraudulent email instructions. No evidence was found to suggest that Lachlan Zimmerman was aware of the fraudulent nature of the communication prior to the completion of the wire transfer.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Upon determining that the outbound funds transfer of $212,736.55 was fraudulent, the reviewing analyst initiated an immediate recall request to the receiving institution. This action was taken on October 29, 2024. The request was transmitted through established interbank messaging channels and cited suspected wire fraud, specifically noting that Lachlan Zimmerman had been induced to execute the transfer by deception. The recall message requested the immediate freezing of the beneficiary account and the return of the full transferred amount. Cortex Bank and Trust received an initial automated acknowledgement of the recall message on the same day.

The receiving institution provided a substantive response on October 2, 2023. The response indicated that the beneficiary account, held in the name of Redstone Imports Enterprises LLC, had been located. However, the receiving institution advised that the funds had been substantially depleted prior to the receipt of the recall request. The response confirmed that a hold had been placed on the remaining balance in the account.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Lachlan Zimmerman initiated a wire transfer of $212,736.55 on October 23, 2024, acting on instructions received via email. The reviewing analyst determined that the email sender's domain closely resembled that of a known vendor, differing by only one character. The email contained urgency language that bypassed the customer's established dual-approval control. The beneficiary of the wire transfer was Bramblewood Management LLC, an entity that did not match the invoicing vendor's name. The transfer was initiated shortly before the daily wire cutoff time. The investigation concluded that the funds were induced out of the customer account by deception. A portion of the funds was frozen at the receiving institution, resulting in a residual loss to the customer. On November 19, 2024, the investigation concluded that the activity was consistent with wire fraud. The case was closed with a disposition of closed_no_action, as the customer had been fully reimbursed and the receiving institution had been notified.
