body:
## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2414
Date opened: July 17, 2024
Subject: Adrian Yarborough (individual), account 13-62414-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: referred_to_fincen

## Case Summary

The Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a review of Adrian Yarborough on July 3, 2024, following a referral from the branch network. The referral stated that the customer reported a suspected fraud incident involving Cortex Bank and Trust account 13-62414-1. The customer indicated that an outbound wire transfer had been induced by deception and sent to a beneficiary not intended by the customer. The investigation was tasked with reviewing the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire, assessing the legitimacy of the beneficiary and the payment instructions, and determining if the activity was consistent with a business email compromise or other wire fraud typology. The investigation was assigned internal reference FIU-WIRE-2414 and designated a medium risk tier. The review period for this investigation was established as March 11, 2024, through July 3, 2024.

The referral indicated that on June 27, 2024, the customer initiated an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $113,070.02. The customer reported that the transfer was intended as payment for an invoice received via email. The customer subsequently contacted Cortex Bank and Trust, stating that the payment instructions were fraudulent and that the funds had been diverted to an unknown beneficiary. The investigation was required to analyze the transactional activity within account 13-62414-1 during the review period to identify the specific transfer, review the customer's communication regarding the payment instructions, and attempt to trace the destination of the funds. The investigation also had to assess whether any indicators of fraud were present during the initiation of the transfer, such as the timing of the request, the beneficiary information, or the nature of the communication authorizing the payment.

The investigation focused on the events leading up to the June 27, 2024 transfer. The customer reported that the wire transfer request was initiated based on an email containing payment instructions. The investigation reviewed the customer's account activity and identified the outbound wire transfer of $113,070.02. The investigation noted that the customer had received correspondence purportedly from an established vendor. The customer indicated that the email contained a request for payment of an outstanding invoice and provided updated beneficiary details. The investigation was required to review the beneficiary information provided in the wire transfer request and compare it to the customer's established vendor records.

The customer stated that the wire transfer request was processed shortly before the bank's wire cutoff time. The investigation reviewed the time of the transfer initiation and the subsequent processing of the wire. The investigation also reviewed the communication authorizing the transfer to determine if any urgency was conveyed that may have bypassed standard verification procedures. The customer indicated that the email requesting payment contained language emphasizing the need for immediate action. The investigation was tasked with determining if the customer's established dual-approval controls for wire transfers were circumvented or overridden in response to this urgency. The investigation was required to evaluate the communication for indicators of spoofing or deception, such as discrepancies in the sender's email address or the beneficiary name. The investigation reviewed the beneficiary name on the wire transfer request and compared it to the vendor name on the invoice to determine if a discrepancy existed. The investigation also attempted to contact the receiving institution to determine the status of the transferred funds and to request a recall of the wire transfer.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On July 3, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit received a referral regarding Adrian Yarborough. The referral was initiated by a relationship manager following communication with the customer. The customer reported a suspected fraudulent event involving a domestic wire transfer originated from his personal checking account, number 13-62414-1, on June 27, 2024. The relationship manager submitted the referral through the internal case management system after the customer expressed concern that he had been the victim of deception resulting in the misdirection of funds. The initial review of the referral indicated that the customer had received an invoice via email and subsequently authorized a wire transfer to fulfill the obligation, but later realized the beneficiary information was incorrect. The customer stated that the intended recipient of the funds had not received payment and had contacted him regarding the outstanding balance. The referral noted that the customer believed his email correspondence had been compromised or intercepted, leading to the fraudulent instructions.

The customer claimed that the wire transfer, executed on June 27, 2024, was intended to settle an invoice related to services provided by Copperfield Equipment Inc. According to the referral, the customer received an email containing payment instructions that he believed originated from a representative of Copperfield Equipment Inc. The customer stated that he had previously communicated with this representative regarding the services rendered. The relationship manager’s notes indicated that the customer acted upon the email instructions and initiated the wire transfer through the online banking portal. The referral further detailed that the customer only recognized the discrepancy when Copperfield Equipment Inc. subsequently inquired about the status of the payment. The customer reported to the relationship manager that he then reviewed the payment instructions and the wire transfer confirmation, realizing that the funds had not been sent to Copperfield Equipment Inc.

The referral stated that the customer, upon recognizing the error, contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to request a recall of the wire transfer. The relationship manager documented the customer's assertion that the email containing the fraudulent payment instructions included language urging immediate payment to avoid penalties or delays. The customer claimed this urgency prompted him to authorize the transfer quickly. The referral also noted the customer's observation that the beneficiary name on the wire transfer confirmation did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Copperfield Equipment Inc. The relationship manager recorded the customer’s belief that the email address from which the fraudulent instructions were received closely resembled the legitimate email address of the Copperfield Equipment Inc. representative. The initial review of the referral prompted the opening of this investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the wire transfer and to assess the potential for financial loss. The referral highlighted the need to investigate the customer's claims of deception and the subsequent misdirection of funds. The relationship manager requested an assessment of the transaction to determine if the activity was consistent with a business email compromise or similar fraudulent scheme. The referral included the customer's request for assistance in attempting to recover the transferred funds. The initial information provided in the referral formed the basis for the subsequent investigative steps, which focused on the details of the June 27, 2024 wire transfer and the customer's communications regarding the invoice. The investigation was initiated to verify the customer's allegations and to evaluate the transaction against known typologies of wire fraud.

## Timeline of Events

On March 11, 2024, Adrian Yarborough received an email at his personal address from an individual representing themselves as an accounts receivable clerk for Millpond Consulting LLC, a vendor Yarborough had previously engaged for tax preparation services. This email was sent from a domain that differed from the legitimate Millpond Consulting LLC domain by a single character. The sender stated that an invoice for services rendered in the previous tax year was past due and required immediate payment to avoid a referral to collections. Yarborough, a longstanding Cortex Bank and Trust customer, maintained a checking account under the number 13-62414-1. No communication occurred on March 12, 2024, but on March 15, 2024, the fraudster sent a follow-up email. This message included urgency language, claiming that the final deadline for payment was imminent and that failure to remit the funds would result in an immediate penalty fee being assessed.

On April 4, 2024, Yarborough visited a Cortex Bank and Trust branch and initiated an outbound domestic wire transfer in the amount of $113,070.02. This transaction was initiated minutes before the daily wire cutoff time. The beneficiary named on the wire instructions was Copperfield Equipment Inc., an entity unrelated to the purported invoicing vendor, Millpond Consulting LLC. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer circumvented the standard dual-approval control for wire transfers exceeding a specific threshold by citing the urgency language from the fraudulent emails, insisting the transfer needed to be completed immediately to avoid the stated penalties. This circumvention was documented by the branch staff processing the request. A week later, on April 11, 2024, the customer contacted Cortex Bank and Trust customer service. He reported that he had received a genuine invoice from Millpond Consulting LLC via the U.S. Postal Service and realized that the email instructions he had followed on April 4, 2024, were fraudulent.

Following this notification, a Cortex Bank and Trust fraud investigator initiated a recall request for the $113,070.02 wire on May 8, 2024. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request on May 14, 2024. Communication between the institutions continued, and on May 17, 2024, the receiving institution informed Cortex Bank and Trust that the beneficiary account had been largely depleted shortly after the funds were credited. The receiving institution confirmed they were able to place a hold on the remaining balance in the Copperfield Equipment Inc. account. On June 27, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received confirmation that a partial recovery had been secured. The receiving institution was able to freeze and return a portion of the original wire, while the remainder of the funds had already been withdrawn or transferred by the beneficiary. The total amount the investigation established as diverted was $113,070.02. The amount frozen at the receiving institution and subsequently returned to Cortex Bank and Trust was $11,307.00. The residual loss to the customer was determined to be $101,763.02. The investigation further revealed that Copperfield Equipment Inc. was not the final destination for all the diverted funds, as transaction records indicated subsequent transfers to another entity, Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd., although the purpose of these subsequent transfers remains unclear. The incident was escalated for further review and reporting based on the confirmed diversion of customer funds through deceptive instructions.

## Funds Tracing

The originating transaction occurred on June 27, 2024, when Cortex Bank and Trust account 13-62414-1, held by Adrian Yarborough, was debited via an outgoing wire transfer. The transfer, in the amount of $113,070.02, was directed to an account at a domestic financial institution. The beneficiary name provided on the wire instructions was Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd., which did not correspond to the purported invoicing vendor, Copperfield Equipment Inc. The wire transfer was initiated late in the business day, shortly before the established wire cutoff time. Following the customer's notification of suspected fraud, a recall request was transmitted to the receiving institution. 

The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request but indicated that the majority of the funds had already been disbursed from the beneficiary account. The receiving institution confirmed that $11,307.00 remained in the Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. account and was subsequently frozen pending further review. The remaining $101,763.02 was no longer available for recovery. 

Information provided by the receiving institution through a 314(b) information sharing request indicated the onward movement of the funds from the Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. account. According to this information, the disbursed funds were transferred via multiple domestic wire transfers to an account held by Millpond Consulting LLC at a third domestic financial institution. The transfers to Millpond Consulting LLC occurred in rapid succession following the receipt of the initial wire from Cortex Bank and Trust. The receiving institution stated that the Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. account exhibited activity indicative of a pass-through account, with funds frequently received and immediately transferred onward with little to no residual balance maintained.

Further tracing of the funds beyond the Millpond Consulting LLC account was constrained by the limitations of the information available to Cortex Bank and Trust. A subsequent 314(b) request directed to the financial institution holding the Millpond Consulting LLC account yielded limited detail. The responding institution confirmed receipt of the funds but declined to provide specific information regarding the ultimate disposition of the funds, citing internal policy restrictions. However, the responding institution did state that the funds in the Millpond Consulting LLC account were rapidly depleted through a series of automated clearing house transactions and debit card purchases. The specific counterparties or merchants involved in these subsequent transactions were not disclosed. 

Based on the available information, the tracing of the funds concludes with their rapid dispersal from the Millpond Consulting LLC account. The movement of funds from the Adrian Yarborough account to Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd., and subsequently to Millpond Consulting LLC, occurred within a short timeframe, suggesting a coordinated effort to obfuscate the origin and destination of the funds. The use of multiple accounts and institutions further complicated the tracing process. The inability to ascertain the final destination of the funds limits the extent to which the proceeds of the suspected fraud can be fully tracked. The $11,307.00 frozen at the first receiving institution represents the only portion of the initial transfer that has been secured. The remaining $101,763.02 remains unaccounted for beyond the Millpond Consulting LLC account. The rapid movement and dissipation of the funds are consistent with typologies associated with wire fraud, where perpetrators seek to quickly move illicit proceeds beyond the reach of the originating institution and the victim. The investigation established that the entire $113,070.02 was diverted from its intended purpose.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary entity for the fraudulent transfer was identified as Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. Cortex Bank and Trust does not hold accounts for this entity. The receiving institution, located in the United Kingdom, provided limited information regarding the beneficiary account in response to a 314(b) inquiry. The account was established on March 12, 2024, approximately one month prior to the receipt of the diverted funds. The stated business purpose of Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd., according to the receiving institution, was the provision of maritime consultancy services. However, a review of open-source intelligence and corporate registries in the United Kingdom yielded no record of an active entity registered under the exact name Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. A similarly named entity, Mapleford Marine Services Ltd., was identified; however, it was registered to a different address and its directors did not match any individuals associated with the beneficiary account. The receiving institution indicated that the account opening documentation presented was consistent with a holding company structure, but the underlying operating entities were not disclosed. This discrepancy between the beneficiary name and the invoicing vendor, Copperfield Equipment Inc., is a significant indicator of potential fraud.

Analysis of the transaction history for the beneficiary account, as provided by the receiving institution, revealed a pattern of activity inconsistent with the stated business purpose of a maritime consultancy firm. The account received a low volume of incoming wire transfers, primarily originating from jurisdictions outside the United Kingdom. These incoming transfers were typically followed within a short period by outbound wire transfers of similar amounts to various international destinations. The receiving institution noted that the outbound transfers were frequently directed to accounts held in the names of individuals rather than corporate entities, which is unusual for a business-to-business consultancy firm. The rapid dissipation of funds and the lack of substantial retention of capital in the account are indicative of an account functioning primarily as a pass-through vehicle.

The specific transaction involving Adrian Yarborough's account at Cortex Bank and Trust occurred on April 11, 2024. The transfer of $113,070.02 was credited to the Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. account. The receiving institution confirmed that a significant portion of these funds was subsequently transferred out of the account in multiple transactions over the following days. On April 11, 2024, an outbound wire transfer of a mid five-figure sum was initiated to an account in the United Arab Emirates. On April 12, 2024, another transfer of a low five-figure sum was directed to an account in Hong Kong. These outbound transfers further demonstrate the pass-through nature of the account and the rapid movement of the diverted funds.

The receiving institution was able to freeze a portion of the funds associated with the fraudulent transfer. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $11,307.00. This action was taken on March 12, 2023, following communication from Cortex Bank and Trust regarding the suspected fraud. The remaining funds from the transfer had already been dissipated prior to the freeze being implemented. The transaction history provided by the receiving institution also indicated that the account was used to receive funds from other potential victims. A transfer of a high five-figure sum was received from a corporate entity in the United States on April 4, 2024, and these funds were similarly disbursed to international accounts within a few days. The pattern of receiving large, irregular sums and rapidly transferring them to various international destinations is consistent with money laundering typologies and suggests that the beneficiary account was established for the purpose of receiving and concealing illicit funds. The investigation established that the receiving entity, Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd., had no legitimate business relationship with either Adrian Yarborough or the invoiced vendor, Copperfield Equipment Inc. The use of a lookalike domain in the deceptive email correspondence further corroborates the malicious intent behind the transaction. The analysis of the beneficiary and counterparties indicates a coordinated effort to divert funds and obscure their origin and ultimate destination.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

On June 28, 2024, the relationship manager for Adrian Yarborough contacted the customer to discuss the unusual circumstances surrounding the outgoing funds transfer on June 27, 2024. During this telephone interview, the customer stated that the wire had been initiated to settle an outstanding invoice with a long-standing supplier, Copperfield Equipment Inc. The customer indicated that the payment instructions were received via email from an individual purporting to be their regular contact at Copperfield Equipment Inc. The relationship manager requested that the customer provide a copy of the email correspondence and the invoice in question.

On May 28, 2023, the relationship manager forwarded the email thread and the invoice provided by the customer to the reviewing analyst. A review of the email headers revealed that the sender's address utilized a lookalike domain name. The legitimate domain for Copperfield Equipment Inc. was known to Cortex Bank and Trust from previous, verified transactions. The domain in the email provided by the customer differed from the legitimate domain by a single character. This discrepancy had not been noted by the customer prior to initiating the transfer.

The email correspondence contained language emphasizing an urgent need for payment, citing a purported delay in the processing of a previous remittance. The communication instructed the customer to bypass their internal dual-approval control process to ensure immediate settlement. The customer confirmed during the interview that they had complied with this instruction, overriding their standard procedures to expedite the payment. The reviewing analyst noted that the circumvention of established internal controls in response to external pressure is a common indicator of social engineering tactics.

The invoice attached to the email was examined by the reviewing analyst. The invoice bore the logo and branding of Copperfield Equipment Inc. but directed payment to a beneficiary named Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. at a different financial institution. The customer stated during the interview that they had assumed Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. was a subsidiary or a newly established holding company for Copperfield Equipment Inc. The customer did not independently verify the change in beneficiary or the new account details with Copperfield Equipment Inc. through a known, trusted communication channel before initiating the wire.

The reviewing analyst also obtained the authentication logs for the customer's online banking session on June 27, 2024. The logs confirmed that the customer had successfully authenticated using their established credentials and had initiated the wire transfer. The timing of the initiation was noted; the transfer was submitted just minutes before the daily wire cutoff time for Cortex Bank and Trust. The reviewing analyst considered this timing, in conjunction with the urgency expressed in the fraudulent email, to be indicative of an attempt to limit the time available for the customer to realize the deception and for the bank to intercept the outgoing funds.

On July 2, 2024, the reviewing analyst contacted the receiving institution regarding the funds transfer to Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the funds and indicated that they had placed a hold on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account upon receiving the inquiry from Cortex Bank and Trust. The receiving institution stated that $11,307.00 was successfully frozen. The reviewing analyst requested that the receiving institution initiate the process for returning the frozen funds to Cortex Bank and Trust. The reviewing analyst also requested any available information regarding the principals or the nature of the business associated with Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. and a third entity mentioned in the receiving institution's preliminary review, Millpond Consulting LLC. The receiving institution declined to provide specific customer information without a formal legal request but confirmed that the account profile for Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd. did not appear consistent with the business operations of Copperfield Equipment Inc.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

On June 27, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust wire operations department received an inquiry from Adrian Yarborough regarding a domestic funds transfer executed on May 17, 2024. The customer reported that the intended payee, Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd., had notified the customer of an outstanding invoice balance. The customer confirmed that the May 17 funds transfer was intended to satisfy this invoice. The wire operations department confirmed that the transfer of $113,070.02 had processed successfully to the routing number and account number specified in the customer's payment instructions. The customer reviewed the payment instructions and determined that the beneficiary account details were fraudulent and did not belong to Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a formal recall request via the Fedwire network on June 27, 2024, citing fraud as the reason for the recall. The recall message requested the return of the full principal amount of $113,070.02. Concurrently, the reviewing analyst attempted to contact the receiving financial institution by telephone to expedite the freezing of the beneficiary account. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request on June 28, 2024, and initiated a review of the beneficiary account, which was held in the name of Millpond Consulting LLC.

The receiving institution responded to the recall request on May 28, 2023. The response indicated that the beneficiary account had been frozen; however, the majority of the funds transferred on May 17, 2024, had already been depleted. The receiving institution confirmed that a hold had been placed on the remaining balance in the account, which totaled $11,307.00. The receiving institution requested a formal letter of indemnity from Cortex Bank and Trust prior to releasing the frozen funds.

The Cortex Bank and Trust legal department drafted and executed the requested letter of indemnity, which was transmitted to the receiving institution on July 2, 2024. The letter of indemnity held the receiving institution harmless for the return of the frozen funds. On July 3, 2024, the receiving institution processed a return wire in the amount of $11,307.00. These funds were credited back to the account of Adrian Yarborough on the same day.

The return of the frozen funds resulted in a residual loss to the customer. The initial fraudulent transfer amount was $113,070.02. Following the recovery of $11,307.00, the unrecovered balance remained at $101,763.02. The receiving institution advised that the depleted funds had been dispersed through a series of outbound transfers and cash withdrawals shortly after the initial credit on May 17, 2024. The receiving institution did not provide specific details regarding the counterparties or destinations of these subsequent transfers, citing privacy regulations.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that an outbound wire transfer of $113,070.02 initiated by Adrian Yarborough was induced by deception. The reviewing analyst confirmed the customer intended to remit these funds to an established vendor, Copperfield Equipment Inc., but the payment instructions were altered. A review of the customer's email correspondence identified a message from a lookalike domain differing from the vendor's actual domain by one character. This communication instructed the customer to remit payment to a new beneficiary, Mapleford Marine Services Holdings Ltd., rather than the customary vendor. The fraudulent instructions included urgency language that circumvented the customer's internal dual-approval controls. The funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time. The investigation concluded that the customer did not intend to pay the beneficiary named in the altered instructions. The reviewing analyst fixed July 5, 2024 as the date the investigation determined the funds were diverted. A portion of the diverted funds was frozen at the receiving institution, resulting in a residual loss to the customer. Based on the findings of induced funds transfer by deception, the matter was referred_to_fincen.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2415
Date opened: December 6, 2024
Subject: Beatriz Sinclair (individual), account 42-45194-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: criminal_referral

## Case Summary

The Financial Intelligence Unit of Cortex Bank and Trust opened this investigation on December 6, 2024, following an escalation from the Wire Operations department. The escalation detailed a suspected business email compromise resulting in a fraudulent funds transfer. The matter involves a single customer, Beatriz Sinclair, and her Cortex Bank and Trust account ending in 45194-1. The review period for this investigation spans from July 29, 2024, to December 5, 2024. The investigation centers on an outbound wire transfer initiated from the subject account on November 14, 2024. The amount of the transfer under review is $128,222.64. The primary objective of the investigation is to determine the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire transfer and to assess the extent of the loss incurred by the customer.

Initial review of the escalation indicated that Beatriz Sinclair authorized the transfer of $128,222.64 from account ending in 45194-1. The beneficiary of the wire transfer was recorded as Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. The escalation noted that the customer contacted the bank on December 5, 2024, asserting that the transfer was unauthorized and that she had been instructed to remit funds to a different entity. The customer stated she had intended to pay an invoice submitted by Fairmount Holdings Inc. The investigation sought to verify the customer's claims regarding the intended payee and the circumstances that led to the funds being directed to Vantage Point Metals Trading Co.

The investigation reviewed the documentation provided by the customer to support the wire transfer request. The customer provided an email chain containing instructions for the remittance. The email correspondence appeared to originate from a representative of Fairmount Holdings Inc. The instructions directed the payment of $128,222.64 to an account held by Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. at a different financial institution. The customer indicated she believed the instructions were legitimate and processed the payment as requested. The reviewing analyst noted that the email address from which the instructions were sent utilized a domain name that closely resembled the legitimate domain of Fairmount Holdings Inc. The domain name in the email address differed from the legitimate domain by a single character.

The investigation also reviewed the timing of the wire transfer request. The request for the transfer of $128,222.64 was submitted by Beatriz Sinclair on November 14, 2024. The request was received by the Wire Operations department shortly before the established cutoff time for processing outgoing wire transfers for that business day. The customer's communication accompanying the request included language emphasizing the necessity for immediate processing of the payment. The customer's communication indicated that failure to remit the funds promptly would result in a disruption of a pending transaction.

Following the customer's notification of the suspected fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request for the wire transfer of $128,222.64. The receiving financial institution responded to the recall request. The receiving institution confirmed the receipt of the funds and the identity of the beneficiary account holder as Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. The receiving institution indicated that a portion of the transferred funds remained in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution successfully froze $20,515.62 of the original transfer amount. The investigation determined that the difference between the original transfer amount and the frozen amount represented the funds that had been moved from the beneficiary account prior to the recall request. The investigation established that the customer sustained a loss of $107,707.02 as a result of the transfer. The investigation sought to identify any additional counterparties or entities involved in the movement of the funds, including a review of transactions involving Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC, an entity noted in the broader account activity during the review period.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On November 14, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received a formal notification from Beatriz Sinclair, a commercial banking customer maintaining account 42-45194-1. The customer alleged that a wire transfer executed from her account on October 30, 2024, was fraudulent. The customer stated that the transfer was induced by a deceptive communication and directed funds to a beneficiary she had not intended to pay. The total amount of the outbound wire transfer subject to this allegation was $128,222.64. The customer reported that she believed she was remitting payment for a legitimate invoice but subsequently realized the payment instructions had been manipulated by an unauthorized third party.

The referral from the customer initiated an internal review by the Financial Intelligence Unit. The customer provided documentation supporting her claim, which she characterized as a business email compromise resulting in wire fraud. According to the customer's account of events, she had been in communication with an established vendor regarding an outstanding invoice. She alleged that during this communication, she received an email containing revised payment instructions, which she initially believed to be authentic. The customer stated that she directed her staff to process the payment according to these new instructions, resulting in the authorization of the wire transfer.

The customer further alleged that she only became aware of the fraud when the legitimate vendor subsequently inquired about the status of the expected payment. Upon reviewing her correspondence, the customer reported identifying discrepancies in the email address that provided the altered instructions. She immediately contacted her relationship manager at Cortex Bank and Trust to report the incident and request a recall of the funds. The customer's referral documentation included copies of the email correspondence and the original, legitimate invoice, which she presented as evidence of the deception.

The customer's allegation centered on the assertion that she was manipulated into authorizing a funds transfer that she otherwise would not have made. She claimed that the communication directing the payment to a new beneficiary account was sophisticated and designed to mimic her known vendor. The customer stated that the urgency conveyed in the fraudulent email contributed to the bypass of internal verification procedures within her own company. The referral from the customer prompted the Financial Intelligence Unit to commence a formal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the October 30, 2024, wire transfer, focusing on the potential for wire fraud as defined by the customer's account.

Following the initial notification from the customer, Cortex Bank and Trust personnel initiated immediate steps to attempt recovery of the funds. The bank's wire operations department transmitted a recall request to the receiving institution, citing the customer's allegation of fraud. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request but indicated that the funds had already been credited to the beneficiary account. The customer's referral and the subsequent actions taken by the bank formed the basis for the escalation to the Financial Intelligence Unit for a comprehensive review of the transactional activity and the associated communications.

The customer's allegation of wire fraud was treated as a high-priority matter given the substantial value of the transfer. The referral provided specific details regarding the timing and nature of the suspected compromise, which guided the initial phases of the investigation. The customer's assertion that she was the victim of a targeted deception involving altered payment instructions was the central focus of the Financial Intelligence Unit's inquiry. The investigation sought to determine the validity of the customer's claims and to assess the extent of the suspected fraudulent activity affecting account 42-45194-1.

## Timeline of Events

On July 29, 2024, Beatriz Sinclair, the sole authorized signer on Cortex Bank and Trust account 42-45194-1, initiated an email exchange with what she believed was her established supplier, Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. The reviewing analyst obtained copies of these communications from the customer during the investigation. The emails discussed an upcoming invoice for imported goods. The sender domain on the initial emails received by the customer matched the known domain for Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. However, a detailed review of the header information indicated that the return path had been manipulated to direct replies to a lookalike domain differing from the authentic domain by only one character.

The correspondence continued sporadically over the following weeks. On August 19, 2024, the customer received an email containing an invoice from the compromised email thread. The invoice requested payment for a shipment of materials. The customer stated she scheduled the payment for a later date in accordance with her usual business practices. On September 20, 2024, the customer received a follow-up email from the lookalike domain. This communication contained urgency language, stating that the previous payment instructions were no longer valid due to an impending audit and provided new wire instructions. The email stressed that the payment needed to be expedited to avoid a disruption in the supply chain. The customer indicated that the pressure tactics caused her to bypass her standard internal dual-approval control for large outgoing payments.

On September 25, 2024, the customer submitted a wire transfer request to Cortex Bank and Trust for $128,222.64. The beneficiary named on the wire request was Fairmount Holdings Inc. This beneficiary name did not match the invoicing vendor, Vantage Point Metals Trading Co., nor did it match the beneficiary on previous, legitimate wires sent to that supplier. The wire transfer was initiated minutes before the bank's daily wire cutoff time. The funds were transmitted to the receiving institution later that same day.

The customer stated she did not realize the funds had been misdirected until October 11, 2024, when she contacted Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. by telephone to inquire about the status of the shipment. The authentic vendor confirmed they had not received the payment and had not sent the September 20, 2024, email containing the altered instructions. The customer contacted Cortex Bank and Trust on October 15, 2024, to report the suspected fraud. The bank immediately initiated a wire recall request with the receiving institution.

On October 17, 2024, the receiving institution responded to the recall request. They advised that they were able to secure a portion of the funds, totaling $20,515.62, which remained in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution indicated that the remainder of the funds had already been withdrawn or transferred elsewhere. Cortex Bank and Trust informed the customer on October 30, 2024, that the remaining $107,707.02 could not be recovered through the banking system.

The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary account at the receiving institution was held by Fairmount Holdings Inc., but the investigation revealed no legitimate business connection between that entity and either the customer or Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. Further review of the account activity at the receiving institution, as communicated during the recall process, suggested that the funds were rapidly dispersed after receipt. On November 14, 2024, the customer provided a copy of a police report she had filed regarding the incident. The investigation established that the customer had been the victim of a business email compromise scheme, resulting in the diversion of funds to an unintended beneficiary.

## Funds Tracing

The funds tracing analysis began with a review of the originating transaction that induced the loss. On October 15, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust account 42-45194-1, held by Beatriz Sinclair, originated an outgoing domestic wire transfer in the amount of $128,222.64. The reviewing analyst noted that the wire transfer request was submitted via the bank's online portal at 3:45 PM, shortly before the daily wire cutoff time. The beneficiary of this transfer was identified in the wire instructions as Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. A review of the wire details indicated the beneficiary institution was a major US commercial bank. The purpose of the transfer was stated in the remittance information as payment for invoice number 88921.

A review of the customer's historical account activity showed no prior transactions with Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. Previous payments for similar invoices had been directed to Fairmount Holdings Inc. The wire request was accompanied by documentation, later determined to be fraudulent, which utilized a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the legitimate vendor's domain. Furthermore, the fraudulent communication contained urgency language that successfully bypassed the customer's internal dual-approval control for wire transfers. The funds cleared Cortex Bank and Trust on October 15, 2024, and the debit of $128,222.64 was posted to Beatriz Sinclair's account.

Subsequent to the initial transfer, the investigation focused on the onward movement of the funds. Cortex Bank and Trust issued a request for information to the beneficiary institution on October 17, 2024, under the safe harbor provisions of Section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act. The response received from the beneficiary institution on October 30, 2024, provided visibility into the disposition of the funds after they credited the Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. account.

The information received indicated that the $128,222.64 credit was immediately followed by a series of rapid, outbound transfers. Specifically, on September 12, 2023, the day after the initial credit, the Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. account originated a wire transfer to a third-party account held by Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC at a different domestic financial institution. The amount of this onward transfer represented a significant portion of the initial diverted funds. The beneficiary institution reported that this onward transfer appeared to be part of a larger pattern of pass-through activity, where incoming funds were quickly moved to secondary accounts with little to no residual balance maintained.

The beneficiary institution further disclosed that, upon receiving the indemnification request and fraud notification from Cortex Bank and Trust, they initiated an internal review and placed a hold on the Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. account. As a result of this action, the beneficiary institution was able to freeze a remaining balance of $20,515.62. This frozen amount represents a partial recovery of the initial wire transfer. The beneficiary institution indicated that they are in the process of returning these funds to Cortex Bank and Trust.

The trail of the funds beyond the transfer to Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC is not definitively documented within the scope of this investigation, as it relies on information sharing that has not yet concluded. However, based on the rapid movement of the funds and the involvement of multiple, seemingly unrelated entities, it is inferred that the funds were likely further dispersed or converted. The investigation established that the total amount diverted from Beatriz Sinclair's account was $128,222.64. After accounting for the $20,515.62 frozen at the receiving institution, the residual loss to the customer is $107,707.02. The tracing efforts confirm that the funds were successfully moved out of the Cortex Bank and Trust account and partially dispersed before intervention occurred.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The funds transfer of $128,222.64, initiated by Beatriz Sinclair, was directed to a beneficiary account held in the name of Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. at a regional financial institution. Analysis of the beneficiary information provided in the wire instructions revealed inconsistencies with the expected invoicing vendor. The customer believed the payment was settling an invoice for imported industrial equipment from a long-standing supplier, Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC. However, the beneficiary name on the executed wire was Vantage Point Metals Trading Co., an entity with no prior relationship to Beatriz Sinclair or her business operations.

Public record research into Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. indicated that the entity was incorporated in a jurisdiction known for permissive corporate registration requirements. The registration date was noted as August 19, 2024, shortly before the fraudulent transfer occurred. The registered agent address for Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. was a commercial mail receiving agency, and no physical operating location could be verified through open-source searches. The stated business purpose on the corporate filing was general trading, which provided limited insight into the specific nature of the entity's activities.

Further investigation into the beneficiary account activity was conducted through collaboration with the receiving institution. Information sharing revealed that the account for Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. was opened on September 20, 2024. The account opening documentation listed a single authorized signer, whose identity could not be corroborated through standard public record databases. The account exhibited minimal activity from its inception until the receipt of the $128,222.64 wire transfer from Beatriz Sinclair on October 11, 2024.

Following the receipt of the wire, the beneficiary account demonstrated a rapid dispersion of funds. On October 15, 2024, a significant portion of the funds was transferred via an outbound wire to another domestic financial institution. The beneficiary of this subsequent transfer was Fairmount Holdings Inc. Public record research into Fairmount Holdings Inc. showed it was incorporated on September 25, 2024, and also utilized a commercial mail receiving agency as its registered address. The rapid movement of funds to a recently established entity with a similar opaque corporate structure is consistent with attempts to obfuscate the flow of illicit proceeds.

Additional analysis of the Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. account revealed a pattern of smaller, structured cash withdrawals occurring between October 17, 2024, and October 30, 2024. These withdrawals, typically in amounts just below the currency transaction reporting threshold, appeared designed to evade regulatory scrutiny. The rapid depletion of the account balance following the initial large credit is a common characteristic of accounts utilized to receive and launder fraudulent funds.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request for the $128,222.64 wire transfer upon notification of the suspected fraud. The receiving institution confirmed the receipt of the recall request and placed a hold on the remaining balance in the Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. account. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $20,515.62. This left a residual loss of $107,707.02 associated with the fraudulent transfer.

The investigation identified no legitimate business purpose for the transfer of funds from Beatriz Sinclair to Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. The discrepancy between the expected vendor, Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC, and the actual beneficiary, combined with the recently established nature of the receiving entity and the rapid dispersion of funds, strongly supports the conclusion that the transaction was fraudulent. The involvement of Fairmount Holdings Inc. as a secondary recipient further indicates a coordinated effort to move and conceal the diverted funds. The use of a lookalike sender domain and urgency language in the fraudulent instructions, which successfully bypassed the customer's internal controls, underscores the sophistication of the scheme. The transfer was initiated late in the business day, minutes before the wire cutoff, a tactic often employed to limit the window for intervention or recall.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

Bank staff interviewed Beatriz Sinclair on October 30, 2024, by telephone to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the suspect wire transfer. Sinclair stated that she believed she was remitting funds to a known supplier, Vantage Point Metals Trading Co., for an outstanding invoice. She provided the reviewing analyst with copies of the email correspondence she relied upon, which included the invoice in question and the payment instructions. Sinclair confirmed that she had initiated the transfer based solely on this communication and had not attempted to verify the new beneficiary account details by an alternative method, such as a phone call to a known contact at the vendor.

The email correspondence provided by Sinclair was subjected to technical review. The initial communication appeared to originate from a contact at Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. However, examination of the email headers revealed that the sender's domain was a lookalike, differing from the legitimate vendor domain by a single character. This spoofed domain had been registered shortly before the initial contact. The correspondence included an invoice that closely resembled the vendor's standard billing format, although the reviewing analyst noted minor discrepancies in the font and alignment compared to historical invoices held on file.

The payment instructions provided in the fraudulent email directed the remittance of $128,222.64 to an account held in the name of Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC at another financial institution. Sinclair stated during the interview that she had not previously conducted business with an entity bearing this name. The email contained language urging immediate payment, citing a purported delay in the shipment of goods until the funds cleared. Sinclair indicated that this urgency prompted her to bypass internal procedures that typically require dual approval for transfers exceeding a certain threshold.

Review of the bank's authentication logs confirmed that the wire transfer request was submitted through the online banking portal using Sinclair's legitimate credentials. The logs indicated that the session originated from an IP address consistent with her historical access patterns. The transfer request was submitted minutes before the bank's daily wire cutoff time.

A review of the account history for Sinclair's account, 42-45194-1, identified prior, legitimate transactions involving Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. These historical remittances were consistently directed to an account held in the vendor's name at a different financial institution than the one specified in the fraudulent instructions. There was no record of prior transactions with either Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC or Fairmount Holdings Inc.

Following the identification of the suspected fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request through the wire network. The receiving institution responded, indicating that a portion of the funds had already been withdrawn or transferred from the beneficiary account. The receiving institution confirmed that a hold had been placed on the remaining balance of $20,515.62. Sinclair was informed of the partial recovery and the residual loss of $107,707.02.

A review of publicly available information regarding Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC yielded limited results. The entity was registered as a limited liability company in the jurisdiction where the beneficiary account was held, but no active business operations or physical storefront could be identified. The address associated with the registration appeared to be a residential property. Similar searches regarding Fairmount Holdings Inc., an entity referenced in the memo line of the fraudulent invoice, did not identify a legitimate business presence. No connection could be established between these entities and the legitimate vendor, Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. The documentary evidence and the customer interview indicate that the customer was induced by a deceptive communication to remit funds to an unintended beneficiary.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

On October 17, 2024, the reviewing analyst submitted a formal request for indemnification to the beneficiary financial institution. This request detailed the fraudulent nature of the $128,222.64 wire transfer initiated from the account of Beatriz Sinclair on October 15, 2024. The request sought the return of the full amount, citing the deceptive circumstances under which the funds were induced. Communication with the receiving institution indicated that the beneficiary account was held in the name of Fairmount Holdings Inc. The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the indemnity request on the same day.

The receiving institution confirmed on October 30, 2024, that they had successfully frozen $20,515.62 remaining in the beneficiary account associated with Fairmount Holdings Inc. The response noted that the remaining funds from the initial wire transfer had already been disbursed prior to the receipt of the indemnification request. The investigation determined that the disbursed funds had been transferred to secondary accounts, which were identified in the receiving institution's communication as belonging to Vantage Point Metals Trading Co. and Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC. The receiving institution stated they were unable to recall the funds that had already cleared their institution.

Following the confirmation of the frozen amount, the reviewing analyst initiated the process to have the $20,515.62 returned to Cortex Bank and Trust. The receiving institution required a signed hold harmless agreement before releasing the frozen funds. This agreement was executed by Cortex Bank and Trust on November 14, 2024. The return of the frozen funds was processed, and the amount was credited back to the account of Beatriz Sinclair.

The investigation established that the residual loss to the customer was $107,707.02, representing the difference between the original fraudulent wire amount and the funds successfully recovered. Cortex Bank and Trust management reviewed the circumstances surrounding the loss to determine the bank's liability. The review considered the fact that the customer had authorized the wire transfer, albeit under deceptive conditions, and that the bank's internal controls were bypassed due to the urgency language employed by the threat actor, which successfully overrode the dual-approval control.

The customer asserted that the bank should bear the loss, arguing that the beneficiary name, Fairmount Holdings Inc., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, which the customer believed they were paying. The customer also highlighted the lookalike sender domain used in the email communication, which differed by only one character from the legitimate vendor's domain. The bank's review noted that the funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff, a common tactic in such schemes to limit the time available for review and recall.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Beatriz Sinclair authorized a wire transfer of $128,222.64 on October 30, 2024, believing she was settling a legitimate invoice with Stonebridge Imports Enterprises LLC. Cortex Bank and Trust records indicate the transfer was executed minutes before the daily wire cutoff. The beneficiary name on the transfer instructions, however, was Vantage Point Metals Trading Co., which did not match the name on the underlying invoice. The customer stated she received the payment instructions via email. Review of the email correspondence provided by the customer revealed a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the known vendor domain, and language urging immediate payment, which the customer cited as the reason for overriding her established dual-approval control. The receiving institution successfully froze a portion of the funds, leaving a residual loss to the customer of $107,707.02. The activity is consistent with wire fraud, wherein funds are induced out of a customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay. Based on the findings, the investigation concluded on November 20, 2024, and the disposition was recorded as criminal_referral.

An internal referral was received by the Financial Intelligence Unit on May 27, 2024, regarding a suspected wire fraud incident involving Cortex Bank and Trust customer Marblehead Logistics LLC.
