The customer provided documentation to the relationship manager suggesting the payment instructions had been manipulated. The Financial Intelligence Unit opened an investigation to determine if the customer had been the victim of a business email compromise or similar scheme, resulting in the diversion of funds.

The referral detailed a single outbound wire transfer in the amount of $1,661,068.92, executed on May 20, 2024. The investigation sought to establish the circumstances surrounding this transfer, specifically whether the instructions originated from an authorized representative of Marblehead Logistics LLC or a malicious actor who had gained unauthorized access to the customer's communication channels. The primary objective was to ascertain the legitimacy of the beneficiary information provided in the wire instructions and to trace the movement of the funds, if possible, to aid in recovery efforts. The investigation was tasked with reviewing the communication history leading up to the transfer, the authorization process employed by the customer, and the details of the beneficiary account to identify any indicators of fraud or deception.

The customer, Marblehead Logistics LLC, is a commercial entity utilizing Cortex Bank and Trust for general operating purposes. The account in question, 73-44458-1, is a standard commercial checking account subject to routine transaction monitoring. The referral noted that the transaction amount of $1,661,068.92 was unusually large compared to the customer's historical transaction profile, prompting further scrutiny. The investigation focused on the period leading up to the May 20, 2024 transfer to identify any preceding events or communications that might have facilitated the suspected fraud. The review period for this investigation was defined as February 8, 2024, through June 6, 2024, to encompass a sufficient timeframe for analyzing historical account activity and subsequent developments.

The initial assessment of the referral highlighted several areas of concern requiring further investigation. The customer's assertion that the intended vendor, Crescent Equipment Inc., had not received payment despite the funds leaving the Cortex Bank and Trust account suggested a potential misdirection of funds. The investigation needed to verify the beneficiary details associated with the executed wire transfer and compare them against the customer's intended payee. Furthermore, the investigation aimed to analyze the method by which the wire instructions were transmitted to the bank and the authentication procedures followed, to determine if any internal or external controls had been circumvented or compromised. The ultimate goal of the investigation was to establish a factual sequence of events leading to the transfer, identify any control failures or vulnerabilities, and support any potential recovery actions for the diverted funds.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On May 27, 2024, an incoming telephone call to the Cortex Bank and Trust commercial services desk reported a suspected wire fraud incident affecting a business account. The caller identified himself as the chief financial officer of Marblehead Logistics LLC. The caller stated that the company had authorized a wire transfer on May 20, 2024, intended to settle an outstanding invoice with an established vendor. The intended beneficiary of the transfer was stated to be Crescent Equipment Inc. The caller reported that Crescent Equipment Inc. had subsequently contacted Marblehead Logistics LLC to inquire about the status of the unpaid invoice. This contact prompted an internal review by Marblehead Logistics LLC of the payment instructions used for the May 20, 2024 transfer.

The caller informed the commercial services desk that the internal review had identified a discrepancy in the email correspondence that provided the payment instructions. The caller stated that the email containing the wire instructions appeared to have originated from a representative of Crescent Equipment Inc., but upon closer inspection, the sender's domain name differed from the vendor's actual domain name by a single character. The caller asserted that Marblehead Logistics LLC had been deceived into transmitting funds to an unauthorized recipient. The caller requested that Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiate a recall of the wire transfer. The commercial services desk escalated the report to the Financial Intelligence Unit for investigation under internal case reference FIU-WIRE-2416.

The Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a review of the transaction history for the Marblehead Logistics LLC account, number 73-44458-1. The review confirmed that a wire transfer was executed from the account on May 20, 2024. The amount of the outbound wire transfer was $1,661,068.92. The transaction records indicated that the beneficiary of the transfer was a corporate entity. The beneficiary name recorded on the wire transfer instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Crescent Equipment Inc., as reported by the customer. The review period for this investigation was established as February 8, 2024 through June 6, 2024, to encompass the period leading up to the transaction and to allow for the monitoring of any subsequent related activity. The initial assessment of the referral indicated that the activity was consistent with a business email compromise scheme resulting in the fraudulent diversion of funds. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the May 20, 2024 wire transfer and the subsequent efforts to recover the funds remains ongoing.

## Timeline of Events

On February 8, 2024, the relationship manager for Marblehead Logistics LLC documented a routine service call, noting no unusual circumstances. The customer profile indicated regular vendor payments via wire, typically requiring dual authorization by the controller and the chief financial officer.

Review of the customer’s electronic correspondence, provided subsequent to discovery of the loss, established that a communication purporting to be from a known vendor, Crescent Equipment Inc., was received by the controller of Marblehead Logistics LLC on March 6, 2024. Analysis of the message headers by the Cortex Bank and Trust information security team confirmed that the sender domain, while closely resembling the established vendor domain, differed by a single, visually similar character. The email directed that all future payments to Crescent Equipment Inc. be routed to a newly established account at a different financial institution. A forged invoice, identical in format to previous legitimate invoices from Crescent Equipment Inc., was attached. The invoice date was March 15, 2024.

On March 25, 2024, the controller for Marblehead Logistics LLC received a subsequent email from the lookalike domain. The message contained language emphasizing urgency and citing potential supply chain disruptions if payment was not expedited. The message directed immediate payment of the March 15, 2024, invoice to the previously provided alternate account instructions.

On March 26, 2024, a wire transfer request was submitted through the Cortex Bank and Trust commercial banking portal on behalf of Marblehead Logistics LLC. The beneficiary listed on the payment instructions was Crescent Imports Corp., rather than Crescent Equipment Inc., which was the entity invoiced. The wire transfer request bypassed the standard dual-approval control, a deviation attributed by the customer during a later interview to the urgency expressed in the March 25, 2024, communication. The wire transfer in the amount of $1,661,068.92 was initiated at 4:51 PM EST, minutes prior to the Cortex Bank and Trust daily wire cutoff time. The funds were transmitted to the receiving institution.

On April 12, 2024, Marblehead Logistics LLC contacted their relationship manager at Cortex Bank and Trust, reporting that Crescent Equipment Inc. had inquired about the overdue payment for the March 15, 2024, invoice. Upon review of the payment confirmation details, the controller for Marblehead Logistics LLC recognized that the funds had been routed according to the instructions provided in the fraudulent emails received from the lookalike domain. Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated a recall request through the wire network to the receiving institution.

On May 8, 2024, the receiving institution responded to the recall request, indicating that the account held in the name of Crescent Imports Corp. had been depleted, with the exception of a residual balance. The receiving institution confirmed that a hold had been placed on the remaining funds, which totaled $265,771.03. The remaining $1,395,297.89 of the original $1,661,068.92 transfer had been dissipated prior to the receipt of the recall request.

The relationship manager documented a subsequent conversation with the principals of Marblehead Logistics LLC on May 20, 2024. During this discussion, the customer confirmed that they had no established business relationship with Crescent Imports Corp. and that the payment was intended solely for Crescent Equipment Inc. A review of historical transaction activity for Marblehead Logistics LLC revealed no prior payments to Crescent Imports Corp., nor any interactions with the entity named Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC, which appeared in open-source research associated with the address provided for Crescent Imports Corp. The matter was escalated to the Financial Intelligence Unit for formal investigation on May 27, 2024.

## Funds Tracing

The originating transaction occurred on March 25, 2024. A debit posted to the Cortex Bank and Trust operating account held by Marblehead Logistics LLC in the amount of $1,661,068.92. This sum represented the entirety of the diverted funds. The transaction was executed as a domestic wire transfer. The beneficiary institution was identified as a regional commercial bank based in the Midwest. The beneficiary name provided on the wire instructions was Crescent Imports Corp. The customer records provided to Cortex Bank and Trust indicated that the intended recipient of this payment was an established vendor, Crescent Equipment Inc., for the purchase of specialized loading machinery.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a trace request with the beneficiary institution on March 26, 2024. The beneficiary institution confirmed receipt of the $1,661,068.92 wire transfer. The receiving account was held in the name of Crescent Imports Corp. The beneficiary institution indicated that the account had been opened recently and exhibited limited historical activity prior to the receipt of these funds.

Subsequent tracing efforts revealed immediate onward movement of the funds from the Crescent Imports Corp. account. The beneficiary institution reported that the majority of the funds were disbursed via multiple outbound wire transfers within forty-eight hours of receipt. A significant portion of the diverted funds was transferred to an account held by Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC at a different domestic financial institution. The beneficiary institution was unable to provide the specific amount transferred to Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC, citing information sharing restrictions, but characterized it as a low seven-figure sum.

The remaining balance in the Crescent Imports Corp. account was depleted through a series of smaller transfers and withdrawals. The beneficiary institution reported several automated clearing house debits directed to various unnamed payment processors and cryptocurrency exchanges. The aggregate value of these automated clearing house transactions was described as a mid six-figure sum. The specific destinations and ultimate beneficiaries of these automated clearing house transactions could not be determined from the information provided by the beneficiary institution.

Further tracing of the funds transferred to Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC proved challenging. Cortex Bank and Trust submitted a formal information sharing request to the institution holding the Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC account. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the funds from Crescent Imports Corp. However, they reported that the funds were rapidly disbursed through a complex web of transactions, including international wire transfers to jurisdictions known for limited financial transparency. The receiving institution indicated that a substantial portion of the funds was converted into foreign currency and transferred to accounts in Southeast Asia. The precise amounts and final destinations of these international transfers remain unverified.

On April 12, 2024, the beneficiary institution holding the Crescent Imports Corp. account notified Cortex Bank and Trust that they had successfully frozen a portion of the diverted funds. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $265,771.03. These funds were secured following a review of the account activity and the identification of the suspicious transfer patterns. The beneficiary institution indicated that the frozen funds represented the remaining balance in the Crescent Imports Corp. account after the initial wave of disbursements.

The recovery of the frozen funds is pending further coordination between Cortex Bank and Trust, the beneficiary institution, and law enforcement agencies. The residual loss to the customer currently stands at $1,395,297.89. The trail for this remaining amount ends with the international transfers executed from the Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC account and the automated clearing house debits directed to cryptocurrency exchanges from the Crescent Imports Corp. account. The ultimate disposition of these funds is inferred to be integration into the broader financial system or conversion into digital assets, rendering further tracing efforts highly complex and unlikely to yield significant recoveries.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The investigation focused on the receiving entity associated with the fraudulent outbound wire amount of $1,661,068.92. This transfer, executed on March 26, 2024, designated Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC as the beneficiary. Review of the payment instructions revealed a discrepancy between the beneficiary name and the vendor typically invoiced by Marblehead Logistics LLC. Historical records indicated that Marblehead Logistics LLC engaged in regular transactions with Crescent Equipment Inc., a supplier of heavy machinery. The March 26, 2024 transfer was directed to Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC, an entity with no prior transaction history with the subject.

Information obtained regarding the receiving account held by Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC indicated that the account was established recently, with the opening date closely preceding the receipt of the fraudulent transfer. The stated business purpose for Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC, as recorded by the receiving institution, was described as management consulting services. This stated purpose appeared inconsistent with the anticipated business activities of Crescent Equipment Inc., the intended recipient of the funds according to the subject's internal records.

Public record research conducted on Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC yielded limited information. A review of state business registries identified a filing for Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC, but the registration date was recent, aligning with the account opening timeframe. No significant web presence or advertising materials were located for the entity. The lack of an established operational history or digital footprint is consistent with characteristics often observed in entities utilized to facilitate the receipt and dispersal of illicit funds.

Further analysis of the counterparties involved revealed that the fraudulent instructions received by Marblehead Logistics LLC originated from a lookalike sender domain. The email address utilized to transmit the altered payment instructions closely resembled the legitimate domain associated with Crescent Equipment Inc., differing by only one character. This deceptive tactic, combined with urgency language overriding the dual-approval control, facilitated the redirection of the funds. The transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff on March 26, 2024, a timing often associated with attempts to limit the window for identifying and intercepting fraudulent activity.

While the full transaction history of the receiving account held by Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC was not available to Cortex Bank and Trust, information provided by the receiving institution during the recall process indicated rapid dissipation of funds following the receipt of the $1,661,068.92 transfer. A portion of the funds, amounting to $265,771.03, was successfully frozen at the receiving institution. The rapid outbound movement of the remaining funds is consistent with efforts to distance the proceeds from the initial fraudulent transfer.

The investigation also identified Crescent Imports Corp. as an entity related to the legitimate vendor, Crescent Equipment Inc. A review of historical transactions on the account of Marblehead Logistics LLC did not reveal any prior payments to Crescent Imports Corp. However, the presence of related entities within the vendor's corporate structure highlights the complexity of the business relationships and the potential for confusion when verifying payment instructions.

The analysis of the beneficiary and counterparties suggests that Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC was utilized as a conduit for the diverted funds. The recent establishment of the entity, the lack of an established operational history, and the rapid dissipation of funds following the receipt of the transfer are indicators of potential involvement in the movement of illicit proceeds. The use of a lookalike domain and urgency language further supports the assessment that the transfer was induced by deception. The residual loss to the customer, after accounting for the frozen funds, was determined to be $1,395,297.89. The investigation into the movement of the dispersed funds and the potential involvement of other counterparties remains ongoing.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The investigation relied on interviews with Cortex Bank and Trust personnel and principals of Marblehead Logistics LLC, supplemented by a review of authentication logs, email correspondence, and vendor invoices. The relationship manager responsible for the Marblehead Logistics LLC account was interviewed on May 27, 2024. The relationship manager indicated that the principal of Marblehead Logistics LLC had described an intent to remit funds to a regular vendor, Crescent Equipment Inc., for a large machinery purchase. The relationship manager noted that the customer had not previously executed a transaction of this magnitude. The relationship manager further stated that the customer had expressed frustration with the bank's dual-approval control for wire transfers, citing a need for expedited processing to secure the equipment purchase. 

The principal of Marblehead Logistics LLC was interviewed by telephone on May 27, 2024. The principal confirmed the intent to pay Crescent Equipment Inc. and stated that the payment instructions were received via email. The principal provided the reviewing analyst with a copy of the email correspondence, which contained an invoice purportedly from Crescent Equipment Inc. The principal stated that the email correspondence was initiated by an individual known to the principal as a representative of Crescent Equipment Inc. The principal could not explain why the beneficiary name on the provided payment instructions did not match the vendor name. The principal confirmed that the wire transfer was initiated on May 8, 2024, and that the funds were subsequently debited from the Cortex Bank and Trust account. 

A review of the email correspondence provided by the principal of Marblehead Logistics LLC revealed that the sender's domain name differed from the legitimate domain name of Crescent Equipment Inc. by a single character. The email correspondence contained language emphasizing the urgency of the transaction, which appears to have been intended to circumvent the customer's internal dual-approval control. The email directed the customer to remit funds to an account held in the name of Crescent Imports Corp. The customer was unable to substantiate a legitimate business relationship with Crescent Imports Corp. 

The investigation obtained copies of previous invoices submitted by Crescent Equipment Inc. to Marblehead Logistics LLC. A comparison of the legitimate invoices with the invoice provided in the email correspondence revealed discrepancies in formatting and contact information. The beneficiary name on the legitimate invoices was Crescent Equipment Inc., whereas the beneficiary name on the fraudulent invoice was Crescent Imports Corp. 

Authentication logs for the Marblehead Logistics LLC account were reviewed for the period of February 8, 2024 through June 6, 2024. The logs indicated that the wire transfer on May 8, 2024, was initiated utilizing the credentials of the principal of Marblehead Logistics LLC. The logs also showed that the wire transfer was initiated minutes before the bank's wire cutoff time. The timing of the transaction is consistent with an attempt to limit the bank's ability to review and potentially interdict the transfer. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer's account profile did not indicate a history of initiating wire transfers near the cutoff time. 

The investigation obtained records pertaining to the receiving account held in the name of Crescent Imports Corp. The records indicated that the account was established shortly before the fraudulent transfer occurred. The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary account activity was not consistent with the stated business purpose of Crescent Imports Corp. A significant portion of the funds received into the account were subsequently transferred to an entity identified as Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC. No legitimate business purpose was identified for the transfers to Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC. 

The investigation established that the customer was induced by deception to remit funds to a beneficiary they never intended to pay. The total amount diverted was $1,661,068.92. The receiving institution was able to freeze a portion of the funds, totaling $265,771.03. The residual loss to the customer was determined to be $1,395,297.89.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Upon confirming the unauthorized nature of the transfer, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated immediate recovery efforts. A recall request was transmitted to the receiving institution via the wire network messaging system, citing fraud as the reason for the recall and requesting the immediate freeze and return of the funds sent by Marblehead Logistics LLC. This action was taken on the same day the fraud was reported by the customer. Cortex Bank and Trust also issued a formal hold harmless agreement to the receiving institution, indemnifying them against claims arising from the return of the funds. The reviewing analyst contacted the receiving institution's fraud department by telephone to escalate the request and emphasize the urgency of securing the transferred amount.

The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the recall request and the indemnity agreement. Following their internal review, they confirmed that the beneficiary account, held in the name of Crescent Equipment Inc., had been frozen. However, the receiving institution reported that a significant portion of the funds had already been disbursed prior to the freeze being implemented. They indicated that the funds had been moved through a series of rapid outgoing transfers to other entities, including accounts in the names of Quarrystone Consulting Group LLC and Crescent Imports Corp. The receiving institution stated they were attempting to trace these subsequent transfers but could not guarantee recovery.

Cortex Bank and Trust was informed by the receiving institution that $265,771.03 remained in the beneficiary account at the time the freeze was executed. These funds were secured and held pending the completion of the receiving institution's internal procedures for returning funds under a fraud claim. The receiving institution indicated that the return of this specific amount would be processed in accordance with their standard timelines for such matters. Cortex Bank and Trust continued to monitor the status of this return closely, maintaining regular communication with the receiving institution to expedite the process wherever possible.

Despite the successful freeze of a portion of the transferred funds, the majority of the original wire amount could not be immediately recovered. The residual loss to Marblehead Logistics LLC, representing the difference between the initial fraudulent transfer and the amount secured at the receiving institution, was calculated at $1,395,297.89. This figure was communicated to the customer, along with a detailed explanation of the recovery efforts undertaken and the limitations encountered. The relationship manager advised the customer that recovery of the remaining funds was highly uncertain and dependent on the outcome of investigations by other institutions and law enforcement.

Cortex Bank and Trust reviewed the circumstances of the fraud against the bank's internal policies regarding customer reimbursement. The investigation determined that the fraudulent transfer was initiated based on instructions received by the customer through a compromised email channel, featuring a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from a legitimate vendor. The instructions also included urgency language that appeared designed to override the customer's internal dual-approval controls. The investigation further noted that the beneficiary name, Crescent Equipment Inc., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, and the transfer was initiated minutes before the bank's wire cutoff time.

Based on these findings, Cortex Bank and Trust concluded that the customer had authorized the transfer, albeit under false pretenses created by a third party. The bank's policies stipulate that in cases of authorized push payment fraud, where the customer initiates the transaction based on deceptive instructions, the bank is generally not liable for the loss. Therefore, Cortex Bank and Trust determined that it would not reimburse Marblehead Logistics LLC for the residual loss. The customer was informed of this decision and advised to pursue potential recovery through their own commercial insurance policies, specifically those covering cybercrime or business email compromise. Cortex Bank and Trust offered to provide any necessary documentation or information to support the customer's insurance claim. The investigation remains ongoing as the bank continues to monitor for the return of the frozen funds and cooperates with any external inquiries.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that a single fraudulent outbound wire transfer was induced by a compromised business email compromise scheme. On May 24, 2024, the customer, Marblehead Logistics LLC, received an email appearing to originate from a known vendor, Crescent Imports Corp., instructing payment for a recently issued invoice. The sender domain in the email differed from the vendor's actual domain by one character. The email utilized language conveying urgency, which resulted in the customer overriding their internal dual-approval control for wire transfers. The customer subsequently initiated a wire transfer in the amount of $1,661,068.92, which was executed minutes before the daily wire cutoff time. The beneficiary of the wire transfer was listed as Crescent Equipment Inc., an entity with no known relationship to the customer or the invoicing vendor. Subsequent review confirmed the funds were directed to an account controlled by unknown actors. A portion of the funds was successfully frozen at the receiving institution, mitigating the total loss to the customer. The investigation into the incident and potential recovery efforts remains ongoing.

## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2417
Date opened: April 17, 2024
Subject: Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC (business), account 77-76418-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: closed_no_action

## Case Summary

The Financial Intelligence Unit initiated this review following a referral from the commercial banking relationship manager on February 5, 2024. The referral concerned Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC, which maintains operating account 77-76418-1 at Cortex Bank and Trust. The relationship manager reported that the customer had been the victim of a business email compromise event, resulting in a misdirected wire transfer of $574,350.56. The objective of the investigation was to establish the circumstances of the diversion, trace the flow of funds where possible, and determine whether the incident indicated broader vulnerabilities in the customer's payment initiation processes or potential complicity by internal actors at the subject entity. The review covered activity between December 7, 2023, and March 29, 2024, focusing on the communication and authorization sequence that led to the execution of the fraudulent payment.

The initial report from the relationship manager indicated that Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC had intended to remit the $574,350.56 to an established vendor, Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, for the purchase of specialized manufacturing equipment. The customer stated that they had received an invoice via email that appeared to be from their usual contact at Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC. The relationship manager noted that the customer had not identified any discrepancies in the email communication at the time the invoice was received. The referral detailed that the funds were wired on January 18, 2024. The customer became aware of the diversion on January 30, 2024, when Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC contacted them regarding the outstanding balance on the equipment purchase. The customer subsequently reviewed the payment details and realized the funds had been routed to an account held by Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., an entity with no known business relationship to Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC.

Upon receiving the referral, the reviewing analyst secured the customer's account records and requested copies of the correspondence related to the transaction. The investigation sought to confirm the details provided by the customer and to identify the specific mechanism by which the fraud was perpetrated. The analyst reviewed the wire transfer authorization records to determine whether Cortex Bank and Trust's authentication protocols were followed. The review also examined the customer's historical payment activity to Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC to establish a baseline for comparison. The analyst noted that the customer had previously executed multiple high-value wire transfers to Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC without incident. The investigation focused on identifying the point of compromise, whether it occurred within the customer's email environment, the vendor's systems, or through a broader phishing campaign targeting the manufacturing sector.

The analyst initiated contact with the receiving institution that held the account for Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. A request was submitted to freeze any remaining funds derived from the January 18, 2024 wire transfer. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the request and later reported that $45,948.04 had been successfully frozen in the beneficiary account. The remaining balance of the transferred funds had already been disbursed prior to the freeze request. The investigation therefore proceeded with the understanding that the customer faced a residual loss of $528,402.52. The analyst documented the communications with the receiving institution and began compiling the evidence necessary to analyze the deceptive tactics employed by the threat actors. The review of the email correspondence provided by the customer was prioritized to identify the specific indicators of compromise that led to the unauthorized diversion of the $574,350.56.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The investigation into Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC was initiated following a customer escalation to a Cortex Bank and Trust relationship manager on February 23, 2024. The relationship manager submitted an internal referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit on the same date, stating that the customer believed they had been the victim of a sophisticated business email compromise scheme. According to the referral, the customer alleged that a fraudulent outbound wire in the amount of $574,350.56 had been authorized and transmitted based on deceptive email instructions. The customer claimed they had intended to remit payment to a known vendor, Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., but the funds were instead directed to an unknown entity.

The internal referral detailed that the customer's accounts payable department had received an email appearing to originate from Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., providing updated wiring instructions for an outstanding invoice. The customer stated that this email was received on January 18, 2024, and the funds transfer was subsequently initiated on January 19, 2024. The relationship manager noted that the customer had not realized the funds were misdirected until February 5, 2024, when Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. contacted them regarding the unpaid invoice. The customer asserted that a review of the communication revealed the email directing the payment had originated from a lookalike sender domain, differing from the vendor's actual domain by a single character.

The referral further indicated that the customer’s internal investigation identified that the email containing the fraudulent instructions included urgency language. This language reportedly pressured the accounts payable employee to bypass the established dual-approval control for wire transfers, a process typically required for transactions exceeding the customer's internal thresholds. The customer also reported that the beneficiary name on the fraudulent wiring instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. Instead, the instructions directed funds to Anvil Ventures Corp. The customer claimed they had no prior business relationship with Anvil Ventures Corp. and that this entity was not an authorized payee.

In addition to the customer's allegations, the internal referral noted that the funds transfer was initiated minutes before the Cortex Bank and Trust wire cutoff time on January 19, 2024. The relationship manager stated that upon being notified by the customer of the suspected fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated a wire recall request to the receiving institution. The referral indicated that the receiving institution was able to secure a portion of the funds, reporting an amount frozen at the receiving institution of $45,948.04. However, the remaining funds had already been dispersed or withdrawn prior to the receipt of the recall notice.

The internal referral concluded by stating that the customer was seeking to recover the residual loss to the customer, which was calculated as $528,402.52. The relationship manager requested that the Financial Intelligence Unit conduct a comprehensive review of the transaction and the circumstances surrounding the authorization of the wire transfer to determine if further action or reporting was warranted. The referral also noted that the customer had been advised to file a report with local law enforcement and the appropriate federal authorities regarding the suspected business email compromise. The Financial Intelligence Unit commenced its review of the transaction and the associated account activity for Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC upon receipt of this internal referral.

## Timeline of Events

The timeline established by the investigation began on January 2, 2024, when the customer's accounts payable department received an email appearing to originate from their established vendor, Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC. A review of the email headers later revealed that the sending domain utilized a lookalike strategy, differing from the legitimate Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC domain by a single transposed character. The communication contained an invoice for industrial equipment along with updated payment instructions, directing a wire transfer of $574,350.56 to a new account held by Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. The email included urgency language, asserting that the equipment delivery would be delayed if payment was not received that day.

On the same date, January 2, 2024, an employee in the customer's accounts payable department, acting on the urgency language in the fraudulent email, initiated the wire transfer of $574,350.56. The investigation noted that the transfer was submitted just minutes before the daily wire cutoff time. Furthermore, the employee bypassed the customer's established dual-approval control for outbound wire transfers, a deviation from standard operating procedure that the customer later attributed to the perceived time sensitivity of the request. The funds were transmitted to the account held by Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., as directed in the fraudulent instructions.

The discrepancy was discovered on January 18, 2024, when the legitimate vendor, Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, contacted the customer regarding the outstanding invoice. The customer realized that the payment of $574,350.56 had not been received by the intended party and subsequently identified the fraudulent nature of the January 2 email. The customer notified Cortex Bank and Trust of the suspected fraud on January 19, 2024.

Upon receiving notification from the customer, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated a recall request to the receiving institution. Concurrently, the Financial Intelligence Unit commenced an investigation into the transaction. The receiving institution responded to the recall request on January 30, 2024, indicating that they were able to freeze $45,948.04 of the funds remaining in the Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. account. The receiving institution confirmed that the balance of the $574,350.56 transfer had already been withdrawn or transferred elsewhere prior to the receipt of the recall request.

The investigation subsequently focused on tracing the movement of the funds prior to the freeze. Analysis of account records provided by the receiving institution revealed that a portion of the funds had been transferred to an entity identified as Anvil Ventures Corp. The customer stated they had no prior business relationship with Anvil Ventures Corp., and no legitimate business purpose for this transfer could be established. The customer was advised of the partial recovery of $45,948.04 and the residual loss of $528,402.52 on February 5, 2024. The investigation determined that the beneficiary name on the fraudulent wire instructions, Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, a red flag that was not identified by the customer's accounts payable department prior to the initiation of the transfer.

## Funds Tracing

The outbound wire transfer under review was initiated against the Cortex Bank and Trust account held by Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC on February 5, 2024. The transfer amount was $574,350.56. Documentation provided by the customer indicated the funds were intended for Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, a known vendor. However, the wire instructions provided by the fraudster directed the funds to an account held in the name of Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. at a different financial institution. The debit to the Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC account was processed successfully, and the funds were transmitted via the Fedwire system.

Tracing the onward movement of the funds required coordination with the receiving institution. Upon receipt of the $574,350.56 wire on February 5, 2024, the receiving institution credited the account held by Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. Analysis of the account activity at the receiving institution, provided under a USA PATRIOT Act Section 314(b) information sharing request, revealed that the funds did not remain in the account for long.

On February 6, 2024, the day following the initial credit, a series of rapid, high-value transfers commenced. The receiving institution reported that a significant portion of the funds, a mid-six-figure sum, was transferred via domestic wire to another account held by Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. at a third financial institution. This rapid movement of funds is a common indicator of attempts to obfuscate the money trail and complicate recovery efforts.

Further analysis of the Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. account at the second receiving institution showed continued dissipation of the funds. Over the next several days, multiple smaller wire transfers, each involving tens of thousands of dollars, were sent to various domestic and international beneficiaries. One notable transfer involved a low six-figure sum directed to an account held by Anvil Ventures Corp., an entity with no apparent business relationship to Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC or Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC. The purpose of these transfers could not be definitively established, but the pattern is consistent with the layering phase of money laundering.

In addition to the wire transfers, a portion of the funds at the second receiving institution was used to purchase several cashier's checks. These checks, totaling a low six-figure sum, were made payable to individuals and entities that could not be identified through public records or commercially available databases. The conversion of funds into cashier's checks further obscures the audit trail and facilitates the anonymous movement of value.

The receiving institution where the initial $574,350.56 wire was sent managed to freeze a portion of the funds remaining in the Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. account. The amount frozen was $45,948.04. However, the majority of the funds had already been dispersed before the freeze could be implemented.

The trail of the funds effectively ends at the point of the onward domestic and international wire transfers and the purchase of the cashier's checks. The rapid and complex movement of the funds, coupled with the involvement of multiple institutions and jurisdictions, significantly hindered efforts to trace the entire $574,350.56. The remaining unrecovered balance, which represents the residual loss to the customer, is $528,402.52.

The investigation into the funds tracing highlights the sophisticated nature of the fraud and the challenges associated with recovering stolen funds once they have been transferred outside the immediate control of the originating institution. The use of multiple accounts, rapid transfers, and the conversion of funds into other instruments demonstrates a coordinated effort to launder the proceeds of the fraud and evade detection.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary of the fraudulent outbound wire was Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC. Information provided by the receiving institution during the recall attempt indicated the receiving account was opened on December 15, 2023, less than two months before the fraud event. The stated business purpose at account opening was the sale and servicing of industrial equipment. Review of corporate registry records identified that Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC was formed on December 7, 2023, eight days prior to account opening. The registered agent address was a commercial mail receiving agency, and no physical operating location could be identified through open-source research or commercial databases. The sole member listed in the registry filings had no identifiable digital footprint or history of business ownership. 

The receiving institution provided a summary of the activity on the Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC account between January 1, 2024, and the date the account was frozen. The account experienced no activity until January 18, 2024, when it received a low six-figure incoming wire from a commercial entity unaffiliated with Cortex Bank and Trust. Over the following two business days, the entirety of those funds was disbursed via multiple outbound domestic wires to Anvil Ventures Corp. and Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. The account then remained dormant until it received the fraudulent wire of $574,350.56 from Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC. 

Following the receipt of the Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC wire, the funds were rapidly disbursed. On the same day the funds were received, multiple outbound domestic wires were initiated, again directed to Anvil Ventures Corp. and Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., as well as several cashiers checks. The rapid movement of funds, particularly the immediate disbursement following a period of dormancy, is consistent with pass-through activity often observed in accounts utilized for the receipt and laundering of illicit proceeds. The beneficiary name, Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, did not match the established invoicing vendor of Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC, a discrepancy that was not identified during the initiation of the transfer. 

The receiving institution confirmed that $45,948.04 remained in the account and was frozen upon receipt of the recall request. The rapid dissipation of the remaining funds prior to the freeze action is indicative of a coordinated effort to remove the proceeds from the banking system or obscure their origin through subsequent transfers. The receiving institution indicated that they are conducting their own investigation into the activity on the Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC account. 

Analysis of the entities receiving the outbound wires from Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, Anvil Ventures Corp. and Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., revealed limited information. Both entities appear to have been recently formed, and public record searches yielded no evidence of established operations or physical locations. The lack of verifiable business presence for both the immediate beneficiary and the subsequent recipients of the funds further supports the assessment that the network of accounts was established primarily to facilitate the movement of illicitly obtained funds. The pattern of activity, characterized by the receipt of large, anomalous wires followed by immediate, structured disbursement to recently formed entities with opaque ownership, is highly indicative of a money laundering operation designed to obfuscate the origin and ownership of the funds induced from Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The investigation reviewed the documentary evidence surrounding the initiation and approval of the outbound wire transfer on January 18, 2024. A review of the email correspondence provided by Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC demonstrated that the instructions to remit funds to Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. originated from an external sender. The email header analysis established that the sender domain used for the communication was a lookalike domain, differing from the legitimate vendor’s domain by a single transposed character. The correspondence, which purported to be from Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, directed Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC to remit payment for an outstanding invoice to an alternative account. The email thread contained language stressing the urgency of the payment to secure a delivery schedule, which the investigation identified as consistent with social engineering tactics designed to bypass established internal controls.

The relationship manager assigned to Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC was interviewed regarding the customer's usual payment practices and the events of January 18, 2024. The relationship manager stated that the customer typically remits payments to Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC via automated clearing house transfers, and that wire transfers are generally reserved for initial deposits on large equipment purchases. The relationship manager confirmed that the wire request was received and processed shortly before the bank’s established wire cutoff time. The customer contact at Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC, interviewed on January 30, 2024, stated that the urgency expressed in the fraudulent email prompted them to expedite the payment, overriding their internal dual-approval requirement for outbound wires. The customer contact acknowledged that the beneficiary name, Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., did not align with the invoicing vendor, Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, but stated they believed it to be a subsidiary or holding company based on the context of the email correspondence.

The investigation obtained and reviewed the invoice referenced in the fraudulent email correspondence. The invoice, which requested payment in the amount of $574,350.56, appeared to be a modified version of a legitimate invoice previously issued by Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC. The modified invoice contained altered payment instructions directing the funds to the account held by Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. The customer contact at Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC confirmed that the underlying transaction—the purchase of heavy machinery—was legitimate and that the invoice amount was anticipated. The investigation noted that the customer did not attempt to independently verify the altered payment instructions with their established point of contact at Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC prior to initiating the wire transfer.

Authentication logs for the online banking session during which the wire was initiated were reviewed. The logs confirmed that the credentials used to access the account and authorize the transfer belonged to an authorized signer for Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC. No anomalies were identified in the login location or device fingerprint, suggesting that the customer's systems were not compromised and that the fraud was entirely reliant on the deception perpetrated through the lookalike email domain. A review of recorded telephone communications between the bank’s wire room and the customer contact at Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC confirmed that the bank performed the required callback verification procedures. During the callback, the customer contact verbally confirmed the beneficiary name, Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd., and the transfer amount, $574,350.56. The investigation determined that the bank’s established procedures for verifying outbound wire transfers were followed. The customer contact stated during the interview that they did not realize the funds had been diverted until Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC inquired about the past-due invoice on February 5, 2024, at which point Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC notified the bank of the suspected fraud.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated standard wire recall procedures following the customer's notification of the suspected fraud on February 23, 2024. A formal indemnification request, citing the fraudulent circumstances of the outbound wire transfer, was transmitted to the receiving financial institution later that same day. The request detailed the lookalike sender domain and the urgency language overriding the customer's dual-approval control, which had facilitated the unauthorized transfer. The reviewing analyst noted that the transfer was initiated mere minutes before the wire cutoff time, a common tactic in such schemes to limit the window for intervention. The receiving institution was provided with all available documentation, including copies of the compromised communications, to substantiate the claim that the funds were induced out of the customer account by deception.

The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the indemnification request on February 26, 2024. Subsequent communications indicated that they had initiated an investigation into the beneficiary account held by Anvil Ventures Corp. On March 5, 2024, the receiving institution informed Cortex Bank and Trust that a portion of the funds had been successfully secured. Specifically, the amount frozen at the receiving institution was $45,948.04. The receiving institution stated that the remaining balance of the original wire amount had already been disbursed from the beneficiary account prior to the receipt of the hold request. The receiving institution declined to provide further details regarding the destination of the disbursed funds, citing customer privacy regulations.

Following standard procedures, Cortex Bank and Trust requested the return of the secured funds. The receiving institution required a signed hold harmless agreement from Cortex Bank and Trust prior to releasing the funds. This agreement was executed and transmitted on March 8, 2024. The funds, totaling $45,948.04, were subsequently credited back to the Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC account, 77-76418-1, on March 12, 2024. This partial recovery significantly reduced the overall impact of the incident, although a substantial deficit remained. The reviewing analyst confirmed the receipt and appropriate crediting of these recovered funds.

The recovery efforts established the residual loss to the customer at $528,402.52. This figure represents the original fraudulent outbound wire amount of $574,350.56, less the recovered amount. The investigation confirmed that this residual sum was diverted and is considered unrecoverable through standard interbank channels. The relationship manager communicated this outcome to the authorized signers for Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC on March 15, 2024. The customer was advised that any further recovery efforts would likely require legal action or involvement from law enforcement agencies.

Cortex Bank and Trust reviewed the circumstances of the fraud against the customer's account agreement and the bank's liability policies. The investigation determined that the fraudulent instruction originated from a compromised email account controlled by the customer, and the customer's own personnel executed the wire request, bypassing established internal controls due to the perceived urgency of the request. As the bank executed the wire transfer in good faith based on an authenticated instruction from the customer, Cortex Bank and Trust concluded it had no liability for the loss. Consequently, no reimbursement was offered to Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC for the unrecovered funds. The relationship manager documented that the customer indicated they would be pursuing a claim through their corporate cybersecurity insurance policy to mitigate the residual loss. Cortex Bank and Trust provided the customer with a formal letter summarizing the bank's findings and the recovery efforts to support their insurance claim. The recovery phase of the investigation was concluded upon the return of the secured funds and the final communication with the customer regarding liability.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that on January 18, 2024, the subject Silverthorn Fabrication Group LLC initiated an outbound wire transfer of $574,350.56, payable to Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. Review of the underlying communications provided by the customer confirmed that the payment instructions were received via email from a lookalike domain differing from the customary invoicing vendor by a single character. The communications contained language urging immediate payment, which the customer stated caused them to bypass their internal dual-approval control and initiate the transfer minutes before the daily cutoff. Cortex Bank and Trust determined that Mapleford Capital Holdings Ltd. was not the intended vendor, Umberfield Machinery Enterprises LLC, and that the funds were diverted by deception. The receiving institution confirmed on April 5, 2024 that a portion of the funds had been secured, resulting in a residual loss to the customer. As the activity represents a loss suffered by the customer through external fraud rather than suspicious activity by the customer or through the Cortex Bank and Trust account, the matter is closed_no_action.
