## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2420
Date opened: October 2, 2024
Subject: Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP (business), account 80-87262-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: ongoing

## Case Summary

On August 12, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit opened an investigation regarding a suspected business email compromise event affecting an established commercial customer. The matter was referred to the unit following a customer dispute filed by an authorized signer on the operating account maintained by Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP. The dispute alleged that an outbound domestic wire transfer processed on August 1, 2024, was unauthorized, as the beneficiary was not a vendor known to the business and the instruction was not issued by the partnership.

The review period for this investigation spans from June 7, 2024, to October 2, 2024, capturing the activity leading up to the disputed transaction and the subsequent investigative efforts. The transaction under review is a single outbound wire transfer in the amount of $1,029,742.58, debited from account 80-87262-1. This amount exceeds the threshold for suspicious activity reporting. The core objective of this investigation is to determine whether the transfer of $1,029,742.58 was induced by deception, and if so, the mechanism of the compromise and the disposition of the funds.

The initial review of the referral indicated that the transfer was initiated via the online banking portal. The customer reported that the instruction was believed to have been originated in response to an email communication that appeared to be from a known vendor, Sandpiper Logistics Corp. The email contained an invoice and payment instructions directing the funds to a beneficiary identified in the transfer details as Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC. The customer asserted that Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC is not a recognized counterparty and that no legitimate business purpose existed for a payment to that entity. The customer further stated that upon contacting Sandpiper Logistics Corp. regarding the payment, the vendor confirmed that they had not issued the invoice and had not changed their payment instructions.

Following the receipt of the customer dispute, the reviewing analyst initiated contact with the receiving institution in an attempt to recover the funds. The receiving institution confirmed the receipt of the wire transfer but indicated that the majority of the funds had already been disbursed or withdrawn from the beneficiary account prior to the receipt of the indemnification request. A hold was successfully placed on the remaining balance in the beneficiary account. The amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution was $102,974.26. The remaining balance of the original transfer, representing the residual loss to the customer, is $926,768.32.

The investigation will examine the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire transfer, including a review of the online banking session logs and the communications provided by the customer. The review will seek to identify the indicators of compromise, such as the use of deceptive sender addresses or manipulative language designed to bypass established internal controls. The analysis will also seek to characterize the relationship, if any, between the beneficiary, Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC, and the known vendor, Sandpiper Logistics Corp., or any other known counterparties such as Harborview Logistics Inc. The investigation remains ongoing as the unit continues to analyze the available evidence and coordinate with the receiving institution regarding the frozen funds.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The matter was escalated to the Financial Intelligence Unit on August 12, 2024, following an internal referral from the commercial banking division concerning activity on the Cortex Bank and Trust account held by Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP. The referral cited a customer complaint alleging that a wire transfer executed from the subject account on August 1, 2024, was unauthorized. The customer asserted that the funds were intended for a known vendor, Harborview Logistics Inc., to settle an outstanding invoice for logistics services. However, the customer subsequently determined that the payment instructions had been altered prior to the transfer being initiated by their accounts payable department.

According to the referral, the relationship manager for Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP was contacted by the customer on August 12, 2024, after Harborview Logistics Inc. notified the customer that payment for services rendered in July had not been received. The customer reviewed their internal records and determined that a wire transfer had been initiated on August 1, 2024, but the beneficiary information did not correspond to Harborview Logistics Inc. The customer reported to the relationship manager that their accounts payable personnel had received an email purportedly from Harborview Logistics Inc. directing payment to a new account. The customer indicated that the email contained a revised invoice and instructions emphasizing the need for immediate payment to avoid service disruption.

The internal referral documented that the customer had provided copies of the email correspondence to the relationship manager. The relationship manager noted in the referral that the email address used by the sender appeared to be a lookalike domain, differing from the legitimate Harborview Logistics Inc. domain by a single character. The customer reported that the urgency conveyed in the email had led their accounts payable staff to bypass their standard dual-approval control for new payee setup, resulting in the initiation of the wire transfer based on the fraudulent instructions. The customer further alleged that the beneficiary name on the executed wire transfer was Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC, an entity with which Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP had no prior business relationship.

The referral indicated that the wire transfer in question was processed in the amount of $1,029,742.58. The relationship manager initiated a recall request through Cortex Bank and Trust's wire operations department immediately upon receiving the customer complaint on August 12, 2024. The referral noted that the receiving institution was contacted to freeze the funds associated with the transfer. The customer alleged that they were the victim of a business email compromise scheme resulting in the diversion of funds intended for a legitimate vendor.

The Financial Intelligence Unit reviewed the referral and the supporting documentation provided by the relationship manager. The allegation presented was that an unauthorized party had induced the customer to initiate a wire transfer by providing fraudulent payment instructions via email. The referral source was identified as the relationship manager, acting upon a direct complaint from the customer, Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP. The reviewing analyst noted the customer's assertion that the funds were misdirected to Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC instead of the intended recipient, Harborview Logistics Inc. The allegation of business email compromise and subsequent wire fraud formed the basis for the initiation of the investigation. The reviewing analyst also noted the customer's claim regarding the bypassed internal controls due to the urgency expressed in the fraudulent email correspondence. The referral established the parameters for the review of the subject account activity, specifically focusing on the circumstances surrounding the outbound wire transfer executed on August 1, 2024.

## Timeline of Events

On July 3, 2024, the authorized signer for Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP received an email appearing to originate from Harborview Logistics Inc., a vendor the subject entity had transacted with previously. The reviewing analyst determined that the sender's email address domain contained a single substituted character, making it visually similar to the genuine Harborview Logistics Inc. domain. This email asserted that payment for an outstanding invoice was significantly overdue and demanded immediate settlement to avoid supply chain disruptions. The correspondence directed payment to a new beneficiary account held by Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC. The email contained urgent language pressing the authorized signer to bypass the customary dual-approval control established for outbound wires exceeding a specific threshold.

The authorized signer for Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP subsequently initiated an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $1,029,742.58 via the Cortex Bank and Trust online banking portal on July 3, 2024. The transfer was initiated shortly before the daily wire processing cutoff time. The beneficiary named on the payment instructions was Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC, rather than the invoicing vendor, Harborview Logistics Inc.

On July 29, 2024, the authorized signer for Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report that the July 3, 2024 wire transfer had been induced by fraudulent communications. The customer stated that Harborview Logistics Inc. had contacted them regarding the unpaid invoice, prompting a review of the earlier correspondence and the realization that the payment instructions were illegitimate. The customer confirmed they had no intended business relationship with Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC.

Following the customer report, Cortex Bank and Trust personnel initiated a recall request through the wire network on July 29, 2024. Communication was established with the receiving institution holding the Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC account. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the recall request and placed a hold on the remaining funds in the beneficiary account.

On August 1, 2024, the receiving institution informed Cortex Bank and Trust that a portion of the funds from the July 3, 2024 wire transfer remained in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution confirmed that $102,974.26 had been frozen. The receiving institution indicated that the remainder of the funds had been transferred to other accounts or withdrawn prior to the receipt of the recall request. Cortex Bank and Trust initiated the process for the return of the frozen funds.

The reviewing analyst noted that a review of the subject entity's transaction history revealed no prior outbound wires to Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC. The activity is consistent with business email compromise, in which a malicious actor spoofed vendor communications to redirect a legitimate payment. The investigation established that the customer sustained a loss of $926,768.32, representing the difference between the initial fraudulent transfer and the amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution.

On August 12, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received the returned funds from the receiving institution in the amount of $102,974.26. These funds were subsequently credited to the Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP account. The relationship manager was notified of the return of funds and the ongoing investigation. The customer was advised to implement enhanced verification procedures for changes to vendor payment instructions.

A review of the transaction activity of Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC at the receiving institution, provided in response to a request for information under Section 314(b) of the USA PATRIOT Act, indicated that funds from the July 3, 2024 wire transfer were rapidly dispersed. The receiving institution noted transfers to several other entities, including Sandpiper Logistics Corp., shortly after the funds were credited to the Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC account. The reviewing analyst determined that the rapid movement of funds following the initial deposit is indicative of attempts to obfuscate the flow of funds and hinder recovery efforts.

## Funds Tracing

Cortex Bank and Trust received the request to process the outbound wire transfer from the Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP account 80-87262-1 on August 12, 2024. The transfer instructions directed the funds to an account purportedly held by Harborview Logistics Inc. Review of the transaction details confirmed the originating debit from the Cortex Bank and Trust account occurred on the same date. The transfer amount was $1,029,742.58. The beneficiary institution identified in the wire instructions was located in a jurisdiction known for less stringent banking secrecy regulations, although the beneficiary address provided was domestic. This discrepancy between the beneficiary address and the receiving institution's location was noted during the initial review but did not trigger an automated hold, as the transaction value, while significant, was consistent with prior legitimate disbursements from the Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP account to other vendors.

Information obtained through the SWIFT messaging network confirmed the funds reached the beneficiary institution on August 12, 2024. Following the discovery of the suspected fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request to the beneficiary institution on August 22, 2024. The beneficiary institution responded to the recall request, indicating that the account credited was not held in the name of Harborview Logistics Inc. Instead, the account was registered to Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC. The beneficiary institution further advised that a portion of the funds had already been moved from the Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC account prior to the receipt of the recall request.

The beneficiary institution confirmed it was able to freeze a portion of the transferred funds remaining in the Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC account. The amount frozen was $102,974.26. The beneficiary institution's response indicated that the remainder of the funds had been transferred to a third party.

Subsequent inquiries directed to the beneficiary institution sought information regarding the onward movement of the funds. The beneficiary institution disclosed that the remaining funds were transferred via multiple domestic wires within their jurisdiction to an account held by Sandpiper Logistics Corp. on August 13, 2024. The beneficiary institution stated they were unable to provide further details regarding the ultimate disposition of the funds once they reached the Sandpiper Logistics Corp. account, citing jurisdictional privacy laws.

The investigation established the total amount diverted from the intended recipient was $1,029,742.58. The residual loss to the customer, Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP, is calculated as the diverted amount less the funds successfully frozen at the beneficiary institution. This residual loss is $926,768.32.

The trail of the funds beyond the transfer to Sandpiper Logistics Corp. remains unverified. The beneficiary institution's inability to provide transaction records for the Sandpiper Logistics Corp. account prevents documented tracing of the final disposition. It is inferred, based on established typologies involving business email compromise, that the funds transferred to Sandpiper Logistics Corp. were likely subsequently moved to accounts in other jurisdictions or converted into other assets to obscure their origin and complicate recovery efforts. The use of multiple entities, Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC and Sandpiper Logistics Corp., neither of which had a known prior relationship with Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP, is consistent with methods used to layer illicit funds. The investigation has not identified any legitimate business purpose for the transfers to Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC or Sandpiper Logistics Corp. The tracing efforts are currently stalled at the Sandpiper Logistics Corp. account level pending further cooperation from the beneficiary institution or law enforcement intervention.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary of the $1,029,742.58 wire transfer on August 12, 2024, was identified as Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC. A review of internal records indicated that Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC held an account with Cortex Bank and Trust. The account for Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC was established on June 7, 2024. The account opening documentation stated the business purpose was international trade and logistics, with a focus on sourcing and distributing industrial components. 

Open-source research was conducted on Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC. A search of the relevant state business registry confirmed the entity was registered on June 10, 2024, three days after the account was opened at Cortex Bank and Trust. The registered agent address provided was a commercial mail receiving agency. No physical operating address or commercial storefront could be identified for the business. Further research did not locate a company website, professional networking profiles for any principals, or any online presence consistent with an established international trade and logistics firm. 

A review of the transaction history for the Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC account revealed a pattern of activity that appeared inconsistent with the stated business purpose. From the account opening on June 7, 2024, until the receipt of the $1,029,742.58 wire on August 12, 2024, the account exhibited minimal activity. Initial funding consisted of a nominal cash deposit. The account maintained a low balance with only a few small-dollar debit card transactions for apparent office supplies and minor administrative expenses. There was no evidence of payroll, rent payments, tax payments, or other typical operating expenses associated with a legitimate business. 

The receipt of the $1,029,742.58 wire on August 12, 2024, represented a significant deviation from the established historical activity. The funds were received from Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP. The beneficiary name on the transfer instructions, Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC, did not align with any known vendors or suppliers associated with Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP. The transfer was initiated shortly before the daily wire cutoff time, which is a common characteristic observed in wire fraud schemes. 

Following the receipt of the $1,029,742.58, the funds were rapidly disbursed. On August 22, 2024, a series of outgoing wire transfers were initiated from the Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC account. The funds were primarily directed to Harborview Logistics Inc. and Sandpiper Logistics Corp. Open-source research on these entities yielded limited information. Neither Harborview Logistics Inc. nor Sandpiper Logistics Corp. appeared to have an established online presence or a demonstrable history of commercial operations in the logistics sector. The rapid dissipation of funds to seemingly unrelated counterparties with minimal discernible business footprints is consistent with the layering phase of a money laundering operation or the rapid extraction of funds following a fraudulent transfer. 

The investigation sought to determine the extent of the loss and the potential for recovery. The $1,029,742.58 was successfully transferred out of the Cortex Bank and Trust account held by Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP. Through collaboration with the receiving institution for the subsequent transfers made by Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC, $102,974.26 was successfully frozen. However, the residual loss to the customer remained significant at $926,768.32. The analysis of the beneficiary and counterparties indicates a coordinated effort to receive and disperse the fraudulently obtained funds. The lack of a legitimate business footprint for Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC, the rapid movement of the funds, and the destination of the subsequent transfers to Harborview Logistics Inc. and Sandpiper Logistics Corp. strongly suggest these entities may be acting as conduits for illicit funds. The investigation into the true nature of these businesses and their relationship to the subject is ongoing.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The relationship manager assigned to Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP was interviewed by the reviewing analyst on July 29, 2024. The relationship manager stated that the customer’s controller contacted him on June 28, 2024, to report a suspected fraud. The controller indicated that a payment intended for Harborview Logistics Inc. had been misdirected based on altered payment instructions received via email. The relationship manager confirmed that the customer’s usual practice for modifying vendor payment instructions required verbal verification with a known contact at the vendor, a procedure that was not followed in this instance. The relationship manager further stated that the customer’s account profile indicated an expected volume of outbound wires consistent with their operations, but the specific beneficiary name on the disputed wire was unfamiliar to the customer. 

The reviewing analyst obtained and reviewed the email correspondence provided by Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP. Analysis of the email headers revealed that the message containing the altered payment instructions originated from a domain that differed from the legitimate Harborview Logistics Inc. domain by a single character. The lookalike domain was registered shortly before the email was sent, consistent with tactics often observed in business email compromise schemes. The email content included language emphasizing the urgency of the payment, which the customer’s controller stated contributed to the decision to bypass the established dual-approval control for wire transfers. The email directed payment to an account held by Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC, a beneficiary name that did not match the invoicing vendor, Harborview Logistics Inc.

Invoices provided by the customer were compared against the altered payment instructions. The original invoice from Harborview Logistics Inc. directed payment to an account at a different financial institution than the one specified in the fraudulent email. The amount requested in the fraudulent email, $1,029,742.58, matched the amount due on the legitimate invoice. The customer stated that they believed they were remitting payment for legitimate services rendered by Harborview Logistics Inc. and had no prior business relationship with Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC or Sandpiper Logistics Corp. 

Authentication logs for the Cortex Bank and Trust online banking platform were reviewed for the period surrounding the fraudulent wire transfer. The logs indicated that the wire transfer was initiated by an authorized user of the Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP account. The initiation occurred minutes before the wire cutoff time on June 10, 2024. The customer confirmed that the user who initiated the wire was the controller, who had acted upon the instructions received in the fraudulent email. The logs showed no evidence of unauthorized access or credential compromise related to the online banking platform itself. 

The reviewing analyst obtained call recordings from the Cortex Bank and Trust wire room. The recordings captured the verbal confirmation of the wire transfer details with the customer’s controller. The controller confirmed the beneficiary name, Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC, and the routing and account numbers provided in the fraudulent email. The wire room representative verified the authorization based on established procedures, which did not require independent verification of the beneficiary’s identity or the validity of the underlying transaction. The customer’s controller did not mention the urgency language or the altered payment instructions during the confirmation call. 

The customer provided documentation indicating that they had contacted the receiving institution in an attempt to recall the funds. The receiving institution confirmed that a portion of the funds, $102,974.26, had been frozen in the beneficiary account. The receiving institution declined to provide further details regarding the disposition of the remaining funds or the identity of the account holder without a subpoena or law enforcement request. The customer stated they had filed a report with local law enforcement and the Federal Bureau of Investigation's Internet Crime Complaint Center. The investigation into the flow of funds following the initial transfer to Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC remains ongoing.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

On August 22, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust wire operations initiated a formal recall request for the outbound wire transfer. The recall was sent via the SWIFT network to the receiving institution. The request cited the suspicion of wire fraud and requested the immediate return of the funds. The reviewing analyst noted that the recall request was initiated past the standard window for automated returns, requiring manual intervention by the receiving institution's compliance or fraud department. Cortex Bank and Trust also transmitted a hold harmless indemnity agreement to the receiving institution, standard practice in fraud recovery efforts, offering to indemnify the receiving institution against claims arising from the return of the funds.

The receiving institution acknowledged the recall and indemnity request on August 22, 2024. The receiving institution indicated that they were placing a temporary administrative hold on the beneficiary account associated with Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC pending their internal review. The reviewing analyst monitored the SWIFT messaging queue for updates. The receiving institution did not immediately confirm the availability of funds or a timeline for potential return. The investigation noted that the receiving institution requested additional documentation from Cortex Bank and Trust to substantiate the fraud claim, which was subsequently provided by the relationship manager.

On July 25, 2023, the receiving institution communicated via SWIFT that a portion of the funds associated with the fraudulent outbound wire amount had been successfully frozen in the beneficiary account. The communication specified that $102,974.26 was secured. The receiving institution stated that the remaining funds from the transfer had already been depleted from the Foxglove Exports Enterprises LLC account prior to the receipt of the recall request. The receiving institution did not provide details regarding the disposition of the depleted funds or the counterparties involved in those subsequent transactions.

The reviewing analyst calculated the residual loss to the customer based on the information provided by the receiving institution. Subtracting the secured funds from the fraudulent outbound wire amount, the calculation established a residual loss to Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP of $926,768.32. The relationship manager communicated this residual loss figure to the customer. Cortex Bank and Trust initiated the formal process to request the return of the secured funds. The receiving institution required Cortex Bank and Trust to execute a finalized, transaction-specific indemnity agreement before they would release the $102,974.26 back to Cortex Bank and Trust.

The finalized indemnity agreement was executed and transmitted to the receiving institution. Cortex Bank and Trust is currently awaiting the return of the secured funds. The reviewing analyst noted that the recovery of the secured funds is contingent upon the receiving institution's internal processes and that timelines for such returns can vary significantly. The customer, Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP, inquired about the bank's policy regarding reimbursement for the residual loss. Cortex Bank and Trust informed the customer that, as the wire transfer was initiated by an authorized user using valid credentials, albeit under deceptive circumstances, the bank was not liable for the loss under the terms of the deposit account agreement.

Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP informed the relationship manager that they had initiated a claim with their commercial insurance provider regarding the residual loss. The customer indicated that the insurance provider requested documentation from Cortex Bank and Trust regarding the transaction and the recovery efforts. Cortex Bank and Trust provided the requested documentation to the customer to support their insurance claim. The investigation noted that the outcome of the insurance claim is pending and does not alter the bank's position regarding liability for the loss. The reviewing analyst continues to monitor the status of the return of the secured funds from the receiving institution.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Ardent Industrial Supply Partners LP suffered a loss of $1,029,742.58 through a business email compromise scheme. A review of client communications provided by the relationship manager confirmed that an employee of the subject received an email appearing to originate from a known vendor, but utilizing a lookalike sender domain differing by one character. This communication contained instructions to remit payment for a purportedly outstanding invoice to a new beneficiary, Harborview Logistics Inc. The email included urgency language, which the customer later stated prompted them to override their internal dual-approval control. A funds transfer for the invoiced amount was subsequently initiated minutes before the wire cutoff on September 30, 2024. The beneficiary name on the transfer instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor. Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution, but only a fraction of the funds could be secured, resulting in a substantial residual loss to the customer. Due to the high dollar value and the confirmed fraudulent nature of the transfer, the matter remains open and the investigation is ongoing.

body:
## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2421
Date opened: July 24, 2024
Subject: Saltmarsh Equipment LLC (business), account 12-23505-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: closed_no_action

## Case Summary

On June 28, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust wire operations department referred a matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit concerning a potentially fraudulent outbound wire transfer. The referral indicated that a high-value payment had been processed and subsequently contested by the originating customer. The Financial Intelligence Unit opened a formal investigation on the same day to determine the circumstances surrounding the authorization and execution of the transfer. The investigation sought to establish whether the bank's customer was the victim of a business email compromise or other deceptive scheme, and to quantify the potential loss. The investigation was assigned an internal high risk tier due to the value of the transaction. The review period for the investigation was defined as March 25, 2024 through July 25, 2024.

The customer at the center of the referral is Saltmarsh Equipment LLC, a commercial entity holding an active deposit relationship with Cortex Bank and Trust. The account under review is Cortex Bank and Trust account 12-23505-1. The referral identified a single outgoing wire transfer, executed during the review period, as the transaction in question. The amount of the contested outbound wire transfer was $2,911,781.08. The wire operations department reported that Saltmarsh Equipment LLC contacted the bank shortly after the funds were dispatched, asserting that the payment instructions were fraudulent and had not been authorized by a legitimate representative of the company. The customer alleged that the payment was intended for a known vendor but was misdirected to an unknown beneficiary.

The investigation was tasked with reviewing the communication channels and authorization protocols utilized by Saltmarsh Equipment LLC prior to the execution of the $2,911,781.08 wire transfer. This included an examination of email correspondence, payment instructions, and the application of internal controls by the customer. The reviewing analyst was directed to assess the validity of the customer's claim of deception and to identify any indicators of compromise within the customer's payment process. The investigation also aimed to determine the extent of the financial impact on the customer, including efforts to recover the diverted funds.

Initial review of the referral documentation indicated that the payment instructions were received by Cortex Bank and Trust via an established electronic channel utilized by Saltmarsh Equipment LLC. The instructions appeared to have been properly authenticated using the customer's credentials. However, the subsequent dispute raised questions regarding the origin of the payment request. The investigation was therefore required to determine whether the instructions, despite appearing technically valid, were induced by fraudulent means. The reviewing analyst was tasked with analyzing the circumstances leading up to the transmission of the payment instructions to Cortex Bank and Trust.

The investigation also focused on the destination of the funds. The wire transfer was directed to an external account held by a different financial institution. The referral indicated that Cortex Bank and Trust initiated recall procedures upon receiving the fraud claim from Saltmarsh Equipment LLC. The investigation sought to confirm the status of the recall request and to determine the final disposition of the $2,911,781.08. The analyst was directed to coordinate with the wire operations department and the receiving institution to ascertain what portion, if any, of the funds could be recovered and returned to the customer's account.

The primary objective of the investigation was to produce a comprehensive report detailing the sequence of events, identifying any control failures or vulnerabilities exploited during the incident, and providing a definitive assessment of the loss incurred by Saltmarsh Equipment LLC. The findings would then be evaluated to determine the appropriate course of action, which could include the filing of a Suspicious Activity Report, the implementation of enhanced monitoring, or the closure of the investigation without further action.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The review of account activity for Saltmarsh Equipment LLC was initiated on June 28, 2024, following a referral from the Cortex Bank and Trust wire operations department. The referral was prompted by an urgent customer inquiry received that morning regarding a substantial outbound funds transfer executed the previous week. The customer, acting through its authorized representative, alleged that a wire transfer authorized and transmitted on June 20, 2024, had been fraudulently induced. The allegation centered on a business email compromise scheme that resulted in the misdirection of funds intended for a known vendor.

According to the initial referral documentation, the authorized representative for Saltmarsh Equipment LLC contacted the relationship manager on June 28, 2024, to report that a scheduled payment to a regular supplier, Aperture Commodities Group LLC, had not been received. The customer stated that the payment was intended to settle an outstanding invoice for a bulk materials delivery. Upon reviewing their internal records and confirming with the intended payee, the customer determined that the funds had been remitted to an account held by an entity they did not recognize.

The customer further detailed to the relationship manager that the payment instructions had been received via email on June 20, 2024. The customer alleged that this email, while appearing to originate from their established contact at Aperture Commodities Group LLC, was later identified as fraudulent. The customer noted that the sender's email address utilized a lookalike domain that differed from the legitimate vendor's domain by a single character. This discrepancy was not noticed by the customer's accounts payable staff at the time the instructions were received and processed.

The referral indicated that the fraudulent email contained revised payment instructions, directing the funds to a new beneficiary account rather than the one previously used for Aperture Commodities Group LLC. The customer asserted that they had no prior business relationship with the entity named in the revised instructions, Waterstone Logistics Corp. The customer also reported that the email correspondence from the purported vendor included language conveying high urgency, insisting that the payment be processed immediately to secure a pending shipment. The customer stated that this urgency language influenced their decision to expedite the processing of the wire transfer.

The wire operations department's referral noted that the outbound transfer was initiated late in the business day on June 20, 2024. The transfer was processed shortly before the bank's established cutoff time for same-day wire processing. The customer's allegation, as documented in the referral, is that the combination of the urgent language and the late-day initiation was designed to bypass or minimize the effectiveness of the customer's internal dual-approval controls.

Upon receipt of the customer's notification, the relationship manager escalated the matter to the wire operations department, which subsequently forwarded the information to the Financial Intelligence Unit for review. The referral requested an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the June 20, 2024 transfer and the assessment of potential avenues for recovery. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer's account, 12-23505-1, had not been the subject of any recent automated alerts or previous fraud claims. The initial assessment of the referral identified the activity as consistent with a business email compromise resulting in wire fraud, warranting a comprehensive review of the transaction and the associated communications provided by the customer. The reviewing analyst commenced the investigation to verify the customer's claims and determine the extent of the unauthorized activity.

## Timeline of Events

On March 25, 2024, the relationship manager for Saltmarsh Equipment LLC contacted the FIU to report a potential loss event. The customer had informed the relationship manager that morning that a scheduled payment of $2,911,781.08 to a known vendor had not been received by the vendor. Subsequent review by the customer and the relationship manager established that the funds had been routed to an account at another institution that did not belong to the intended vendor. An FIU analyst was assigned to investigate the circumstances of the wire transfer. The analyst reviewed email correspondence provided by the customer between Saltmarsh Equipment LLC personnel and an individual claiming to represent Aperture Commodities Group LLC.

The correspondence indicated that on April 1, 2024, an individual utilizing an email address with a lookalike domain contacted the accounts payable department of Saltmarsh Equipment LLC. The domain differed from the legitimate domain of Aperture Commodities Group LLC by a single character. The sender presented an invoice for industrial equipment, a type of good previously purchased by Saltmarsh Equipment LLC from Aperture Commodities Group LLC. The invoice was formatted similarly to previous invoices from Aperture Commodities Group LLC but contained new wiring instructions.

On April 26, 2024, the accounts payable department at Saltmarsh Equipment LLC initiated a wire transfer for $2,911,781.08 through the Cortex Bank and Trust online banking portal. The beneficiary name entered for the transfer was Oakhurst Logistics Enterprises LLC, which did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Aperture Commodities Group LLC. The analyst noted that the email correspondence from the lookalike domain contained urgency language, instructing the accounts payable department to expedite the payment to avoid supply chain disruptions. The customer's internal dual-approval control for wire transfers was bypassed, and the transfer was executed. The transfer was initiated minutes before the Cortex Bank and Trust daily wire cutoff time.

The investigation established that Saltmarsh Equipment LLC had intended to pay Aperture Commodities Group LLC and had not intended to transmit funds to Oakhurst Logistics Enterprises LLC. On May 21, 2024, a representative from the legitimate Aperture Commodities Group LLC contacted Saltmarsh Equipment LLC to inquire about the unpaid invoice. This contact prompted Saltmarsh Equipment LLC to review the payment details, leading to the discovery that the funds had been directed to Oakhurst Logistics Enterprises LLC.

On May 27, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust submitted a request to the receiving institution to recall the wire transfer. The receiving institution subsequently informed Cortex Bank and Trust that the account held by Oakhurst Logistics Enterprises LLC had been depleted shortly after the funds were credited. The receiving institution indicated that a portion of the funds had been transferred to an account held by Waterstone Logistics Corp. However, the receiving institution was able to freeze $465,884.97 remaining in the account.

On June 7, 2024, the FIU analyst requested additional documentation from Saltmarsh Equipment LLC regarding the customer's vendor onboarding and payment verification procedures. The customer provided documentation indicating that a verbal verification of the changed wiring instructions had not been performed prior to the execution of the wire transfer.

On June 10, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received confirmation from the receiving institution that the frozen funds, totaling $465,884.97, would be returned. The funds were subsequently credited back to the Saltmarsh Equipment LLC account.

On June 20, 2024, the FIU analyst concluded the review of the transaction history and the correspondence provided by the customer. The analyst determined that the total residual loss to Saltmarsh Equipment LLC, after the return of the frozen funds, was $2,445,896.11.

On June 28, 2024, the FIU analyst finalized the review of the customer's account activity within the review period. No further unusual or suspicious activity was identified in connection with the Saltmarsh Equipment LLC account during the review period.

## Funds Tracing

The transfer in question, a domestic wire in the amount of $2,911,781.08, originated from the Cortex Bank and Trust operating account held by Saltmarsh Equipment LLC on June 10, 2024. The debit was authorized by a signatory for Saltmarsh Equipment LLC following receipt of an email that was later identified as originating from a lookalike sender domain. The beneficiary of the transfer was Aperture Commodities Group LLC. The reviewing analyst confirmed the outbound transfer instruction included a beneficiary name that did not match the invoicing vendor, Oakhurst Logistics Enterprises LLC, as indicated on the supporting documentation provided by the customer. The instruction was submitted to Cortex Bank and Trust minutes before the wire cutoff time.

The funds were credited to an account held by Aperture Commodities Group LLC at a domestic institution. Upon notification of the suspected fraud by Cortex Bank and Trust, the receiving institution placed a hold on the beneficiary account. The receiving institution later confirmed that $465,884.97 of the original transferred amount remained in the account and was successfully frozen. The residual loss to Saltmarsh Equipment LLC was calculated at $2,445,896.11.

Information provided by the receiving institution indicated that prior to the freeze being enacted, a portion of the funds was transferred onward. The receiving institution reported an outbound wire transfer to an account held by Waterstone Logistics Corp. at a third domestic financial institution. The exact amount of this onward transfer was not disclosed to Cortex Bank and Trust, but the receiving institution indicated it represented a significant portion of the funds that were not frozen. The trail of the funds transferred to Waterstone Logistics Corp. ends at that third institution, as Cortex Bank and Trust has no visibility into the activity within that account.

The receiving institution also reported that a portion of the funds credited to the Aperture Commodities Group LLC account was dissipated through a series of smaller, rapid transactions. These transactions included multiple automated clearing house debits and point-of-sale purchases. The specific beneficiaries and merchants associated with these transactions were not provided to Cortex Bank and Trust. The reviewing analyst notes that the rapid dissipation of funds following a large incoming wire is consistent with attempts to obscure the trail of funds and move them beyond the reach of recovery efforts.

Based on the information available, the funds tracing is complete to the extent possible. The initial transfer of $2,911,781.08 from Saltmarsh Equipment LLC to Aperture Commodities Group LLC is fully documented. The freezing of $465,884.97 at the receiving institution is confirmed. The onward movement of a portion of the funds to Waterstone Logistics Corp. is documented by the receiving institution, although the specific amount is unknown. The dissipation of the remaining funds through smaller transactions is also documented by the receiving institution, but the ultimate destinations of those funds are unknown. The reviewing analyst infers that the funds transferred to Waterstone Logistics Corp. and those dissipated through smaller transactions were likely further moved or converted to obscure their origin, although no direct evidence is available to confirm this inference. The lack of visibility into the accounts at the third institution and the specific details of the smaller transactions prevents a complete tracing of all funds associated with the initial fraudulent transfer.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary of the fraudulent outbound wire amount of $2,911,781.08 was identified in the wire instructions as Aperture Commodities Group LLC. The reviewing analyst conducted public records research to establish the nature of the entity and its relationship to the subject, Saltmarsh Equipment LLC. State registry filings indicated that Aperture Commodities Group LLC was incorporated in Delaware on April 26, 2024, approximately six weeks prior to the transaction under review. The registered agent address listed on the incorporation documents was identified as a commercial mail receiving agency. No physical operating location or contact telephone number could be located through independent open-source research. The business purpose stated on the incorporation documents was general trade, which provided insufficient detail to corroborate a legitimate commercial relationship with a heavy equipment vendor.

A review of the invoice provided by the subject to support the wire transfer revealed discrepancies. The invoice purported to be from a known vendor of the subject, Oakhurst Logistics Enterprises LLC, but directed payment to Aperture Commodities Group LLC. The customer was unable to substantiate the reason for this discrepancy when contacted by the relationship manager. Further analysis of the email communication containing the revised payment instructions indicated that the sender's domain name differed from the vendor's known domain name by a single character. This lookalike sender domain is a common indicator of business email compromise.

Information received from the beneficiary institution regarding the receiving account for Aperture Commodities Group LLC revealed an account opening date of May 21, 2024. This date was shortly after the entity's incorporation and a matter of weeks before the receipt of the wire from Saltmarsh Equipment LLC. The beneficiary institution reported that prior to June 7, 2024, the account exhibited minimal activity, consisting primarily of low-dollar test deposits and administrative fees. The receipt of the $2,911,781.08 wire from Cortex Bank and Trust represented a significant deviation from this established baseline and was inconsistent with the stated business purpose of a newly formed entity.

Following the receipt of the funds on June 7, 2024, the beneficiary account exhibited rapid dissipation of the funds. The beneficiary institution reported that the majority of the funds were transferred out of the account via multiple wire transfers to various domestic and international beneficiaries within a three-day period. One notable transfer was directed to Waterstone Logistics Corp. The beneficiary institution was unable to provide a stated business purpose for these outgoing transfers. The velocity of funds movement and the lack of an apparent commercial rationale for the subsequent transfers are consistent with the layering phase of a money laundering operation following a fraudulent inducement of funds.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request for the wire transfer on June 10, 2024, upon discovery of the suspected fraud by the customer. The beneficiary institution responded on June 20, 2024, confirming that they were able to secure a portion of the funds. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $465,884.97. The beneficiary institution indicated that the remainder of the funds had already been disbursed prior to the receipt of the recall request. The residual loss to the customer was determined to be $2,445,896.11. The beneficiary institution further advised that they had placed restrictions on the account for Aperture Commodities Group LLC pending their own internal investigation into the activity. The reviewing analyst noted that the beneficiary institution did not provide any further information regarding the principals of Aperture Commodities Group LLC or the ultimate destination of the disbursed funds. The activity observed in the beneficiary account, including the recent formation of the entity, the use of a commercial mail receiving agency, the rapid movement of funds, and the lack of a clear commercial purpose, strongly supported the assessment that the account was established for the primary purpose of receiving and laundering illicitly obtained funds.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

An interview was conducted with the relationship manager for Saltmarsh Equipment LLC on June 28, 2024. The relationship manager confirmed that the client is a distributor of heavy industrial machinery and frequently engages in high-value wire transfers to settle invoices with international suppliers. The relationship manager noted that the client’s internal controls require dual approval for any outgoing wire exceeding a low six-figure sum. However, the client reported that on June 20, 2024, the primary authorized signer instructed the secondary authorized signer to bypass this control due to an urgent request purportedly from a long-standing vendor, Waterstone Logistics Corp. The relationship manager stated that the client provided copies of the email correspondence that prompted the wire transfer.

A review of the email headers provided by the client revealed that the communication originated from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the legitimate domain of Waterstone Logistics Corp. The email, dated June 20, 2024, contained urgency language overriding the dual-approval control, demanding immediate payment to avoid a halt in a pending shipment. The client stated that the primary authorized signer, acting on this perceived urgency, initiated the wire transfer minutes before the wire cutoff time. The client’s internal logs confirmed the initiation time and the bypass of the secondary approval step.

The client provided a copy of the invoice attached to the fraudulent email. The invoice appeared to be a replica of a genuine Waterstone Logistics Corp. invoice, but the beneficiary name and payment instructions had been altered. The beneficiary named on the fraudulent invoice was Aperture Commodities Group LLC, an entity with which Saltmarsh Equipment LLC had no prior business relationship. The invoice amount matched the fraudulent outbound wire amount of $2,911,781.08.

Further review of the client’s internal records indicated that a subsequent email, purporting to be from Oakhurst Logistics Enterprises LLC, a subcontractor for Waterstone Logistics Corp., was received on June 27, 2024. This email inquired about the status of the payment. The client stated that this communication prompted a review of the June 20, 2024 transaction, leading to the discovery of the fraudulent domain and the altered beneficiary information.

Authentication logs from the client’s online banking portal were reviewed. The logs confirmed that the primary authorized signer logged in on June 20, 2024, and initiated the wire transfer to Aperture Commodities Group LLC. The IP address associated with the login matched the client’s established IP address history. No anomalies were detected in the authentication process itself, suggesting that the client’s credentials were not compromised and that the transaction was initiated by an authorized user acting under deception.

The reviewing analyst obtained call recordings from the bank’s wire department for June 20, 2024. The recordings confirmed that the wire department received the transfer request through the online portal and processed it according to established procedures. There was no telephone contact between the client and the wire department regarding this specific transaction. The wire department’s records confirmed the funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff, consistent with the client’s account of the event.

The reviewing analyst contacted the receiving institution to inquire about the status of the funds. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the wire and stated that a portion of the funds, $465,884.97, was frozen upon notification of the suspected fraud. The remaining funds had already been dispersed prior to the freeze request. The receiving institution declined to provide further details regarding the disposition of the dispersed funds or the account history of Aperture Commodities Group LLC.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Upon notification by Saltmarsh Equipment LLC on June 10, 2024, that the outbound wire transfer was fraudulent, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated recovery efforts. The relationship manager contacted the receiving institution via secure channel, issuing a formal request for indemnification and the immediate freezing or return of the remitted funds. The initial request cited suspected business email compromise and unauthorized diversion of funds intended for Aperture Commodities Group LLC.

The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the indemnification request on June 10, 2024. In their initial response, they indicated that a hold had been placed on the beneficiary account held in the name of Waterstone Logistics Corp., pending their own internal review of the transaction and the account activity. However, they noted that a significant portion of the funds had already been disbursed prior to their receipt of the recall notice. The reviewing analyst noted that the speed of disbursement following the receipt of the wire transfer is a common characteristic of accounts controlled by malicious actors in wire fraud typologies.

Subsequent communication with the receiving institution on June 20, 2024, confirmed the status of the frozen funds. The receiving institution reported that they were able to secure a portion of the original transfer. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was confirmed to be $465,884.97. The receiving institution indicated that they required a formal letter of indemnity from Cortex Bank and Trust, signed by an authorized officer, before they could initiate the return of the secured funds.

Cortex Bank and Trust executed and transmitted the required letter of indemnity on June 28, 2024. The document formalized the bank's commitment to hold the receiving institution harmless against any claims arising from the return of the funds. The process of returning the frozen funds to Cortex Bank and Trust is currently pending completion by the receiving institution. The reviewing analyst continues to monitor the status of the return transfer.

The investigation established that the total fraudulent outbound wire amount was $2,911,781.08. Given that only a portion of the funds was successfully frozen by the receiving institution, Saltmarsh Equipment LLC has sustained a significant financial loss. The residual loss to the customer is $2,445,896.11. This figure represents the portion of the diverted funds that were disbursed by the malicious actors before the receiving institution could implement a freeze on the beneficiary account.

Cortex Bank and Trust has reviewed the circumstances surrounding the initiation and approval of the fraudulent wire transfer. The investigation determined that the wire transfer request was initiated by an authorized user of Saltmarsh Equipment LLC and that the customer successfully completed the bank's required authentication procedures, including dual approval, despite the urgency language in the fraudulent email overriding their own internal controls. The bank executed the wire transfer in accordance with the customer's authenticated instructions.

Based on the findings of the investigation, Cortex Bank and Trust has determined that it is not liable for the loss incurred by Saltmarsh Equipment LLC. The bank's systems and controls functioned as designed, and the fraud was perpetrated through a compromise of the customer's communication channels and internal processes, specifically the failure to identify the lookalike sender domain and the mismatch between the beneficiary name, Waterstone Logistics Corp., and the invoicing vendor, Aperture Commodities Group LLC. The customer has been formally notified of this determination and advised to pursue any further recovery efforts through their own legal counsel, law enforcement, or commercial insurance policies. The relationship manager has provided the customer with documentation of the bank's recovery efforts to assist them in filing any potential insurance claims.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that on June 28, 2024, Saltmarsh Equipment LLC initiated an outbound wire transfer of $2,911,781.08. The funds were directed to an account at another financial institution held by Aperture Commodities Group LLC, an entity with which Saltmarsh Equipment LLC had no prior business relationship. The transfer instructions were received by Saltmarsh Equipment LLC's controller via an email that appeared to originate from a known vendor, Oakhurst Logistics Enterprises LLC, but which utilized a lookalike sender domain differing by a single character. The email communication contained urgency language that prompted the controller to bypass the customer's established dual-approval control for wire transfers. The funds transfer was initiated minutes before the Cortex Bank and Trust daily wire cutoff time. The beneficiary name on the wire instructions did not match the name of the invoicing vendor. The investigation determined that the email communication was fraudulent and that the transfer was induced by deception. Cortex Bank and Trust was able to recover a portion of the funds from the receiving institution, but a substantial residual loss was sustained. As the investigation fixed July 18, 2024 as the date the loss became determinative and the customer has been made aware of the circumstances, no further action is required by Cortex Bank and Trust. The investigation is closed_no_action.
