body:
## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2422
Date opened: July 24, 2024
Subject: Bastion Marine Services Corp. (business), account 73-96983-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: referred_to_fincen

## Case Summary

The Financial Intelligence Unit initiated a review of Cortex Bank and Trust customer Bastion Marine Services Corp. on May 30, 2024. The matter was escalated by the relationship manager following a customer inquiry regarding a missing vendor payment. Bastion Marine Services Corp. holds a commercial checking account, number 73-96983-1, with Cortex Bank and Trust. The customer asserted that a scheduled payment to a long-standing supplier had not been received by the intended beneficiary, despite funds having been debited from the account. The relationship manager’s preliminary review identified a recent high-value wire transfer that appeared to correspond to the customer’s inquiry, prompting the referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit for further investigation into potential wire fraud.

The investigation focused on a single outbound wire transfer in the amount of $2,999,227.97, which posted to the customer's account on May 23, 2024. The customer stated that this transfer was intended to settle an invoice for a major equipment purchase. However, the beneficiary of the wire transfer did not match the name of the expected vendor. The primary objective of the investigation was to determine whether the transfer of $2,999,227.97 was authorized by the customer and directed to the intended recipient, or if the funds were induced out of the account by deception.

The Financial Intelligence Unit established a review period from March 11, 2024 through July 11, 2024, to analyze the account activity leading up to and immediately following the suspect transaction. A review of the customer's historical wire activity was conducted to establish a baseline for typical transaction volumes, frequencies, and beneficiaries. The transaction on May 23, 2024, represented a significant deviation from the customer’s established historical pattern, both in the transaction amount and the beneficiary. The beneficiary of the $2,999,227.97 wire was identified as Emberline Management Group LLC. The customer confirmed to the relationship manager that Emberline Management Group LLC was not a known vendor and that no business relationship existed between Bastion Marine Services Corp. and that entity.

A review of the communication records associated with the wire request revealed that the instructions were received via email. The reviewing analyst noted that the email domain used to transmit the wire instructions closely resembled the domain of the customer's actual vendor, differing by a single character. The email contained language emphasizing the urgency of the payment, which appeared to have circumvented the customer's internal dual-approval controls. Furthermore, the wire transfer was initiated late in the business day, shortly before the daily wire cutoff time.

The investigation sought to trace the flow of funds following the outbound wire transfer. Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution to request the recall of the funds. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the $2,999,227.97 transfer and subsequently reported that a portion of the funds, totaling $629,837.87, had been frozen in the beneficiary's account. The remaining balance of the transferred funds had already been moved out of the receiving institution prior to the recall request.

The analysis of the account activity within the review period also identified prior transactions involving entities named Hearthstone Exports Inc. and Wheatfield Ventures LLC. These transactions occurred on March 18, 2024, March 20, 2024, March 21, 2024, March 25, 2024, March 26, 2024, and April 8, 2024. The investigation assessed these prior transactions to determine if they were related to the suspected fraudulent activity or if they represented legitimate business operations. The relationship manager engaged the customer to clarify the nature of these earlier transactions and to identify any potential connections to the suspect wire transfer to Emberline Management Group LLC. The investigation prioritized confirming the legitimacy of the instructions for the $2,999,227.97 transfer and quantifying the final financial impact on the customer.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On May 23, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust received a formal complaint from a principal of Bastion Marine Services Corp. regarding a wire transfer executed two months prior. The customer alleged that a wire transfer initiated from their account, 73-96983-1, on March 21, 2024, was fraudulently induced. The customer asserted they were the victim of a business email compromise scheme, wherein deceptive communications led them to authorize a payment to an unintended beneficiary. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer’s account was typically used for transactions related to marine logistics and supply chain management, and the transaction in question was purportedly for the settlement of an outstanding invoice with a known vendor.

The customer provided documentation supporting the claim, including a series of email exchanges. The investigation identified that the email correspondence instructing the payment originated from a lookalike sender domain. The customer indicated they believed they were corresponding with their established vendor, Hearthstone Exports Inc. The email instructions directed payment to a new beneficiary, Emberline Management Group LLC, rather than the expected vendor. The reviewing analyst observed that the beneficiary name, Emberline Management Group LLC, did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Hearthstone Exports Inc.

The customer further detailed that the deceptive emails contained urgency language, stressing the immediate need for the funds to secure a critical shipment. This urgency language, according to the customer, was cited as the reason for overriding their internal dual-approval control process for wire transfers. The customer claimed this override was a direct result of the pressure applied in the fraudulent communications. The reviewing analyst noted that the transaction was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time on March 21, 2024.

The customer reported that they only realized the payment had been diverted when the legitimate vendor, Hearthstone Exports Inc., subsequently contacted them on May 23, 2024, to inquire about the unpaid invoice. Upon realizing the error, the customer immediately contacted Cortex Bank and Trust to report the fraud and request a recall of the funds. The reviewing analyst noted that the time lapse between the transaction and the discovery of the fraud was approximately two months.

The customer’s complaint prompted an immediate review of the transaction by the Financial Intelligence Unit. The reviewing analyst confirmed the execution of a single outbound wire transfer from Bastion Marine Services Corp.’s account on the specified date. The wire transfer, in the amount of $2,999,227.97, was directed to the account of Emberline Management Group LLC at an external financial institution. The customer alleged that this entire sum was diverted through deception.

Following the customer’s report, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately issued a recall request to the receiving institution. The receiving institution subsequently confirmed that a portion of the funds, totaling $629,837.87, remained in the beneficiary account and was frozen pending the outcome of the investigation. The customer alleged that the remaining funds, representing a residual loss of $2,369,390.10, had been dissipated by the beneficiary prior to the freeze order.

The reviewing analyst noted that the customer also mentioned previous, legitimate transactions with other entities, including Wheatfield Ventures LLC, during the review period. However, the customer clarified that these transactions were not related to the alleged fraud and were part of their normal business operations. The customer's primary concern remained the March 21, 2024, transaction and the resulting financial loss. The allegation of business email compromise and the subsequent diversion of funds formed the basis for the Financial Intelligence Unit's comprehensive investigation into the matter.

## Timeline of Events

On March 11, 2024, the accounting department at Bastion Marine Services Corp. received an email bearing the sender name of Wheatfield Ventures LLC, an established vendor to the business. The email contained an invoice for a low seven-figure sum and payment instructions. Cortex Bank and Trust investigators later determined that the sender domain used in this communication differed by one character from the legitimate domain of Wheatfield Ventures LLC, a lookalike strategy consistent with business email compromise.

The initial email from the compromised sender was followed by a subsequent communication on March 18, 2024. This second email contained language stressing the urgency of the payment and directed that the funds be wired immediately to avoid disruption to an ongoing service contract. The communication specified that the payment should be routed to an account held by Emberline Management Group LLC at an external domestic financial institution, rather than to the established Wheatfield Ventures LLC account details on file with the customer.

On March 20, 2024, an authorized signer for Bastion Marine Services Corp. logged into the Cortex Bank and Trust corporate banking portal. At 4:22 PM Eastern Time, minutes before the bank's established daily wire cutoff time, the signer initiated an outgoing domestic wire transfer in the amount of $2,999,227.97. The beneficiary was listed as Emberline Management Group LLC. The investigation noted that the transaction was executed by a single user, bypassing the dual-approval control normally required by the customer's portal configuration. The customer later stated this was done in response to the urgency language contained in the March 18, 2024 email. The funds were deducted from Cortex Bank and Trust account 73-96983-1 and successfully transmitted to the receiving institution.

The following day, March 21, 2024, the authorized signer contacted the legitimate Wheatfield Ventures LLC regarding the payment. Wheatfield Ventures LLC confirmed they had not sent the invoice or the subsequent communication and had not received the funds. The customer realized they had been the victim of a business email compromise and immediately contacted their relationship manager at Cortex Bank and Trust.

The relationship manager notified the Cortex Bank and Trust fraud operations team, who initiated a wire recall request with the receiving institution on March 21, 2024. The fraud operations team also requested that the receiving institution place a hold on the beneficiary account.

On March 25, 2024, the receiving institution responded to the recall request, confirming that a portion of the funds had been secured. The receiving institution stated that $629,837.87 had been frozen in the account of Emberline Management Group LLC. The receiving institution further indicated that the remainder of the funds had been depleted through subsequent outgoing wire transfers and could not be recovered. The customer was notified of the partial recovery and the residual loss of $2,369,390.10.

A review of the customer's account activity prior to the incident revealed no prior dealings with Emberline Management Group LLC or Hearthstone Exports Inc. The customer confirmed they had no legitimate business relationship with either entity. The investigation established that the total sum diverted through the deceptive communication was $2,999,227.97. The case was subsequently escalated to the Financial Intelligence Unit for further review and reporting.

## Funds Tracing

The funds tracing element of this investigation focuses on the disposition of the $2,999,227.97 fraudulent outbound wire initiated from the Cortex Bank and Trust account held by Bastion Marine Services Corp. on March 25, 2024. The originating debit was posted to account 73-96983-1. The beneficiary institution was identified as a large national bank. The beneficiary name on the wire instructions was Emberline Management Group LLC, an entity previously unknown to Bastion Marine Services Corp. and not matching the name of the invoicing vendor, Hearthstone Exports Inc.

Information obtained through a 314(b) request to the beneficiary institution confirmed the initial receipt of the $2,999,227.97 on March 25, 2024, into an account held by Emberline Management Group LLC. The receiving institution reported that the funds did not remain in the Emberline Management Group LLC account for a significant duration. On March 26, 2024, the beneficiary institution observed onward movement of the funds. The reviewing analyst notes that this rapid onward movement is consistent with attempts to obscure the origin and ultimate destination of illicit proceeds.

The beneficiary institution's records indicate that a significant portion of the funds was transferred via domestic wire to another account held at a different regional bank. The beneficiary of this secondary wire was identified as Wheatfield Ventures LLC. The exact amount of this secondary transfer was not disclosed in the 314(b) response, but the beneficiary institution characterized it as representing the majority of the initial deposit.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a subsequent 314(b) request to the regional bank holding the Wheatfield Ventures LLC account. The response from this institution confirmed the receipt of funds from Emberline Management Group LLC. However, the trail of the funds became fragmented at this stage. The regional bank reported that the funds received into the Wheatfield Ventures LLC account were rapidly dissipated through a series of smaller wire transfers and automated clearing house disbursements to numerous, disparate beneficiaries.

These subsequent beneficiaries included various corporate entities and individuals, none of which appeared to have a logical business connection to Wheatfield Ventures LLC, Emberline Management Group LLC, Hearthstone Exports Inc., or Bastion Marine Services Corp. The regional bank indicated that the volume and velocity of these disbursements made further tracing highly complex. The reviewing analyst infers that this fragmentation was a deliberate strategy to complicate recovery efforts and obfuscate the final disposition of the funds.

Following the initial notification of the suspected fraud by Bastion Marine Services Corp., Cortex Bank and Trust immediately issued a recall request for the original $2,999,227.97 wire. The beneficiary institution placed a hold on the Emberline Management Group LLC account. However, due to the rapid onward movement of the funds, only $629,837.87 remained in the account at the time the hold was executed. The beneficiary institution confirmed that these funds were successfully frozen and are pending return to Cortex Bank and Trust, subject to their internal indemnification procedures.

The successful freezing of a portion of the funds mitigates the total impact, but a substantial residual loss remains. The investigation established that $2,369,390.10 was successfully diverted and dissipated through the network of accounts, primarily originating from the subsequent transfers out of the Wheatfield Ventures LLC account. The ultimate destination and form of these diverted funds, whether converted to cash, cryptocurrency, or other assets, cannot be definitively established based on the available information from the responding institutions. The tracing trail ends with the fragmented disbursements from the Wheatfield Ventures LLC account, as further hops involve numerous institutions and counterparties beyond the scope of current information sharing responses.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary of the outbound wire transfer from the account of Bastion Marine Services Corp. was identified as Emberline Management Group LLC. Analysis of the receiving account, held at a different domestic financial institution, indicated that it was established on March 11, 2024. This date was nine days prior to the receipt of the $2,999,227.97 wire transfer on March 20, 2024, a sequence of events sometimes observed in cases where an account is established specifically to receive misappropriated funds. The stated business purpose for Emberline Management Group LLC, as recorded by the receiving institution, was management consulting services. This business description did not align with the nature of the transaction described in the fraudulent invoice presented to Bastion Marine Services Corp., which purported to be for the procurement of maritime specialized equipment.

Registry research conducted on Emberline Management Group LLC revealed that the entity was formed on March 11, 2024, the same day the receiving account was opened. The registered agent address was determined to be a commercial mail receiving agency. Public record searches did not yield any evidence of a physical operating presence for Emberline Management Group LLC, nor did they identify any website, advertising, or other indicia of a legitimate consulting business. The absence of a verifiable business footprint for an entity receiving a transfer approaching three million dollars was considered unusual and warranted further scrutiny of the account activity.

A review of the transaction history for the Emberline Management Group LLC account, obtained through collaboration with the receiving institution, showed minimal activity between the account opening date and the receipt of the wire transfer from Bastion Marine Services Corp. The initial funding consisted of a nominal cash deposit. Following the credit of the $2,999,227.97 on March 20, 2024, the account exhibited rapid depletion. On March 21, 2024, an outbound wire transfer of a mid-six-figure sum was initiated to an account held in the name of Hearthstone Exports Inc. at a third domestic financial institution. Subsequent analysis of Hearthstone Exports Inc. indicated it was also a recently formed entity with no discernible business operations.

Further disbursements from the Emberline Management Group LLC account occurred on March 25, 2024, and March 26, 2024, involving several large-dollar transfers to various domestic counterparties, including Wheatfield Ventures LLC. These transfers, while individually smaller than the transfer to Hearthstone Exports Inc., collectively accounted for a significant portion of the remaining funds. The velocity of these outbound transfers, occurring within days of the initial credit, is consistent with attempts to distance funds from their source. The receiving institution reported that the counterparties receiving these funds, including Wheatfield Ventures LLC, also exhibited characteristics of recently established entities with limited operational history.

The pattern of credits and debits on the Emberline Management Group LLC account did not appear consistent with the stated business purpose of management consulting. There were no observed payroll expenses, vendor payments typical of a consulting firm, or tax remittances. The activity was primarily characterized by the receipt of a single large incoming wire followed by immediate, rapid disbursements to other domestic entities with opaque ownership and operational structures. This flow of funds, combined with the lack of a verifiable business presence for Emberline Management Group LLC, suggested that the entity and its account were utilized primarily as a conduit for the movement of funds following the initial transfer from Bastion Marine Services Corp.

By the time the receiving institution initiated a freeze on the Emberline Management Group LLC account following the notification of the suspected fraud, the balance had been significantly depleted. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $629,837.87. The rapid movement of funds to secondary and tertiary counterparties like Hearthstone Exports Inc. and Wheatfield Ventures LLC complicated recovery efforts and highlighted the orchestrated nature of the post-transfer activity.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The investigation included a review of the email correspondence provided by the customer. The customer supplied a chain of messages culminating in the authorization of the wire transfer of $2,999,227.97 on May 30, 2024. The reviewing analyst examined the email headers for the message purporting to originate from Hearthstone Exports Inc. The analysis revealed that the sender's email address utilized a domain name differing from the vendor's actual domain by a single transposed character. The spoofed domain was registered shortly before the fraudulent communication commenced, which is consistent with the preparation for a business email compromise scheme.

The fraudulent emails contained language creating a false sense of urgency, stating that the goods would not be released from port unless the funds were received immediately. The customer's internal procedures require dual approval for transactions exceeding a predetermined threshold. However, an interview with the customer's controller established that this control was bypassed due to the perceived urgency conveyed in the emails. The controller stated that the president of Bastion Marine Services Corp. authorized the transaction based on the belief that immediate payment was necessary to avoid significant supply chain disruptions.

The investigation reviewed the invoice attached to the fraudulent email. The invoice appeared to be a modified version of a legitimate invoice previously issued by Hearthstone Exports Inc. The analyst observed that while the invoice format and logo were consistent with prior legitimate invoices, the payment instructions had been altered. The beneficiary name provided on the altered invoice was Emberline Management Group LLC, which did not correspond to the invoicing vendor, Hearthstone Exports Inc. The customer's controller indicated during the interview that this discrepancy was noted but disregarded due to the urgency expressed in the accompanying email and the belief that Emberline Management Group LLC was a subsidiary or payment processor for the vendor.

Cortex Bank and Trust's wire transfer authentication logs were examined for the May 30, 2024 transaction. The logs indicate that the wire transfer request for $2,999,227.97 was initiated via the bank's online platform. The analyst noted that the transfer was initiated minutes before the daily wire cutoff time. This timing is a common tactic employed in wire fraud schemes to minimize the window for the victim or the financial institution to detect the anomaly and recall the funds. The authentication logs confirm that the customer's credentials were used to initiate the transfer, and there was no evidence of unauthorized access to the customer's online banking profile.

Following the customer's report of the suspected fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution to request a freeze on the funds. The receiving institution confirmed that a portion of the funds had already been disbursed or transferred out of the beneficiary account. The receiving institution was able to freeze a remaining balance. The investigation established that the amount frozen at the receiving institution was $629,837.87. This action mitigated the total loss, resulting in a residual loss to the customer of $2,369,390.10.

The investigation also reviewed correspondence related to Wheatfield Ventures LLC. The customer's controller stated that Wheatfield Ventures LLC was another vendor they frequently engaged with. The customer provided email correspondence indicating that the threat actor had also attempted to compromise communications related to Wheatfield Ventures LLC, using similar tactics of spoofed domains and altered payment instructions. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer recognized the suspicious nature of these communications and did not initiate any funds transfers based on those instructions. This incident highlights the targeted nature of the attacks against the customer's vendor communications.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

The relationship manager for Bastion Marine Services Corp. initiated a wire recall request through the Cortex Bank and Trust wire operations department on May 23, 2024, immediately following the customer's assertion that the wire instructions were fraudulent. The recall request cited suspected wire fraud and requested the immediate return of the $2,999,227.97 transferred to Wheatfield Ventures LLC. The request also included a formal letter of indemnity from Cortex Bank and Trust, holding the receiving institution harmless for the return of the funds. The reviewing analyst noted that the recall request was transmitted within two hours of the customer's notification to the bank.

The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request on May 30, 2024. In its response, the receiving institution indicated that the account held by Wheatfield Ventures LLC had been frozen, but that a significant portion of the funds had already been disbursed prior to the receipt of the recall notice. The receiving institution confirmed that $629,837.87 remained in the account and was successfully frozen. The response further stated that the remaining funds had been transferred to unknown third parties, and the receiving institution was unable to compel the return of those funds from subsequent receiving banks.

The reviewing analyst assessed the receiving institution's response and determined that the funds frozen represented a partial recovery of the original wire transfer amount. The $629,837.87 was subsequently returned to Cortex Bank and Trust on May 2, 2023, and credited back to the Bastion Marine Services Corp. account. The return of these funds mitigated the total loss incurred by the customer, but a substantial shortfall remained.

The residual loss to Bastion Marine Services Corp. was calculated as the original wire amount less the funds successfully recovered from the receiving institution. This residual loss amounted to $2,369,390.10. The reviewing analyst documented this figure as the confirmed financial impact of the suspected fraud event on the customer. The customer was formally notified of the partial recovery and the outstanding residual loss.

Following the partial recovery, the customer inquired about potential reimbursement for the residual loss from Cortex Bank and Trust. The reviewing analyst consulted with the bank's legal and compliance departments regarding the customer's reimbursement request. It was determined that the bank had executed the wire transfer in accordance with the instructions provided by the authorized signers on the Bastion Marine Services Corp. account, and that the bank's internal controls, including dual approval, had been bypassed at the customer's insistence due to the urgency language in the fraudulent communication.

Consequently, Cortex Bank and Trust declined to reimburse the customer for the residual loss of $2,369,390.10. The bank's position was that the loss resulted from the customer's internal compromise and their subsequent authorization of the transfer, rather than any failure or negligence on the part of the bank. The customer was advised to pursue recovery through their own corporate insurance policies or through civil litigation against the suspected perpetrators, should they be identified. The reviewing analyst noted that the customer indicated they would be filing a claim with their cyber insurance provider. The bank provided the customer with a summary of the investigation findings to support their insurance claim.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Bastion Marine Services Corp. sustained a loss of $2,999,227.97 as a result of wire fraud. The activity is consistent with a business email compromise scheme. Review of the communication records provided by the customer indicated that the fraudulent instructions originated from a lookalike sender domain differing by one character from the legitimate vendor's domain. The instructions employed urgency language, which the customer stated was the reason they overrode their internal dual-approval control for wire transfers. The funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time. The beneficiary name, Emberline Management Group LLC, did not match the invoicing vendor, which the customer identified as Hearthstone Exports Inc. The customer was unable to substantiate any legitimate business purpose for a transfer to Emberline Management Group LLC. The investigation fixed July 8, 2024 as the date the customer became aware of the diversion, following inquiries from the legitimate vendor regarding the unpaid invoice. Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request with the receiving institution. The receiving institution confirmed that a portion of the funds remained in the beneficiary account. The residual loss to the customer was $2,369,390.10. The matter was referred_to_fincen.

body:
## Report Header

Cortex Bank and Trust - Financial Intelligence Unit
Investigation report: FIU-WIRE-2423
Date opened: November 13, 2024
Subject: Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. (business), account 77-85818-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: criminal_referral

## Case Summary

On October 9, 2024, the Financial Intelligence Unit received an expedited escalation from the commercial banking division concerning anomalous wire transfer activity on account 77-85818-1, held by Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. The escalation detailed a customer-reported loss stemming from a wire transfer that Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. asserted was induced by deception. The relationship manager noted that the customer contacted the bank earlier that day, stating they had remitted funds based on what they now believed were fraudulent payment instructions. The Financial Intelligence Unit subsequently opened an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the transfer, the total funds diverted, and the viability of any recovery efforts.

The investigation centered on an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $4,062,937.17, initiated on October 9, 2024. This transaction was identified by the customer as the focal point of the suspected fraud. The primary objective of the review was to establish whether the activity was consistent with wire fraud, specifically an instance where a customer was manipulated into directing funds to an unintended beneficiary. The review period for this matter was established as July 11, 2024 through November 14, 2024, to encompass the transaction date and provide a baseline for the customer's typical wire activity.

Initial review of the escalation indicated that the customer, Glenhaven Fabrication Inc., had intended to remit payment to an established vendor. However, the customer reported that the payment instructions they utilized directed the $4,062,937.17 to a beneficiary they did not intend to pay. The investigation was tasked with evaluating the communications and internal processes at Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. that led to the execution of the wire transfer, to the extent such information could be obtained from the customer. The reviewing analyst noted that the escalation described a scenario where the funds were moved by wire, consistent with the suspected typology of funds induced out of a customer account by deception.

The investigation sought to answer several key questions, including the origin of the fraudulent instructions, the identity of the beneficiary, and the sequence of events leading up to the transaction. The Financial Intelligence Unit also needed to verify the customer's claim that the funds were diverted from their intended destination. A critical component of the inquiry was the immediate initiation of recall procedures in an attempt to secure the transferred funds. The investigation would track the progress of these efforts, communicating with the receiving institution to ascertain if any portion of the $4,062,937.17 could be frozen or returned.

The escalation from the commercial banking division provided the initial framework for the investigation. The relationship manager relayed the customer's assertion that they were the victim of a targeted deception. The Financial Intelligence Unit was tasked with substantiating this claim by analyzing the transaction details and any supporting documentation provided by Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. The investigation would also review the account's historical wire activity, noting any transactions with counterparties such as Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd., Anvil Metals Trading Co., or Umberfield Textiles Group LLC, to determine if the October 9, 2024 transaction deviated from established patterns. The focus remained on the specific circumstances surrounding the $4,062,937.17 wire transfer and the mechanisms by which the customer was purportedly induced to initiate it.

## Allegation and Referral Source

On October 9, 2024, the Cortex Bank and Trust Financial Intelligence Unit received an escalation from the commercial banking relationship manager assigned to Glenhaven Fabrication Inc., regarding a potentially fraudulent outbound wire transfer. The relationship manager reported that a representative of Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. had contacted them earlier that day, asserting that a wire transfer initiated from the company’s operating account, ending in 85818-1, had been induced by a deceptive communication and sent to a beneficiary not intended by the company. The customer alleged that the payment, intended to settle an invoice with a known vendor, had been misdirected due to compromised email communications.

The relationship manager relayed that the customer believed the fraudulent activity stemmed from an email interaction they thought was with a representative of Anvil Metals Trading Co., a regular supplier. According to the customer's account, they received an email on October 9, 2024, containing an invoice and updated payment instructions. The customer stated that this email appeared to originate from a known contact at Anvil Metals Trading Co., but upon later review, the sender's domain was found to be a lookalike, differing by a single character from the legitimate vendor's domain. The customer indicated that the fraudulent email contained language emphasizing the urgency of the payment to secure a critical shipment of materials, which the customer cited as the reason they bypassed their internal dual-approval controls for wire transfers.

The escalation detailed that the customer, acting on the fraudulent instructions, initiated an outbound wire transfer in the amount of $4,062,937.17. The customer reported that the transfer was submitted shortly before the daily wire cutoff time on October 9, 2024. The relationship manager noted that the customer only realized the error when the actual representative from Anvil Metals Trading Co. contacted them later to inquire about the status of the expected payment. At that point, the customer reviewed the wire confirmation and observed that the beneficiary name on the transfer did not match Anvil Metals Trading Co., the invoicing vendor.

Upon receiving the escalation, the reviewing analyst confirmed that the wire transfer in question, totaling $4,062,937.17, had been successfully processed from the Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. account. The analyst noted that the beneficiary of the wire transfer was listed as Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd., an entity with no prior transaction history with Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. in the preceding six months. The analyst further confirmed that the transfer was initiated by a registered user on the Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. account and that the transaction had not triggered any automated alerts within the bank's transaction monitoring system prior to processing.

The relationship manager also provided information suggesting that Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. may have been targeted by a broader Business Email Compromise campaign. The customer mentioned to the relationship manager that they had recently received suspicious emails purporting to be from other vendors, including Umberfield Textiles Group LLC, though no payments had been made in response to those communications. The customer was unable to substantiate whether these other emails were linked to the same actors responsible for the fraudulent instructions regarding Anvil Metals Trading Co.

Following the initial contact from the customer, the relationship manager submitted a formal internal referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit, prompting the commencement of this investigation. The referral requested an immediate review of the transaction and the initiation of efforts to recall the funds. The reviewing analyst initiated a case within the bank's case management system, referencing internal identifier FIU-WIRE-2423, to document the investigation into the alleged wire fraud and coordinate with relevant internal departments and external financial institutions.

## Timeline of Events

The first action of consequence within the review period occurred on July 11, 2024. The relationship manager for Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. received a telephone call from an individual identifying themselves as the chief financial officer of the business. The caller inquired about the bank's procedures for initiating large-value, same-day domestic wire transfers. The caller indicated that a significant payment to a supplier, Anvil Metals Trading Co., would likely be necessary before the end of the month to secure favorable pricing on raw materials. The relationship manager explained the dual-approval requirements and the cutoff times for same-day processing. This interaction was documented in the customer relationship management system.

On July 23, 2024, the relationship manager received an email ostensibly from the chief financial officer of Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. The email sender domain, however, was a lookalike domain differing by one character from the customer's registered domain. The email referenced the earlier telephone conversation and stated that the payment to the supplier was now urgent and required execution by July 30, 2024. The email contained instructions for a wire transfer of $4,062,937.17. The stated beneficiary was Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd., not Anvil Metals Trading Co. The relationship manager replied to the email, requesting the standard authorization form.

A completed authorization form was received via email on July 30, 2024. The signature on the form appeared to match the signature card on file for the chief financial officer. The email accompanying the form contained language emphasizing the urgency of the transaction, stating that failure to execute the wire that day would result in severe supply chain disruptions and a breach of contract with Umberfield Textiles Group LLC. This urgency language appeared intended to override the established dual-approval control, as the email demanded immediate processing without secondary verification from another authorized signer on the account.

The funds transfer of $4,062,937.17 was initiated by the wire department on July 30, 2024, minutes before the daily wire cutoff. The transaction was processed and the funds were transmitted to the receiving institution. The beneficiary account was held in the name of Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd.

On August 15, 2024, the legitimate chief financial officer of Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. contacted the relationship manager to inquire about a discrepancy in their account balance. The customer stated they had not authorized the July 30 wire transfer and had no business relationship with Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. The customer confirmed they had expected to make a payment to Anvil Metals Trading Co., but that payment had not yet been processed. The bank immediately initiated an investigation and submitted a request to the receiving institution to recall the funds.

The receiving institution responded on August 20, 2024, indicating they were able to secure only a portion of the transmitted funds. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $1,015,734.29. The receiving institution reported that the remainder of the funds had already been dispersed.

The bank's Financial Intelligence Unit commenced a formal review of the incident on August 29, 2024. The reviewing analyst analyzed the email communications, the authorization form, and the wire transfer details. The analyst identified the lookalike domain and noted the discrepancy between the beneficiary name on the wire instructions and the expected supplier name.

On September 13, 2024, the bank formally notified the customer that $3,047,202.88 of the transferred funds could not be recovered. The investigation established this amount as the residual loss to the customer. The customer was advised to contact law enforcement.

The reviewing analyst finalized the compilation of evidence on September 23, 2024. The investigation confirmed that the funds were induced out of the customer account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay. The timeline of events and supporting documentation were prepared for internal review. The case was advanced to the final review stage on October 9, 2024.

## Funds Tracing

On September 23, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust originated an outgoing domestic wire transfer in the amount of $4,062,937.17, drawing on the operating account of Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. The transfer instructions directed the funds to an account held in the name of Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. at a large regional bank in the southeast United States. The wire instructions included routing and account numbers that were correctly formatted for the destination bank, and the transfer was executed successfully through the Federal Reserve Wire Network. A review of the outgoing message format confirmed that the beneficiary name supplied by the initiator was Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd., not Anvil Metals Trading Co., which the customer later identified as the intended recipient of the payment. The reviewing analyst noted that the transfer was authorized and transmitted shortly before the daily wire cutoff time on that date.

Cortex Bank and Trust received notification from the customer regarding the suspected fraudulent nature of the wire transfer on October 9, 2024. The bank immediately initiated a recall request through the Federal Reserve system. The receiving institution responded to the recall request, indicating that the beneficiary account had been frozen. The receiving institution confirmed that $1,015,734.29 remained in the account and had been secured pursuant to the hold. The receiving institution declined to provide specific details regarding the disposition of the remaining funds, citing privacy restrictions. The reviewing analyst inferred that the balance of the wired funds had been moved out of the Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. account prior to the placement of the freeze. The investigation established that the residual loss sustained by Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. as a result of the fraudulent transfer was $3,047,202.88.

Cortex Bank and Trust subsequently engaged in communication with the fraud department of the receiving institution in an attempt to trace the onward movement of the missing funds. Information provided verbally by a representative of the receiving institution suggested that significant outbound wire activity from the Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. account occurred in the days immediately following the receipt of the initial transfer. The receiving institution indicated that a portion of these outbound transfers was directed to domestic accounts, while another portion was transmitted internationally. The receiving institution declined to identify the specific beneficiary accounts or the destination institutions for these onward transfers. The reviewing analyst noted that the rapid dissipation of funds following receipt is consistent with common typologies for the laundering of proceeds derived from business email compromise schemes.

The reviewing analyst examined historical account activity for Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. to determine if any previous transfers to Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. had occurred. The review of the period from July 11, 2024, to November 14, 2024, did not identify any prior transactions between the customer and that entity. The customer confirmed during the course of the investigation that they had no prior business relationship with Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. and that the payment was intended to satisfy an invoice ostensibly issued by Anvil Metals Trading Co. The customer provided documentation indicating that they had conducted legitimate business with Umberfield Textiles Group LLC during the review period; however, no funds transfers to that entity were identified that appeared related to the fraudulent activity under review. The trail of the diverted funds remains obscured beyond the initial receiving account at the domestic regional bank. The investigation could not confirm whether the funds were subsequently converted to cash, cashier's checks, or other negotiable instruments, or whether they were further transmitted through the international financial system.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

The beneficiary of the fraudulent outbound wire transfer was identified as Anvil Metals Trading Co., receiving the funds at an account held at an external financial institution. Open-source research was conducted to verify the existence and legitimacy of this entity. The investigation found a corporate registration for Anvil Metals Trading Co. established on July 11, 2024, in a state known for relaxed corporate transparency requirements. This date of incorporation is notably proximate to the fraudulent activity, occurring just weeks prior to the transaction in question. The registered agent address provided for Anvil Metals Trading Co. was determined to be a commercial mail-receiving agency, a common characteristic of shell companies designed to obscure beneficial ownership. No physical business address or operational footprint could be established through public records or commercially available databases.

A review of the external financial institution's records, obtained through a 314(b) information-sharing request, revealed the account for Anvil Metals Trading Co. was opened on July 23, 2024. The stated business purpose at account opening was described generally as international commodities brokerage. However, an analysis of the account activity did not align with this stated purpose. Prior to the receipt of the $4,062,937.17 wire from Glenhaven Fabrication Inc., the account exhibited minimal activity. The only credits were small, round-dollar deposits, characteristic of test transactions used to verify account functionality. There was no evidence of regular operational expenses, payroll, or typical business-to-business transactions that would substantiate an active commodities brokerage.

The receipt of the funds from Cortex Bank and Trust on August 29, 2024, marked a significant deviation from the established, albeit brief, account history. Immediately following the credit, the funds began to dissipate rapidly. Within two days, the external institution observed multiple outward wire transfers. A review of the transaction details for these outward wires indicated a pattern of rapid disbursement to various secondary beneficiaries. The investigation noted that a low six-figure sum was directed to Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. Open-source research on this entity revealed it to be registered in a jurisdiction known as a high-risk offshore financial center. The rapid movement of funds to an offshore entity is consistent with efforts to launder illicit proceeds and complicate recovery efforts.

Another significant portion of the funds, amounting to several thousand dollars, was transferred to Umberfield Textiles Group LLC. This transfer is notable due to the incongruity between the stated business of Anvil Metals Trading Co. (commodities brokerage) and the apparent industry of the receiving entity (textiles). This lack of apparent economic or business rationale further supports the assessment that the account of Anvil Metals Trading Co. was utilized primarily as a conduit for illicit funds. The external financial institution initiated a freeze on the account, successfully securing a portion of the funds. The rapid dissipation of the remaining balance highlights the swift nature of the suspected laundering cycle following the initial fraudulent transfer. The pattern of activity observed in the Anvil Metals Trading Co. account, characterized by recent establishment, use of a commercial mail-receiving agency, lack of typical business transactions, and rapid disbursement of a large influx of funds to seemingly unrelated entities and offshore jurisdictions, strongly suggests the account was established and operated for the purpose of receiving and laundering the proceeds of wire fraud.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The investigation involved extensive interviews with personnel at Glenhaven Fabrication Inc., specifically focusing on the events preceding the $4,062,937.17 outbound wire transfer. The relationship manager conducted initial inquiries with the customer's controller and accounts payable manager on October 9, 2024. These interviews were intended to establish the customer's understanding of the transaction's purpose and the authorization procedures followed. The customer maintained that the transfer was intended for a long-standing supplier, Umberfield Textiles Group LLC, to settle a large materials invoice.

During these interviews, the customer disclosed that the wire instructions were received via email. The reviewing analyst requested copies of the email correspondence, the invoice in question, and any related communications. The customer provided printouts of the email thread on October 9, 2024. A review of these documents revealed that the emails, ostensibly from Umberfield Textiles Group LLC, originated from a lookalike sender domain. The domain used in the fraudulent emails differed from the legitimate vendor's domain by a single character.

The emails provided by the customer contained urgency language, specifically citing a critical supply chain disruption and demanding immediate payment to secure materials. The customer's accounts payable manager stated during the interview that this urgency prompted a deviation from their standard dual-approval control for large transfers. The customer indicated that the urgency expressed in the emails, coupled with the perceived importance of the vendor relationship, led to the circumvention of established internal procedures.

The invoice provided by the customer, which accompanied the fraudulent email instructions, was also examined. The invoice appeared to mirror previous invoices from Umberfield Textiles Group LLC in format and branding. However, the beneficiary name listed on the provided payment instructions did not match the invoicing vendor. The wire instructions directed funds to Anvil Metals Trading Co., an entity previously unknown to the customer. The customer was unable to substantiate any legitimate business relationship with Anvil Metals Trading Co.

Cortex Bank and Trust obtained and reviewed the call recordings between the customer's representative and the bank's wire department. The recordings from September 23, 2024, confirmed that the customer's representative verbally authorized the $4,062,937.17 transfer. The representative reiterated the urgency of the payment during the call, aligning with the language used in the fraudulent emails. The call recordings also confirmed that the customer requested the transfer be processed immediately, resulting in the funds transfer being initiated minutes before the bank's wire cutoff time.

Authentication logs for the customer's online banking session on September 23, 2024, were reviewed. The logs showed a successful login using the established credentials of the authorized user. No anomalies, such as unrecognized IP addresses or multiple failed login attempts, were identified in the authentication logs preceding the wire request. This suggests that the customer's online banking credentials were not compromised in this instance, and the authorization was executed by the legitimate user acting on fraudulent instructions.

Following the discovery of the fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution in an attempt to recover the funds. The reviewing analyst obtained documentation from the receiving institution regarding the status of the transferred funds. The documentation indicated that a portion of the funds, $1,015,734.29, remained in the beneficiary account at Anvil Metals Trading Co. and had been frozen at the receiving institution. The receiving institution provided transaction records showing that the remaining funds had been rapidly disbursed shortly after receipt.

The customer was interviewed again by the relationship manager regarding their relationship with Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd., another entity identified during the investigation of related transfers. The customer stated they had no prior dealings with Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. and could not explain why this entity might be associated with the transactions under review. The customer was unable to provide any documentation or correspondence linking Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. to Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd. or Anvil Metals Trading Co.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

Upon notification of the suspected wire fraud on November 13, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust immediately initiated a wire recall request through the Fedwire system. The request identified the outbound wire of $4,062,937.17 to the receiving institution, citing suspected fraud. Concurrent with the Fedwire message, the reviewing analyst contacted the receiving institution's fraud department by telephone to provide supplemental context and request a hold on the beneficiary account. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the recall request and placed a temporary freeze on the beneficiary account.

Subsequent communication with the receiving institution on November 14, 2024, revealed that a significant portion of the funds had already been disbursed from the beneficiary account. The receiving institution confirmed that $1,015,734.29 remained in the account and was successfully frozen pursuant to the hold request. These funds were secured pending the execution of a formal indemnification agreement. Cortex Bank and Trust transmitted the standard hold harmless agreement to the receiving institution later that day, providing the necessary legal assurances to facilitate the return of the frozen funds.

The receiving institution indicated that the disbursed funds had been transferred to multiple secondary beneficiaries prior to the receipt of the recall request. Due to the rapid dissipation of funds, typical of such fraud schemes, the receiving institution stated that recovery of the disbursed amounts was highly unlikely. The reviewing analyst documented the receiving institution's confirmation that no further funds were available for recovery from the primary beneficiary account.

The successful freeze of a portion of the transferred funds resulted in a partial mitigation of the total loss. The residual loss to the customer, representing the unrecovered portion of the wire, was calculated at $3,047,202.88. The relationship manager contacted the principals of Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. to communicate the status of the recovery efforts. The customer was informed of the successful freeze of a portion of the funds and the confirmation from the receiving institution that the remaining balance had been disbursed.

The customer inquired about potential reimbursement from Cortex Bank and Trust for the residual loss. The reviewing analyst, in consultation with the legal department, reviewed the customer's account agreement and the specific circumstances surrounding the wire transfer. The review confirmed that the customer had initiated the wire transfer through the online banking portal, utilizing their established credentials. The funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time, and the customer had authorized the transaction, albeit under fraudulent inducement.

Based on the review of the transaction initiation and authorization process, Cortex Bank and Trust determined that the bank had executed the wire transfer in accordance with the customer's instructions and within established operational procedures. The bank concluded that it bore no liability for the loss, as the customer had authorized the transaction and the bank had fulfilled its obligations under the account agreement. The customer was formally notified in writing that Cortex Bank and Trust would not provide reimbursement for the residual loss of $3,047,202.88.

The customer was advised to pursue recovery through their own commercial insurance policies, specifically those covering cybercrime or social engineering fraud. The reviewing analyst provided the customer with the necessary documentation, including copies of the wire transfer records and correspondence with the receiving institution, to support their insurance claim. The bank also recommended that the customer engage legal counsel to explore potential avenues for recovery directly from the perpetrators or other involved parties. The return of the frozen funds, totaling $1,015,734.29, is pending the finalization and execution of the indemnification agreement by both institutions. The reviewing analyst will monitor the return process and update the case file upon receipt of the funds.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Glenhaven Fabrication Inc. was the victim of a business email compromise resulting in a fraudulent wire transfer on October 31, 2024. The reviewing analyst determined that a bad actor, using a lookalike sender domain differing by a single character from an established vendor, submitted fraudulent payment instructions. The communication employed urgency language that successfully induced the customer to override their internal dual-approval control. The funds transfer was initiated minutes before the wire cutoff time. The beneficiary name on the transfer instructions, Tidewater Commodities Holdings Ltd., did not match the invoicing vendor, Anvil Metals Trading Co. The sum established as diverted was $4,062,937.17. While Cortex Bank and Trust was able to coordinate with the receiving institution to freeze a portion of the funds, the residual loss to the customer remained substantial. The customer was unable to substantiate any legitimate business relationship with the beneficiary entity. Based on the identified deception and the resulting material loss, the activity is consistent with wire fraud. The disposition of this matter is criminal_referral.
