Date opened: September 13, 2024
Subject: Wilhelmina Braithwaite (individual), account 84-61695-1
Matter type: wire fraud
Disposition: ongoing

## Case Summary

This investigation was initiated on August 8, 2024, following a referral from the Cortex Bank and Trust Wire Operations group concerning an outbound domestic funds transfer from the commercial checking account of Wilhelmina Braithwaite, account number 84-61695-1. The referral indicated that the customer contacted the bank on that date to report that a wire transfer authorized and transmitted on July 30, 2024, in the amount of $103,582.40, was sent in error. The customer stated she had intended to remit payment to a known vendor, Emberline Imports LLC, but had subsequently learned from that vendor that payment had not been received. The customer indicated she believed her email communications with the vendor had been intercepted and altered by an unknown third party, causing her to direct the funds to an incorrect account and beneficiary. The Financial Intelligence Unit opened the matter to review the transaction, assess the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the wire, and determine if the activity was consistent with wire fraud. The review period for this investigation was established as May 16, 2024, through September 13, 2024, to encompass historical account activity and allow for the assessment of relevant counterparties.

The referral detailed that the transaction in question, for $103,582.40, was initiated via the bank's online commercial banking portal. The initiation occurred late in the business day, shortly before the bank's established wire cutoff time. The beneficiary on the transaction was listed as Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co., an entity not previously observed in the transaction history for account 84-61695-1. The customer reported to the bank that she had received an email appearing to be from Emberline Imports LLC, a vendor with which she had an established relationship, containing an invoice and payment instructions. The customer stated the email contained language stressing the urgency of the payment to secure a pending shipment, which prompted her to bypass her customary internal dual-approval procedure for outbound wires. The customer asserted she did not notice the discrepancy between the expected vendor name and the beneficiary name entered in the wire instructions until the intended vendor notified her of non-payment.

Upon receipt of the customer's report on August 8, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust Wire Operations immediately transmitted a recall request to the receiving institution, citing suspected fraud. The receiving institution acknowledged the recall request but indicated that the majority of the funds had already been depleted from the beneficiary account. The receiving institution confirmed that a remaining balance of $20,716.48 was successfully frozen and would be returned to Cortex Bank and Trust. The customer was notified that the remaining balance of the transfer was considered unrecoverable at that time. The primary objective of the Financial Intelligence Unit investigation was to review the transaction details, the customer's statements, and the associated communications to evaluate the likelihood that the customer was the victim of a business email compromise scheme resulting in the fraudulent diversion of funds. The investigation sought to confirm the details of the communication that induced the payment and to identify the recipient of the diverted funds, Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co.

## Allegation and Referral Source

The investigation was initiated following a referral received by Cortex Bank and Trust on August 23, 2024, concerning suspected wire fraud involving the account of Wilhelmina Braithwaite. The referral originated from the customer’s relationship manager, who reported that Ms. Braithwaite had contacted the bank earlier that day, stating she had been the victim of a business email compromise scheme. According to the relationship manager's initial report, Ms. Braithwaite alleged she had remitted a substantial payment, $103,582.40, intended for a known vendor, Emberline Imports LLC, but had subsequently learned the funds were diverted to an unauthorized beneficiary.

Ms. Braithwaite claimed that on August 8, 2024, she received an email appearing to be from her regular contact at Emberline Imports LLC. The email contained an invoice for heavy machinery parts and requested payment by wire transfer. The customer stated that the email included revised payment instructions, directing funds to a new account held in the name of Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. The customer reported that she did not notice that the sender's email domain, while resembling that of Emberline Imports LLC, differed by a single character. The customer alleged that she believed the email and the revised payment instructions were legitimate and proceeded to initiate the wire transfer.

The customer further stated that the fraudulent email contained language urging immediate payment to secure the shipment, which she claimed influenced her decision to bypass her company's internal dual-approval controls for wire transfers. She alleged that she authorized the wire transfer of $103,582.40 on August 8, 2024, minutes before the bank's daily wire cutoff time. The customer reported that she only realized the payment had been misdirected on August 23, 2024, when the genuine vendor, Emberline Imports LLC, contacted her regarding the outstanding invoice.

Upon realizing the error, Ms. Braithwaite contacted her relationship manager at Cortex Bank and Trust to report the suspected fraud and request assistance in recovering the funds. The relationship manager immediately escalated the matter to the Financial Intelligence Unit, prompting the commencement of this investigation. The initial review of the referral confirmed that a wire transfer in the amount of $103,582.40 had been executed from Ms. Braithwaite's account on August 8, 2024, directed to an account held by Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. at an external financial institution.

The referral indicated that the customer had been unable to contact the purported vendor at the email address from which the fraudulent instructions were received. The customer also stated she had no prior business relationship with Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. and had not authorized any payments to that entity. The referral noted that the beneficiary name on the wire transfer instructions, Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co., did not match the name of the invoicing vendor, Emberline Imports LLC, nor did it match the name of a related entity, Emberline Equipment LLC, with which the customer also conducted business.

The allegation presented in the referral suggests that the customer was deceived into authorizing a wire transfer to a fraudulent beneficiary through the use of a lookalike email domain and deceptive communication tactics. The referral asserts that the funds were induced out of the customer's account by deception and moved by wire to a beneficiary the customer never intended to pay. The initial information provided by the customer and the relationship manager forms the basis for the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the wire transfer and the subsequent efforts to trace and recover the funds.

## Timeline of Events

The sequence of events leading to the suspected diversion of funds began on May 16, 2024. On this date, Cortex Bank and Trust customer Wilhelmina Braithwaite received an email appearing to originate from a known vendor, Emberline Imports LLC. The message advised of a change in banking details for future invoice payments. The reviewing analyst noted that the sender email address utilized a domain closely resembling the legitimate vendor's domain, differing by a single character. The customer updated the vendor payment instructions in her accounting software based on this communication. No secondary verification of the new banking details, such as a telephone call to a known contact at the vendor, was documented by the customer.

On June 28, 2024, the customer received an invoice via email from the same lookalike domain, purportedly from Emberline Imports LLC, for a mid-five-figure sum. The invoice instructed payment to the previously provided, updated banking details. The beneficiary name on the invoice was listed as Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co., rather than Emberline Imports LLC or its known affiliate, Emberline Equipment LLC. The customer did not remit payment at that time, and the record indicates no communication occurred between the customer and the fraudulent sender or the legitimate vendor regarding this invoice prior to the next contact.

Subsequent communication from the fraudulent sender occurred on July 4, 2024. An email from the lookalike domain urged immediate payment of the June 28 invoice, citing impending supply chain disruptions if the balance remained unsettled. The language used in this communication was characterized by the reviewing analyst as conveying a high degree of urgency. The customer did not respond to this email, and no payment was initiated. A further email on July 11, 2024, reiterated the demand for payment, again employing urgency language and threatening a cessation of services.

On July 22, 2024, the customer received another invoice from the lookalike domain, again purportedly from Emberline Imports LLC, for a low six-figure sum. This invoice, like the previous one, directed payment to Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. and included language emphasizing the necessity of immediate payment to secure pending orders. The customer initiated a wire transfer on July 30, 2024, in the amount of $103,582.40, payable to Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. The reviewing analyst noted that this transfer was initiated minutes prior to the bank's wire cutoff time. The urgency language in the email correspondence appears to have influenced the customer to bypass established internal controls, specifically a dual-approval process typically required for transfers exceeding a certain threshold.

The customer was contacted by the legitimate vendor, Emberline Imports LLC, on August 1, 2024, regarding the outstanding balance on her account. During this communication, the customer learned that the vendor had not requested a change in banking details and had not issued the invoices received from the lookalike domain. The customer contacted Cortex Bank and Trust on August 8, 2024, to report the suspected fraud and request a recall of the wire transfer.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated a recall request to the receiving institution on August 8, 2024. The receiving institution responded on August 23, 2024, confirming that $20,716.48 remained in the beneficiary account and had been frozen. The remainder of the funds had been dissipated. The investigation established that the total amount diverted was $103,582.40, resulting in a residual loss to the customer of $82,865.92. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the transfer and the identity of the beneficiary remains ongoing as of the report date, September 13, 2024.

## Funds Tracing

An outbound wire transfer in the amount of $103,582.40 was initiated from Wilhelmina Braithwaite's Cortex Bank and Trust checking account ending in 61695-1 on August 8, 2024. The transfer instructions directed the funds to a beneficiary account held at a large national financial institution, which the investigation identified as the primary receiving bank. The beneficiary name provided on the wire instructions was Emberline Equipment LLC. This name differed from the vendor name, Emberline Imports LLC, listed on the purportedly compromised invoice, a discrepancy noted during the post-incident review.

A review of the Fedwire details confirmed the successful transmission of the $103,582.40 to the receiving institution. Cortex Bank and Trust's visibility into the onward movement of funds is limited to information provided by the receiving bank in response to a request for indemnification. Following the initiation of the fraud recovery process, the receiving institution reported that a portion of the funds had already been moved or withdrawn prior to the placement of a hold on the beneficiary account.

The receiving institution confirmed that $20,716.48 was successfully frozen in the beneficiary account held in the name of Emberline Equipment LLC. The recovery of these frozen funds is currently being coordinated through standard interbank indemnification procedures. The remaining balance of the original wire transfer is considered the residual loss and the trail of these specific funds is no longer visible to Cortex Bank and Trust.

Information provided by the receiving institution, although not comprising a complete transactional history of the beneficiary account, indicated that the unfrozen funds were rapidly dissipated. The receiving bank communicated that shortly after the receipt of the $103,582.40 wire from Cortex Bank and Trust, several outbound transfers were executed from the Emberline Equipment LLC account. The destination and nature of these subsequent transfers were not disclosed to Cortex Bank and Trust. It is inferred, based on the rapid dissipation of funds typical in such schemes, that the money was moved to other accounts, potentially at different institutions, or converted to untraceable instruments.

Further communication with the receiving institution suggested that some portion of the dissipated funds may have been directed to an entity named Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. The receiving bank did not specify whether Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. held an account at their institution or if the funds were wired externally. The relationship between Emberline Equipment LLC and Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. is unknown, and no legitimate business purpose for transactions between these entities was established during the investigation.

The investigation established that the total sum diverted from Wilhelmina Braithwaite's account was $103,582.40. With $20,716.48 secured by the receiving institution, the residual loss to the customer currently stands at $82,865.92. The trail of this remaining amount ends at the beneficiary account held by Emberline Equipment LLC, as Cortex Bank and Trust has no direct means to trace the funds beyond the initial receiving institution. The onward movement of the $82,865.92 is known only to the extent that it was transferred out of the initial beneficiary account, with a possible connection to Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co., before the receiving bank could secure the remaining balance.

## Beneficiary and Counterparty Analysis

Cortex Bank and Trust conducted a review of the beneficiary account receiving the $103,582.40 outgoing wire transfer from Wilhelmina Braithwaite. The receiving account was held at a domestic financial institution under the name Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. The funds transfer was sent to this beneficiary on August 8, 2024. Review of the payment instructions confirmed that the beneficiary name, Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co., did not match the name of the intended vendor, Emberline Imports LLC, as recorded in the underlying invoice provided by the customer. A request for information was submitted to the receiving institution regarding the beneficiary account and the disposition of the transferred funds.

The receiving institution responded that the Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. account was opened on June 28, 2024. This date is approximately six weeks prior to the receipt of the $103,582.40 wire transfer. The stated business purpose at account opening was the domestic wholesale distribution of agricultural equipment. The receiving institution indicated that the account profile anticipated monthly transaction volumes in the low five-figure range, consisting primarily of domestic ACH credits and checks. The receipt of a six-figure wire transfer on August 8, 2024, represented a significant deviation from the stated expectations and the established historical activity on the account.

A review of the transaction history provided by the receiving institution revealed that prior to August 8, 2024, the account exhibited minimal activity, consistent with a newly established entity or a dormant account. Following the receipt of the $103,582.40 wire transfer, the funds were rapidly dissipated. A series of immediate outgoing transfers were executed, directing portions of the funds to various third-party accounts and facilitating a withdrawal of cash. The receiving institution reported that the pattern of rapid fund depletion following a large, anomalous credit was consistent with the operation of a mule account or an entity established solely to receive and launder illicit proceeds.

Cortex Bank and Trust initiated public records research on Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. The entity was registered as a limited liability company on May 16, 2024, in the same state where the receiving institution is headquartered. The registered address for the business was identified as a mail-drop location, and no physical operating presence could be verified. The registered agent and sole listed member of the LLC could not be linked to any other business entities or public records indicative of established commercial activity. The lack of a verifiable physical presence and the use of a mail-drop address are factors often associated with shell companies or entities created to obscure beneficial ownership.

Further analysis of the communication patterns surrounding the transaction revealed that the email directing Wilhelmina Braithwaite to alter the payment instructions utilized a lookalike sender domain. The fraudulent domain differed from the legitimate vendor’s domain by a single character. The email purported to originate from a representative of Emberline Imports LLC, but directed payment to Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co., citing a recent change in banking relationships. The email also included language stressing the urgency of the payment to secure a critical shipment, which the customer cited as the reason for expediting the transfer and bypassing internal dual-approval controls.

The customer stated that the intended payment was for an invoice issued by Emberline Imports LLC. However, the customer also provided documentation indicating previous dealings with an entity named Emberline Equipment LLC. A review of these prior transactions showed that payments to Emberline Equipment LLC were typically routed to a different domestic financial institution. The discrepancy between the invoiced vendor, the historical vendor, and the beneficiary named in the fraudulent instructions highlights the deceptive nature of the communication that induced the transfer.

The receiving institution confirmed that a hold was placed on the Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co. account upon receipt of the fraud notification from Cortex Bank and Trust. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $20,716.48. The receiving institution indicated that the remaining balance of the transferred funds had already been disbursed prior to the hold being enacted. This resulted in a residual loss to the customer of $82,865.92. The receiving institution stated that they are continuing their internal investigation into the beneficiary account and the disposition of the outgoing transfers.

## Interviews and Documentary Evidence

The reviewing analyst conducted an interview with Wilhelmina Braithwaite on August 23, 2024, to establish the circumstances surrounding the initiation of the outbound wire. The customer stated she received an email on August 8, 2024, purporting to be from a known vendor, Emberline Imports LLC. The email contained an invoice for machinery and a request for immediate payment. The customer indicated the email stressed the need for expedited processing, citing a risk of delayed shipment if funds were not received that day. The customer further stated she had previously transacted with Emberline Imports LLC and recognized the invoice format. The customer provided a copy of the email and the attached invoice to Cortex Bank and Trust for review.

Analysis of the provided email correspondence revealed the sender’s address originated from a domain that was visually similar to the known vendor’s domain, differing by a single character. The invoice attached to the email listed the beneficiary as Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co., a name that did not align with the known vendor, Emberline Imports LLC. A review of historical account activity for the customer showed prior wire transfers directed to Emberline Equipment LLC, a related entity of the known vendor. The customer stated she did not notice the discrepancy in the beneficiary name at the time of the transaction. The customer also stated she was unaware of the domain name variation until the reviewing analyst brought it to her attention.

The customer initiated the wire transfer on August 8, 2024. A review of the wire transfer authorization logs indicated the request was submitted shortly before the daily wire cutoff time. The customer stated the urgency conveyed in the fraudulent email prompted her to expedite the transaction. The customer acknowledged that the typical dual-approval process for wire transfers was bypassed due to the perceived time constraint. The customer stated she believed she was remitting payment to the legitimate vendor, Emberline Imports LLC, for a valid business expense.

The reviewing analyst obtained call recordings from the customer service center for the dates surrounding the transaction. The recordings did not indicate any contact from the customer regarding the wire transfer prior to its initiation. Following the initiation, the customer contacted the bank on August 23, 2024, to inquire about the status of the transfer, stating the vendor, Emberline Imports LLC, had not received the funds. The customer service representative informed the customer the wire had been processed and completed on August 8, 2024. The customer then expressed concern that the funds may have been diverted.

The reviewing analyst contacted the receiving institution on August 23, 2024, to request a recall of the funds. The receiving institution confirmed receipt of the recall request and placed a hold on the remaining funds in the beneficiary account. The amount frozen at the receiving institution was $20,716.48. The receiving institution indicated the remainder of the funds had already been withdrawn or transferred out of the account. The reviewing analyst requested any available information regarding the beneficiary, Falcon Crest Machinery Trading Co., and the subsequent movement of funds. The receiving institution stated they were unable to provide specific details regarding the account holder or the subsequent transactions due to privacy regulations. The customer was notified of the partial recovery and the residual loss. The customer stated she would pursue the matter further with law enforcement. The reviewing analyst obtained a copy of the police report filed by the customer. The report detailed the customer's account of the events and the financial loss incurred. The reviewing analyst continues to monitor the customer's account for any further unusual activity and remains in contact with the receiving institution regarding the frozen funds.

## Recovery and Indemnification Efforts

On August 23, 2024, Cortex Bank and Trust sent a formal request for indemnification to the receiving institution, seeking the return of the $103,582.40 outbound wire transfer. The request cited suspected fraud, noting that Wilhelmina Braithwaite had been deceived into authorizing the transaction and that the beneficiary was not the intended recipient. The communication included a detailed summary of the compromised email correspondence and the misdirected invoice.

The receiving institution acknowledged receipt of the indemnification request on August 26, 2024. In their response, they stated that an investigation into the beneficiary account had been initiated. They requested further documentation to substantiate the claim of fraud, specifically asking for copies of the original email instructions and any correspondence with the legitimate vendor, Emberline Imports LLC.

Cortex Bank and Trust provided the requested documentation on August 28, 2024. This included copies of the emails showing the lookalike sender domain and the urgency language that bypassed the customer's internal controls. The documentation also included correspondence confirming that the legitimate vendor had not received payment and that the invoice provided by the fraudulent sender was not authentic.

On September 5, 2024, the receiving institution informed Cortex Bank and Trust that a portion of the funds had been secured. They reported that $20,716.48 remained in the beneficiary account and had been frozen pending further review. The receiving institution stated that the remainder of the funds had been transferred or withdrawn prior to the receipt of the indemnification request.

The receiving institution did not provide details regarding the disposition of the remaining funds, citing privacy regulations. They indicated that the frozen funds would be held pending a formal request for return from Cortex Bank and Trust, accompanied by a standard hold harmless agreement.

Cortex Bank and Trust executed the required hold harmless agreement and submitted it to the receiving institution on August 6, 2023. The agreement stipulated that Cortex Bank and Trust would indemnify the receiving institution against any claims arising from the return of the funds. The return of the $20,716.48 is currently pending processing by the receiving institution.

The difference between the initial fraudulent wire transfer amount and the amount successfully frozen at the receiving institution resulted in a residual loss of $82,865.92. This amount represents the funds that were successfully diverted by the unknown actors and are currently unrecoverable through standard interbank processes.

The relationship manager assigned to Wilhelmina Braithwaite contacted the customer to advise her of the status of the recovery efforts. The customer was informed of the amount that had been secured and the amount that remained unrecovered. The customer was also advised to contact law enforcement and to review her internal security protocols.

A review of the customer's account agreement and the circumstances surrounding the authorization of the wire transfer was conducted to determine liability for the residual loss. The review noted that the customer had authenticated the transaction using established procedures, despite the presence of red flags such as the beneficiary name discrepancy and the urgency language.

Cortex Bank and Trust has initiated a review of its internal policies regarding customer liability in cases of authorized push payment fraud. The decision regarding potential reimbursement or indemnification for the residual loss of $82,865.92 remains pending the outcome of this review and any subsequent legal or regulatory developments. The customer has been advised that the bank is continuing to evaluate the situation.

The bank's insurance carrier has been notified of the incident and the resulting loss. A preliminary claim has been filed, and the carrier has requested additional information regarding the circumstances of the fraud and the bank's internal controls. The outcome of the insurance claim is currently pending. The bank continues to monitor the situation and will update the customer as new information becomes available.

## Findings and Disposition

The investigation established that Wilhelmina Braithwaite was the victim of a business email compromise scheme resulting in the diversion of funds. On August 28, 2024, the customer received an email containing a fraudulent invoice, purportedly from an established vendor. The email originated from a lookalike domain differing from the vendor's true domain by a single character. The invoice directed payment to a beneficiary account held by Emberline Imports LLC, an entity with no prior relationship to the customer. The email contained urgency language that successfully circumvented the customer's internal dual-approval controls. The resulting wire transfer, initiated shortly before the daily processing cutoff, directed $103,582.40 to the fraudulent beneficiary. Upon discovery of the fraud, Cortex Bank and Trust contacted the receiving institution. A portion of the funds was successfully frozen, mitigating the total impact, but the customer sustained a residual loss of $82,865.92. The investigation remains ongoing pending further communication with the receiving institution regarding the potential recovery of the frozen funds.
